[RESOLVED 2026-07-31 -- re-examined via the standing 17-step workflow;
  decided against changing counting semantics]
  COUNT_SETTLED_PREDICTIONS() COUNTS RAW ROWS, NOT DISTINCT
  TEMPERATURE-OBSERVATION EVENTS
Priority: was Low -- a real design question, not a live-money-critical gap
  (doesn't change today's live gate outcomes; ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE/F3 clear
  either way at current counts), but the codebase already has an explicit,
  opus-reviewed precedent for the opposite choice on a sibling function.

Problem:
  tracker.count_settled_predictions() (tracker.py:1866) joins
  multiday_predictions to outcomes_valid on ticker and counts every
  matching ROW, not distinct settlement events. A city/date pair with
  multiple ladder-bracket tickers that all settle from the same real
  observation (e.g. multiple above/below/between brackets on the same
  city+date) each contribute their own +1, so the live-trading maturity
  gate's count can overstate how many independent real-world observations
  actually back it. This is the exact same shape count_settled_snow_
  predictions() (tracker.py:1926) was deliberately hardened against
  (opus-review-caught 2026-07-30, same day): "Denver's own KXDENSNOWM
  ladder alone has 7 sibling brackets that all settle from the SAME real
  snowfall observation for a given month, so a raw-row floor could clear
  the 20-sample threshold with as few as ~3 real months of data, not 20
  independent real-world observations." That function now counts DISTINCT
  (ticker prefix, year, month) accrual events instead of raw rows.
  count_settled_predictions() was NOT given the same treatment -- it
  still counts raw rows, same as count_settled_rain_predictions()
  (tracker.py:1898), whose own docstring explicitly accepts this as a
  known, deliberate tradeoff: "rain has 11 cities' worth of decorrelation
  across those rows, and changing its counting semantics now would shift
  an already-accumulating live gate's count out from under it."
  count_settled_predictions() is in the same position as rain's counter
  (already live/shipped, changing its semantics now would shift an
  already-accumulating gate), which is likely why it was left alone --
  but that reasoning was never stated for this function, only inferred.

What it would look like:
  Either (a) leave as-is and explicitly document the same "already live,
  changing semantics would shift an accumulating gate" reasoning rain's
  counter states, so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for an
  oversight, or (b) redesign to count distinct temperature-observation
  events (city + date, or ticker-prefix + date depending on how directly
  correlated same-day above/below/between brackets on one city really
  are) the way snow's counter now does -- a bigger, live-gate-semantics-
  changing decision that needs the user's input on whether the maturity
  gate should measure "settled rows" or "independent observations."

Why not now:
  Found via adjacency while fixing the condition_type filter gap (a
  different, narrower bug) -- this is a separate, larger design decision
  about what the gate should actually measure, not a bug with an obvious
  single fix. Changing the counting semantics now would also change
  ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE/F3's live count again (a second change to the same
  gate in the same day), which deserves its own explicit user decision
  and its own dedicated verification pass, not a drive-by bundled into
  the condition_type fix.

What was decided:
  Re-verified live data (2026-07-31, data/predictions.db): 61 raw rows vs.
  60 distinct (city, market_date) pairs -- only ONE apparent duplicate
  (Dallas, 2026-05-19). Investigating that single case changed the
  conclusion entirely: it is NOT a duplicate ladder bracket at all -- it's
  `KXHIGHTDAL-26MAY19-T83` and `KXLOWTDAL-26MAY19-T69`, the day's HIGH and
  LOW temperature markets, which are two genuinely independent real
  observations that happen to share a city+date. A naive `(city,
  market_date)` distinct-event key -- the direct analog of what count_
  settled_snow_predictions() does with (ticker prefix, year, month) --
  would have silently merged those two into one event, which is a new
  correctness bug, not a fix: the `var` column that should distinguish
  high/low is mostly NULL on live data (53/61 rows), so the only reliable
  signal is the KXHIGH/KXLOW ticker prefix, which would need its own parser
  (mirroring snow's `_parse_monthly_ticker_month`) to do this safely.
  Correctly grouping by (city, market_date, high-or-low-from-ticker-prefix)
  gives 61 distinct events against 61 raw rows -- there are ZERO actual
  duplicate-ladder-bracket rows in live data today. The snow precedent
  doesn't carry over as cleanly as it first looked: snow's 7 KXDENSNOWM
  sibling brackets are near-redundant restatements of one monthly accrual
  number, while temperature's above/below brackets on a given city+date+
  high-or-low are today, in practice, one row each -- no observed
  duplication to fix.
  Also surfaced during review: count_settled_predictions()'s own docstring
  already commits it to counting "the same population F3's own calibration
  math (calibration.py) ... already train on" -- calibration.py's grid
  search and get_multiday_calibration_cli both train on raw rows with no
  dedup. Switching this counter to distinct-event counting would break that
  stated alignment, trading one mismatch (vs. snow's precedent) for another
  (vs. this function's own calibration-population contract).
  Decision (via AskUserQuestion, user confirmed after the KXHIGH/KXLOW
  finding changed the calculus): leave as raw-row counting. Documented the
  full reasoning above in count_settled_predictions()'s docstring
  (tracker.py:1866) so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for an
  oversight, matching rain's counter's existing precedent of stating its
  tradeoff explicitly. Added a regression test (tests/test_tracker.py,
  `test_count_settled_predictions_counts_raw_rows_not_distinct_events`,
  mutation-tested against a distinct-event implementation to confirm it
  actually catches that regression) locking in the decision so a future
  change can't silently flip this semantics without the test failing.

When to revisit:
  If live data ever shows the same city+date+high-or-low combination
  settling more than once (i.e. real ladder-bracket duplication, not a
  high/low pair) -- that would be the actual trigger condition this entry
  was watching for, and did not find as of 2026-07-31.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-27 -- found live during a cron output review, root-caused,
  fixed same session]
  SAFE_IO -- EMERGENCY-COPY FALLBACK SILENTLY CLOBBERED THE ORIGINAL FILE
Priority: was High once found -- a crash-safety utility used by 20+ callers
  across the codebase (including paper.py's live trade-state file) had its
  entire safety guarantee silently defeated by default, for every real
  caller, in exactly the failure scenario (contested/locked file) where it
  matters most.

Problem:
  A live cron run on 2026-07-27 hit a Windows file-lock collision writing
  `data/forecast_sigma.json` (`climatology.py`'s `load_all_sigmas()`) --
  `safe_io.atomic_write_json()`'s 3 retry attempts all failed with
  WinError 32/2/5, then it fell through to its "emergency copy for manual
  recovery" path and logged success. Investigated because the run also
  showed persistent rain-market anomalies (see the RAIN MARKETS entry
  above) and this ERROR-level log line stood out as worth checking, not
  assumed safe just because cron exited 0.
  Traced `safe_io.py`'s fallback logic (added by commit `335ded8`, "Batch S:
  R28 + P2-H", intended to make the emergency copy "operator-visible" by
  landing it in the monitored `data/` dir instead of system temp): when a
  caller omits `fallback_dir`, the first candidate is `project_root() /
  "data"` -- but every real target file already lives in that exact
  directory (`DATA_DIR`, defined identically in `climatology.py`,
  `acis_precip.py`, `backtest.py`, etc.), so `emergency_path = fb_dir /
  path.name` resolves to the SAME path as the file that just failed 3
  atomic-write attempts. The "emergency copy" was actually a plain
  non-atomic `open(path, "w")` overwrite of the live file -- silently
  defeating `atomic_write_json`'s entire crash-safety purpose (temp-write +
  fsync + rename) in precisely the scenario it exists to protect against.
  Grepped every call site (20+: `paper.py`'s live trade-state `DATA_PATH`,
  `circuit_breaker.py`'s kill-switch state, `weather_markets.py`'s forecast
  caches, `climatology.py`, `acis_precip.py`, `alerts.py`, `ab_test.py`,
  `param_sweep.py`, `kalshi_ws.py`, `monte_carlo.py`,
  `settlement_monitor.py`, `main.py`) -- NONE pass `fallback_dir`, so this
  was a universal, not file-specific, gap. Tonight's actual outcome was
  benign (the lock was transient; the plain overwrite happened to succeed
  with correct data, verified by re-reading `forecast_sigma.json` after the
  run) -- but a crash or another process interrupting that non-atomic write
  could have left any of these files (including live trade state)
  truncated/corrupted with only a buried ERROR log to show for it. The only
  existing test for this path
  (`test_atomic_write_emergency_copy_written_on_failure`) explicitly passes
  a distinct `fallback_dir`, so the real-world default-omitted-fallback_dir
  behavior had never been exercised.

What was fixed:
  Default emergency candidate changed from `project_root()/"data"` to a
  dedicated `project_root()/"data"/".emergency"` subdir -- preserves P2-H's
  original "operator-visible, monitored location" intent while guaranteeing
  no collision with any real target file (none live in `.emergency/`), with
  zero caller changes needed across all 20+ call sites.
  `cleanup_data_dir()` (main.py) only globs `data/*.json` non-recursively
  and already skips dot-prefixed entries at the top level, so
  `data/.emergency/` is invisible to its 2-day-retention sweep -- recovery
  copies won't get silently deleted (independently re-verified by the
  opus review below, not just asserted).
  Added a belt-and-suspenders guard in the fallback loop itself: any
  candidate (default or explicitly-passed `fallback_dir`) that resolves to
  the same path as the original target is skipped with a warning rather
  than written to, so an explicit-but-colliding `fallback_dir` can never
  reintroduce the same class of bug.
  Considered and rejected two alternatives (via `AskUserQuestion`): renaming
  the file in place (`forecast_sigma.json.emergency`) fixes the same bug but
  buys nothing extra over the subdir approach and forces an unrelated
  test-assertion change; reverting to temp-only fallback regresses P2-H's
  operator-visible intent and, without the belt-and-suspenders guard,
  doesn't close the underlying class of bug (an explicit colliding
  `fallback_dir` would still trigger it).

  Independent review (opus, effort=high) before push found the core fix
  correct but surfaced real gaps in the first pass, all addressed:
  - HIGH: the two new tests didn't isolate `project_root()` to a tmp dir in
    every case, so a real test run wrote actual recovery-copy junk into
    THIS repo's own `data/.emergency/` (reviewer reproduced it: a genuine
    `paper_trades.json` emergency copy could be silently overwritten by a
    routine `pytest` run). Fixed by patching `project_root` in every
    affected test (`test_safe_io.py` and, once the fix made it possible to
    even notice, a pre-existing, previously-unrelated test in
    `test_infrastructure.py` -- `test_atomic_write_raises_on_double_failure`
    -- that had the identical gap, exposed only because this fix introduced
    a new subdirectory for it to silently create in the real repo).
  - MEDIUM: the `AtomicWriteError` message claimed "Emergency copy written
    to None" when no copy could be written at all (disk-full-everywhere
    case) -- fixed with an explicit truthful branch plus a dedicated ERROR
    log line, and a new test forcing total failure (`os.replace` mocked to
    fail unconditionally) to pin the accurate message.
  - MEDIUM: the emergency copy itself was a plain non-atomic `open(path,
    "w")` with no fsync -- weaker durability than the primary write it
    exists to back up, and two processes failing on the same target
    simultaneously could interleave-corrupt it. Fixed by giving the
    emergency copy the identical temp+fsync+`os.replace` discipline as the
    primary write, with its own pid-suffixed temp name.
  - MEDIUM: root-caused the likely actual trigger of tonight's incident --
    the primary write's temp filename (`.{name}_{attempt}.tmp`) has no
    per-process component, so two processes racing to write the same target
    (exactly what Windows lock contention implies) could share one temp
    file and interleave-corrupt it before an atomic rename installs the
    corruption "successfully." Fixed by adding `os.getpid()` to the temp
    name; verified `paper.py`'s own stray-temp-file cleanup glob
    (`.paper_trades.json_*.tmp`) still matches with a pid inserted.
  - Self-caught during the fix for the above: giving the emergency copy its
    own temp+replace step introduced a new leak -- on emergency-write
    failure the temp file was never cleaned up (reproduced live: a stray
    `.paper_trades.json_<pid>.emergency.tmp` was left in this repo's own
    `data/.emergency/` after a single test run). Fixed with the same
    `os.unlink` cleanup-on-except the primary write already had; added a
    dedicated regression assertion (glob-checks both the tmp-isolated dir
    and real system temp for leftover `*.tmp` files) and mutation-tested it
    by temporarily removing the cleanup and confirming the new assertion
    catches it.
  - LOW: `circuit_breaker._save_state`'s failure log bumped from WARNING to
    ERROR -- under the old bug a same-path clobber meant CB/kill-switch
    state usually landed on disk anyway despite the "failure"; after this
    fix a failed save now genuinely loses that cycle's state.
  - LOW: fixed the second new test's docstring (wrongly claimed the
    colliding candidate falls through to "system temp" -- it actually falls
    through to the next candidate in order, the default `.emergency` subdir)
    and added the assertion it was missing for where the copy actually landed.
  - LOW: documented the fallback_dir/`.emergency` default location in
    `atomic_write_json`'s own docstring (previously only in an inline
    comment).
  - LOW (accepted, not fixed): emergency copies are keyed by `path.name`
    (basename) only, so a same-named target in two different directories
    would share one recovery slot. Verified live against every real
    `atomic_write_json` call site 2026-07-27 -- no actual collision exists
    today (confirmed `ab_test.py`'s dynamic per-test-name files live under
    a distinct `data/ab_tests/` subdir with no top-level basename overlap).
    Left as a documented, reasoned limitation (comment added at the call
    site) rather than adding relative-path-encoding complexity for a
    theoretical case -- the emergency copy is a best-effort recovery aid,
    not the source of truth.
  - INFO items (redundant dead assignment, docstring-adjacent nits,
    `.resolve()` hoisting): folded into the same diff since each was a
    one-line change already touching that exact code.
  - Deferred, NOT fixed now (genuinely separate scope -- a new monitoring/
    alerting mechanism, not a fix to this change): nothing currently reads,
    alerts on, or surfaces a non-empty `data/.emergency/` beyond one ERROR
    log line in a rotating file. See the new OPEN entry below.
  - Deferred, NOT fixed now (historical point-in-time snapshots, never
    revised since their one authoring commit `b897d39` -- correcting them
    would break that convention, not follow it): `docs/grade_audit/
    outputs/safe_io.py.md` and `docs/audit_findings.md` both describe/score
    the old, buggy cascade. Left as-is; this backlog entry is the live
    record now.

  3 new regression tests + 2 pre-existing tests fixed for test-isolation
  (`tests/test_safe_io.py`: 20 tests total in the file, up from 17 before
  this session; `tests/test_infrastructure.py`: 1 test fixed, 33 total
  unchanged in count). Every new/changed assertion mutation-tested --
  reverted the relevant code (via manual diff-swap after `git checkout`
  was found to blow away the whole file rather than one hunk, corrected by
  keeping a working backup and using targeted `git show HEAD:<file>` swaps
  instead) and confirmed each test fails with the exact predicted
  AssertionError against pre-fix code, then restored and re-confirmed
  green. Full scoped regression (`tests/test_safe_io.py` +
  `tests/test_infrastructure.py`, 53 tests) passes; ruff + ruff format +
  mypy clean on every touched file (`safe_io.py`, `circuit_breaker.py`,
  `tests/test_safe_io.py`, `tests/test_infrastructure.py`). Verified twice,
  after the fix and after restoring from the `git checkout` mishap, that no
  test run leaves stray files behind in either this repo's real
  `data/.emergency/` or the real system temp directory.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-31 -- shipped via the standing 17-step workflow]
  SAFE_IO -- NOTHING MONITORS data/.emergency/ FOR REAL RECOVERY COPIES
Priority: was Low -- a genuine emergency copy landing there today is only
  visible via one buried ERROR log line; the fix above stopped the
  clobbering, but a human still won't notice a real one exists without
  reading logs.

Problem:
  Once `atomic_write_json()`'s emergency-copy fallback actually works (see
  the resolved entry above), a real recovery copy can sit in
  `data/.emergency/` indefinitely with nothing surfacing it -- no startup
  check, no cron-summary warning, no alert. An operator would only find out
  by grepping logs.

What was fixed:
  Re-verified first: `data/.emergency/` doesn't exist in this repo today
  (the underlying clobber bug is fixed and has never fired for real since),
  so this ships with zero live behavior surfaced yet -- it's instrumentation
  for the day it does fire, not a response to an active incident.
  Added `safe_io.check_emergency_copies(base_dir=None)`, which lists every
  file under `project_root()/"data"/".emergency"` (filename, full path, ISO
  8601 mtime, size in bytes; oldest first), returning an empty list when
  nothing is found (the healthy default, not an error). Wired into
  `cron.py`'s per-cycle checks (same place as the calibration readiness
  reminder and the dead-man's-switch check, guarded by the same
  `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` check so a routine test run can't trip a false
  alarm -- the test-isolation fix the entry asked for was already done as
  part of the resolved entry above, verified no stray files land in the
  real `data/.emergency/` during test runs). A non-empty result now: logs
  an ERROR with filename/mtime/size/path for every file, prints an inline
  `[EmergencyCopy]` warning during interactive runs, AND fires
  `notify.send_system_alert()` -- the same multi-channel (desktop/pushover/
  ntfy/discord/email) mechanism already used for the dead-man's-switch
  48h-cron-gap alert. Upgraded from an initial log-line-plus-console-print
  design after noticing `send_system_alert()` already existed and was the
  correct fit -- a log line alone doesn't solve "an operator would only
  find out by grepping logs" (the exact problem this entry describes)
  during a silent unattended cron run; only a real push notification does.
  Independent `Agent(opus, effort=high)` review found 6 real issues, all
  fixed: (1) MEDIUM, the monitor only checked `data/.emergency/`, blind to
  the system-temp last-resort location `atomic_write_json()` also falls
  back to -- exactly the scenario ("disk full, permissions error, or path
  unavailable") where `data/.emergency/` itself might also be unwritable;
  fixed by also checking system temp for basenames that already exist in
  `project_root()/"data"` (bounded to known names, not a wholesale temp
  scan, so unrelated files from other processes aren't reported as false
  positives). (2) MEDIUM, `mtime`/`path`/`size_bytes` were computed but
  never surfaced in the log, while the console text claimed "see log for
  names/mtimes" -- fixed, the ERROR log now includes all four fields per
  file. (3) MEDIUM-LOW, `send_system_alert()`'s 6h cooldown used one shared
  `"__system__"` key for every caller, so this new alert and the existing
  dead-man's-switch alert would silently suppress each other for 6h; fixed
  by adding an optional `cooldown_key` parameter (default `"__system__"`,
  so the 2 pre-existing callers are unaffected) and passing a distinct key
  here. Also documented (not fixed -- a bigger, separate change affecting
  all 3 callers) that the cooldown is in-process memory only and does NOT
  survive a fresh-process cron invocation under Windows Task Scheduler,
  only within `main.py`'s long-lived `loop`/`watch --auto` modes; filed as
  its own new backlog entry below rather than bundled in here. (4) LOW, a
  file with a corrupt/out-of-range mtime made `datetime.fromtimestamp()`
  raise `OSError` OUTSIDE the function's own `try/except` (verified live: a
  large-negative mtime raises `OSError [Errno 22]` on this platform), which
  would silently blank out the ENTIRE result (caught by cron's outer
  `except Exception`, logged at DEBUG) at exactly the moment a real file
  needs recovery; fixed by moving `fromtimestamp` inside the per-entry
  `try` and widening it to `(OSError, ValueError, OverflowError)`, so one
  corrupt entry is skipped without losing every other real file in the same
  scan. (5) LOW, reordered the cron block so `send_system_alert()` fires
  before the console `print()` -- if the print ever raised, the loudest
  channel would otherwise be the one skipped. (6) LOW, this resolution note
  itself originally miscounted the new tests as 11 (actually 6 at review
  time) and misnamed the pre-existing suite it was added alongside as
  `count_settled_predictions()` tests (that suite doesn't exist in this
  file at all -- the actual pre-existing tests are the `atomic_write_json`
  emergency-copy ones); corrected here.
  10 tests total in `tests/test_safe_io.py` for `check_emergency_copies()`
  (missing dir, empty dir, real files with correct fields, multi-file
  oldest-first ordering via a real `os.utime`-forced mtime gap,
  subdirectories ignored, default `project_root()`-based path, system-temp
  fallback found, system-temp scan ignores unrelated files, explicit
  `base_dir` skips the temp scan, corrupt-mtime file skipped without
  losing other real files), all mutation-tested (reverted each assertion

  predicted symptom -- including reproducing the opus-review-caught
  uncaught-`OSError` bug live before fixing it -- then restored).
  ruff/ruff-format/mypy clean on all 4 touched files (`safe_io.py`,
  `cron.py`, `notify.py`, `tests/test_safe_io.py`). No dedicated cron.py-
  level test added for the wiring itself -- matches this file's own
  existing precedent (the calibration reminder and dead-man's-switch blocks

[RESOLVED 2026-07-31 -- send_system_alert()'s cooldown only, per explicit
  user scope decision; alert_strong_signal()'s per-ticker cooldown
  deliberately left in-process, see resolution note below]
  NOTIFY.SEND_SYSTEM_ALERT()'S COOLDOWN IS IN-PROCESS MEMORY ONLY, DOESN'T
  SURVIVE A FRESH CRON PROCESS
Priority: Low -- affects operational alert spam, not trading correctness;
  none of `send_system_alert()`'s 3 current callers (prod reminder,
  dead-man's-switch, the emergency-copy monitor above) have actually spammed
  a real operator yet.

Problem:
  `notify._last_notified` (the dict `send_system_alert()`'s 6h cooldown
  reads/writes) is a plain in-process module-level dict, never persisted to
  disk. CORRECTED 2026-07-31 (user caught this before any implementation
  started): the original framing below cited Windows Task Scheduler
  specifically -- live-verified via `schtasks /Query` that zero Kalshi-
  related scheduled tasks are actually registered on this machine; cron is
  manual-only until the VM migration (`cmd_schedule_cycles()`, `main.py`,
  only ever *prints* the schtasks commands for the user to register by
  hand, it doesn't register them itself, and nobody has run those commands
  here). The real root cause is invocation-mode-agnostic, not specific to
  Task Scheduler: every `py main.py cron` invocation -- manual or scheduled
  -- is a fresh Python process, so the cooldown dict starts empty every
  single time and never actually suppresses a repeat alert across separate
  invocations, only within one long-lived process (`main.py`'s `loop` /
  `watch --auto` modes). This makes it, if anything, MORE immediately
  relevant during the current manual-only operating mode than the original
  "Task Scheduler" framing implied -- re-running `py main.py cron` by hand
  within 6h of a real alert firing hits this exact gap, which is a normal
  thing to do manually, not a future-only scenario. `AUDIT_PLAN.md`'s P1-7
  already fixed this exact class of bug for `circuit_breaker.py`'s state,
  but `notify.py`'s cooldown was never covered by that fix. This matters
  more for a condition that persists until fixed (an unrecovered emergency
  copy sits in `data/.emergency/` until a human deletes it -- every cron
  invocation in between, manual or scheduled, would alert again) than for
  one that self-clears (the dead-man's-switch's own trigger condition
  resets the moment cron next completes successfully).

What it would look like:
  Persist `_last_notified` to disk (e.g. via `safe_io.atomic_write_json`,
  matching the pattern P1-7 already established for circuit breaker state)
  so the cooldown survives across separate process invocations -- manual or
  scheduled -- not just within one long-lived process.

When to revisit:
  Whenever a real emergency copy or another `send_system_alert()`-gated
  condition actually fires and the operator (manually or via a future
  scheduled task) re-runs cron within the 6h window, spamming a repeat
  alert in practice -- not urgent today since none of the 3 current
  callers have fired for real yet, but no longer gated on the VM
  migration/Task-Scheduler transition as the original framing implied.

RESOLVED 2026-07-31: scoped via explicit AskUserQuestion decision before
  writing any code -- persistence covers send_system_alert()'s cooldown
  only, not alert_strong_signal()'s per-ticker trade-signal cooldown
  (which stays in-process, deliberately). Research before deciding found a
  second, independent reason beyond "matches the original ask": alert_
  strong_signal()'s real duplicate-alert guard is `previous_tickers`
  (main.py's watch loop state, itself in-process-only) -- persisting just
  `_last_notified` for trade signals wouldn't even achieve full restart-
  safety on its own, since `previous_tickers` would still reset on a fresh
  process and treat every currently-strong ticker as "new" regardless.
  Shipped: `paths.NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_STATE_PATH` (`data/.notify_cooldowns.json`)
  + `notify._system_cooldown_elapsed()`, mirroring `circuit_breaker.py`'s
  established `_save_state()` shape exactly -- read, decide, and write all
  happen under one lock acquisition (`_NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_FILE_LOCK`), not two
  separate ones, to avoid a TOCTOU race between concurrent callers. Fails
  OPEN (fires the alert) on a missing or corrupt cooldown file -- a
  bookkeeping failure must never silently suppress a real system alert,
  matching `paper.is_accuracy_halted()`'s precedent for this failure class.
  `send_system_alert()` now calls this instead of reading/writing the
  shared `_last_notified` dict; `alert_strong_signal()`'s own use of
  `_last_notified` is completely untouched. Also fixed the stale "Windows
  Task Scheduler" framing this entry's own Problem section had (see the
  CORRECTED note above) everywhere else it appeared: `send_system_alert()`'s
  docstring and the emergency-copy-monitor comment block in cron.py (both
  previously said the gap only mattered "under Task Scheduler" -- corrected
  to invocation-mode-agnostic language matching the real root cause).
  New tests (tests/test_notify.py, no prior test coverage existed for this
  function at all): 8 direct tests of `_system_cooldown_elapsed()` (first-
  call fires+persists, second-call-suppressed, the actual cross-invocation
  regression this entry is about, cooldown-elapses-after-window, distinct
  keys don't interfere, missing-file/corrupt-file both fail open, missing
  parent dir auto-created) plus 2 integration-level tests calling
  `send_system_alert()` itself end to end with external channels
  monkeypatched to a fake recorder. All isolated to a tmp_path file via
  monkeypatch -- never touches the real data/.notify_cooldowns.json.
  Mutation-tested twice: (1) reverted to the old in-process-only behavior
  (state always empty) -- 4 tests correctly failed, including the one named
  for this exact regression; (2) flipped the fail-open exception handler to
  fail-closed -- the corrupt-file test correctly failed. Both reverted and
  re-verified green. ruff/ruff-format/mypy clean on notify.py, paths.py,
  cron.py, tests/test_notify.py.

  Independent Agent(opus, effort=high) review before push, given this
  touches the alerting/operational-safety path: found no vacuous claims on
  first pass, but 2 HIGH and 4 MEDIUM real findings, all addressed --
  (1) HIGH -- `cron.py`'s prod-reminder (`:436`) and dead-man's-switch
  (`:582`) callers both omitted `cooldown_key`, defaulting to the shared
  `"__system__"` key. Harmless before this fix (a fresh in-process dict
  each cron run meant the two alert types could only ever collide within
  the SAME process run), but persistence turned this into a real cross-
  process hazard: cron run N's prod reminder would silently suppress run
  N+1's dead-man's-switch alert for 6h, and vice versa -- exactly the
  scenario `send_system_alert()`'s own docstring already warns callers to
  avoid, just never actually fixed at these two call sites. Fixed: gave
  both their own distinct keys (`"prod_reminder"`, `"cron_gap"`).
  (2) HIGH -- the docstring/comments claimed the single lock acquisition
  avoids "a TOCTOU race between concurrent callers (e.g. two processes)" --
  false. `threading.Lock` is process-local; two separate `py main.py cron`
  processes each hold their own independent lock object, so this provides
  NO cross-process serialization, only thread-level protection within one
  process (matching what `circuit_breaker.py`'s own analogous lock actually
  claims -- re-read its comment directly, it only ever claims in-process
  thread safety + Windows os.replace collision avoidance, never cross-
  process). True cross-process locking (e.g. an O_EXCL lockfile) was
  judged out of scope for this pass -- the actual operating model is
  sequential manual invocation today, not concurrent processes -- so the
  fix was correcting the overclaiming wording, not building new lock
  infrastructure. (3) MEDIUM -- valid JSON that isn't a dict (e.g. a bare
  `null`) parsed without error, then crashed on `state.get(...)` with an
  AttributeError, silently swallowed by every caller's own broad
  try/except but breaking `send_system_alert()`'s documented "Never
  raises" contract. Fixed with an explicit `isinstance(state, dict)`
  check inside the same try block. (4) MEDIUM -- on ANY read failure
  (corrupt file, non-dict JSON, or a transient I/O error --
  `circuit_breaker.py`'s own `_load_state()` comment documents a real
  observed Windows PermissionError mid-os.replace for this exact read
  shape), the code fell back to `state = {}` and then wrote back only the
  current key -- silently erasing every OTHER already-persisted cooldown
  key in the file. Fixed: a read failure now fails open WITHOUT writing
  at all, since a call that can't safely see existing state must not
  blindly overwrite it. (5) MEDIUM -- a sustained write failure (state
  read fine, write keeps failing) silently degrades back to the exact
  pre-fix in-process-only behavior forever, with only a warning log line
  -- judged disproportionate to build dedicated escalation for in this
  pass (would need its own design), but documented explicitly rather than
  left silent: `atomic_write_json`'s own emergency-copy fallback plus the
  existing `.emergency/` monitor (`cooldown_key="emergency_copy"`, a
  distinct key from anything this failure mode would affect) already
  independently surfaces a sustained write failure of this kind via a
  separate, working alert channel -- not a fully silent failure mode in
  practice, a residual risk explicitly accepted rather than silently
  dropped. (6) MEDIUM -- the code comment (and this note, before this
  correction) claimed `alert_strong_signal()`'s real duplicate-alert guard
  `previous_tickers` is "in-process-only" -- false, live-verified against
  `main.py`: `_load_watch_state()`/`_save_watch_state()` persist it to
  `data/.watch_state.json` and the function's own docstring says "survives
  restarts." The scope decision itself (send_system_alert() only, this
  pass) still stands -- it was the primary, explicit AskUserQuestion-
  confirmed reason, not this secondary point -- but the comment's
  reasoning was corrected rather than left factually wrong.
  Also fixed 2 LOW findings: a citation of `paper.is_accuracy_halted()` as
  a "fail-open precedent" was backwards -- that function actually fails
  CLOSED (changed 2026-07-09 specifically because fail-open silently
  disabled the halt); the fail-open choice here is correct on its own
  merits for an alerting path, just not modeled on that function, so the
  citation was removed rather than left misleading. And a redundant
  `NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_STATE_PATH.parent.mkdir(...)` call was removed --
  `atomic_write_json()` already does this as its own first step
  (safe_io.py), so the extra call (and the test that only proved atomic_
  write_json's mkdir works, not notify.py's own) was dead weight.
  New tests added addressing the findings: a non-dict-JSON test (finding
  3), a read-failure-doesn't-clobber-other-keys test (finding 4), and a
  real 20-thread concurrency test proving the lock's actual job (finding
  1's neighbor -- nothing in the original suite would have caught the
  lock being deleted). All 3 mutation-tested the same way: reverted the
  specific fix, confirmed the specific new test failed for the right
  reason (the concurrency mutation manifested as write collisions/
  emergency-copy fallbacks rather than a clean logical race, but still
  reliably failed), restored, re-verified green. 13 tests total in
  tests/test_notify.py. Also updated `safe_io.py`'s basename-collision
  note (2026-07-27) to record re-verification against the new
  `.notify_cooldowns.json` call site (still no real collision). Full
  regression sweep re-run clean; ruff/ruff-format/mypy clean on all 5
  changed files (notify.py, paths.py, cron.py, safe_io.py,
  tests/test_notify.py).

[PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-07-28 -- near-term (<=16-day) ensemble forecast

  RAIN MARKETS -- MONTHLY MODEL HAS NO DAY-SPECIFIC FORECAST SIGNAL
Priority: Medium -- shadow-only today (RAIN_TRADING_ENABLED gate +
  TRADING_PAUSED both mean nothing sizes off this yet), but should be
  looked at before the rain model is ever trusted for real sizing.

Problem:
  Cron's `check_market_anomalies()` flagged the same 2-3 rain tickers as
  "price drifted against model" on 3 consecutive runs on 2026-07-27:
  KXRAINSTPM-26JUL-8 (our 39-43% vs market 68-70%), KXRAINNYCM-26JUL-6
  (our 7-10% vs market 30-44%), KXRAINNYCM-26JUL-7 (our 1-7% vs market
  14-21%), plus one-off KXRAINCHIM-26JUL-4. Investigated live rather than
  assuming a bug: reproduced `_analyze_monthly_rain_trade()`'s bootstrap by
  hand against real ACIS data (month-to-date actual + 30yr remaining-days
  history for NYC/StPetersburg/Chicago) and got raw pre-bias probabilities
  matching cron's "our" values almost exactly (NYC >6in: 6.7% vs cron's 7%;
  NYC >7in: 0.0% [never happened in 30 years] vs cron's 1%; StPetersburg
  >8in: 42.9% vs cron's 39%; Chicago >4in: 7.1% vs cron's 7%) -- the model
  is not malfunctioning, it's doing exactly what Step 2 (`1839d76`) built
  it to do.
  Root cause: the model's only "what's actually going to happen the rest of
  this month" signal beyond the 30yr climatological bootstrap is Open-Meteo
  Seasonal's ECMWF SEAS5 tilt, and that's a *monthly mean* only (already
  flagged as a limitation in this file's own RAIN/SNOW/HURRICANE MARKETS
  entry, Step 2 handoff item 1: "mean-only, no per-member spread ... can
  adjust central tendency but can't itself supply distribution shape") --
  it has no day-level resolution, so it structurally cannot see "a system
  is forecast to bring heavy rain on day 29" the way a trader checking an
  actual short-range forecast (or the market itself) can.
  Pulled Open-Meteo's real 7-day `precipitation_sum` forecast live for the
  divergent cities to check which side of each divergence looks right:
    - NYC: forecast for the remaining accrual days (Jul 27-31) sums to only
      ~0.87in -- nowhere near the 2.31in/3.31in still needed for rungs 6/7.
      The real short-range forecast supports the model's LOW probability,
      not the market's 30%/14% pricing -- on these two rungs the market
      looks like the mispriced side (or reflects something about these
      illiquid deep-OTM brackets this bot doesn't have visibility into),
      not the model.
    - St. Petersburg: forecast shows a building wet pattern right at
      month's end (0/0/0.9/2.7/6.5mm Jul 27-31, continuing into 13.2mm Aug
      1 -- just past this ticker's settlement), consistent with the
      market's higher 68-70% price. This looks like real information the
      climatology-only model can't see, not market noise.

What the fix looks like (not yet designed in detail):
  Blend a real short-range forecast signal for the remaining days of the
  current accrual month into `_analyze_monthly_rain_trade()`, on top of
  (not replacing) the 30yr empirical bootstrap -- Open-Meteo's regular
  forecast API (already used elsewhere in this bot, ~16-day horizon) covers
  "the rest of the month" for any ticker whose remaining days fit inside
  that window, which is most of a typical month once a chunk of it has
  already accrued. Needs its own design pass, not a mechanical wire-up:
  how to combine a per-day deterministic/ensemble forecast total with the
  bootstrap's right-skewed remaining-days resample (add the forecasted
  near days as a fixed increment before resampling history only for the
  tail beyond the forecast horizon?), and whether the existing SEAS5
  monthly-mean tilt becomes redundant for the near-term portion once a
  real day-level forecast is wired in (it would still be the only signal
  for the tail beyond 16 days out, e.g. brackets checked early in a month).

When to revisit:
  Before `RAIN_TRADING_ENABLED`'s shadow gate is ever allowed to size real
  trades. No live cost today (shadow-only + TRADING_PAUSED), but this is
  exactly the class of gap Step 2's own handoff predicted (item 1's
  "mean-only" caveat) and now has 3 days of live confirmation behind it.

  `_fetch_ensemble_precip`'s existing single-day ensemble fetch (same

[RESOLVED 2026-07-26 -- explicit guard shipped. UPDATE 2026-08-03: the

  HURRICANE MARKETS -- EXPLICIT GUARD ADDED AFTER A CONFIRMED LIVE GAP
Priority: was believed Low/inert (see the parent RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE
  MARKETS entry) -- reclassified High for the guard fix itself once live
  testing found the "safe by coincidence" story was actually wrong.

Problem:
  Split out of the combined RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE MARKETS entry because
  hurricane isn't the same shape as rain/snow's per-city monthly ladder:
  Kalshi's real hurricane series are season-aggregate count/category
  markets keyed by storm name (`KXHURCAT-26FAUSTO-T5`, "Will Fausto become
  a Category 5 hurricane?") or by season (`KXHURCTOT-26DEC01-T9`, "more
  than 9 Atlantic hurricanes in 2026?"), plus a separate family of per-city
  landfall series (`KXHURMIA`, `KXHURTB`, `KXHURNYC`, ...) that show 0 open
  markets as of 2026-07-26 (confirmed live, pre-season -- hurricane season
  peaks Aug-Oct). Neither shape is city-keyed the way a `_KXHUR_MONTHLY_
  CITY`-style dict would assume, so this was never going to get the same
  Step-1 treatment as snow.
  A first-pass plan assumed hurricane tickers were already safe by
  coincidence -- `_parse_city_from_ticker()` returns `None` for count/
  category tickers and `_parse_market_condition()` returns `None` for
  landfall tickers, so `analyze_trade()`'s existing `no_city`/
  `no_condition` gates would catch both. An adversarial re-check against
  real, currently-open Kalshi tickers found this was WRONG: `KXHURCAT-
  26FAUSTO-T5` defeats BOTH gates simultaneously -- `_parse_city_from_
  ticker()` matches `"Austin"` off a substring inside `"FAUSTO"`, and
  `_parse_market_condition()` parses the `-T5` suffix + `yes_sub_title:
  "Category 5 or above"` into a real `{"type": "above", "threshold": 5.0}`
  condition. It was blocked today only by an unrelated, fragile accident --
  `KXHURCAT-26FAUSTO` has no ticker-embedded date, so `analyze_trade()`'s
  earlier `no_date` gate fires first -- and this exact codebase already has
  precedent (`KXRAIN*M`'s `close_time`-derived dating) for removing that
  kind of date dependency on a future pass, which would have silently
  reactivated the misclassification. Separately, `main.py`'s manual
  `cmd_order` path was confirmed to place a real order against ANY ticker,
  including a hurricane one, without `analyze_trade()`'s gates passing at
  all (`paper.py`'s own `check_position_limits()` docstring already
  documented this as "the one call path that can be reached WITHOUT going
  through analyze_trade() first").

What was fixed:
  An explicit `if ticker_up.startswith("KXHUR"): return None` guard, added
  in the three places that matter rather than relying on incidental gate
  ordering: `analyze_trade()` (first check in the function, before every
  other gate), `main.py cmd_order` (refuses the order outright, not just a
  warning), and `paper.check_position_limits()` (one of several call paths
  reachable without `analyze_trade()` -- see the correction below). 11 new
  regression tests (`tests/test_hurricane_gating.py`) pin the new explicit
  guard directly, including the concrete `KXHURCAT-26FAUSTO-T5` ticker that
  proved the old assumption wrong, plus controls confirming ordinary
  daily/rain tickers are unaffected and that `cmd_order` still refuses
  without even fetching the market. `order_executor.py` was deliberately
  NOT touched -- that loop only ever processes opportunities that already
  survived `analyze_trade()`, whose new guard makes it unreachable for this
  ticker family, same reachability shape as rain's own original Step 1
  found for that file (commit `b2171ba`).

  CORRECTION (same-day second opus review, before this ever got committed):
  the first-pass guard used a bare `ticker.startswith("KXHUR")` check in
  all three places. A live series-list scan (291 real "Climate and
  Weather" series) found this missed a large real, currently-open surface:
  `KXTROPSTORM` (8 open markets), `KXFIRSTHURRICANE` (53 open markets),
  `KXNAMEDSTORM`, `KXNEXTHURDATE`/`KXNEXTCAT5HURDATE`, and an entire
  *unprefixed* legacy `HUR*` namespace (`HURCAT`, `HURMIA`, `HURNYC`, ... --
  23 series, registered separately from their `KXHUR*` counterparts, both
  real) -- confirmed live that `HURCAT-26FAUSTO-T5` (no "KX") reproduces
  the exact same `_parse_city_from_ticker`/`_parse_market_condition`
  double-defeat as the original finding, and that `py main.py buy
  KXTROPSTORM-... yes 5 0.50` would have placed a real order under the
  first-pass guard. Fixed by replacing the prefix check with a single
  shared `weather_markets.is_hurricane_ticker()` (substring match on
  `("HUR", "TROPSTORM", "NAMEDSTORM")`, live-verified zero false positives
  against every tracked/known series -- in particular `KXSNOWSTORM`, a
  real but unrelated national snow-event series, does NOT match, which a
  naive `"STORM"`-only check would have wrongly caught) used by all three
  guard sites instead of three independent hardcoded literals. Also added
  the same explicit guard directly in `cmd_order` for monthly-snow tickers
  (previously relied solely on `check_position_limits`, which fails open
  on an unhandled exception in that call site) and corrected the "the one
  call path reachable without analyze_trade()" comments in `paper.py`/
  `order_executor.py` -- `main.cmd_paper` and `web_app`'s `/api/paper-order`
  are two more such paths (both still funnel through `check_position_limits`,
  so no live hole resulted, but the claim was wrong -- the same untraced-
  call-sites shape flagged before in this project, see
  [[feedback_trace_all_call_sites]]). A separately-flagged vacuous test
  (`KXDENSNOWM`'s city resolution passed even with the new dict deleted,
  since the pre-existing "DEN" substring fallback coincidentally agrees)
  was fixed with a mutation-style test pointing the dict at a fake city.
  8 more regression tests added for the broadened marker set (`KXTROPSTORM`,
  `KXFIRSTHURRICANE`, `KXNAMEDSTORM`, legacy `HURCAT`, `KXSNOWSTORM`-must-
  NOT-match, plus the new `cmd_order` snow guard) -- 19 hurricane +
  20 snow tests total, full scoped sweep (504 tests) passing, ruff/mypy/
  ruff-format clean.

What the fix does NOT do:
  No probability model exists for either hurricane market shape. This is a
  safety tightening only -- discovery, a real count/category model, and
  the per-city landfall series (still 0 open markets) all remain
  completely unbuilt. `KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES`/`check_series_drift()` still
  don't watch any hurricane series at all (deliberately -- adding one
  there without a matching parser branch would just reproduce this same
  bug class for a series check_series_drift would then be actively
  prompting someone to add).
  UPDATE 2026-08-03: the season-total count-market half of "count/category"
  now has a real model (see the dated resolution block below) --
  `KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES`/`check_series_drift()` now DO watch those 5 exact
  series (and only those 5, by exact series-ticker membership, not
  substring). KXHURCAT (the per-STORM category shape, e.g. "will Fausto
  become a Category 5 hurricane?") and the per-city landfall series (still
  0 open markets) remain completely unbuilt and still fully blocked by
  is_hurricane_ticker()'s original guard.

Why not now (for the real model):
  - Count/category markets aren't city-keyed at all -- they need their own
    data model (storm-name or season-keyed), not a per-city dict like
    rain/snow. The per-city landfall series ARE city-keyed but have 0 open
    markets today, so there's nothing live to build against yet.
  - Effort scales as its own product line, same reasoning the parent
    RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE MARKETS entry already gives for snow/hurricane
    generally.
  - UPDATE 2026-08-03: this reasoning held for KXHURCAT (per-storm, needs a
    live per-storm NHC forecast/advisory pipeline -- a genuinely different,
    more novel real-time data problem than the season-total shape) and for
    per-city landfall (still 0 open markets, confirmed live again
    2026-08-03 -- unchanged since 2026-07-26) -- both remain deliberately
    unbuilt. It did NOT hold for the season-total count shape once actually
    scoped: NOAA HURDAT2 (public, historical) plus Kalshi's own settled
    markets (for the live tilt) turned out to be a tractable, non-"own
    product line" lift once broken out from the other two shapes -- see the
    dated resolution block below.

When to revisit:
  - Once real per-city landfall markets actually open (re-check once
    hurricane season is underway, Aug-Oct 2026 -- still 0 open as of
    2026-08-03) AND there's real appetite to design that model separately.
  - KXHURCAT (per-storm category): needs a live per-storm NHC forecast/
    advisory data pipeline and a storm-name registry -- a different, more
    novel problem than the season-total shape below. Not started.
  - Independent of that: if `KXRAIN*M`'s close_time-derived dating pattern
    is ever extended to other market families, re-verify this guard still
    covers `KXHURCAT`-style tickers -- the fragile `no_date` accident this
    entry documents would stop being a backstop at that point, though the
    explicit `KXHUR` guard added here does not depend on it.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-03] HURRICANE MARKETS -- SEASON-TOTAL COUNT MODEL SHIPPED SHADOW-ONLY
Priority: was Low (see the parent RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE MARKETS entry and
  this entry's own "Why not now" above) -- the season-total count shape is
  now Medium, matching rain/snow's own real-shadow-model priority; KXHURCAT
  and per-city landfall remain Low/unbuilt.

Problem:
  Re-verified live 2026-08-03 (this session's own first step, per the
  standing "re-verify before building" workflow): the per-city landfall
  gate this entry's "When to revisit" named had NOT fired -- all ~54
  per-city/regional landfall series (KXHURMIA, KXHURNYC, KXHURPATH*, etc.)
  still show 0 open markets, unchanged since 2026-07-26. But the OTHER
  count/category shape -- season-total hurricane/tropical-storm counts --
  was very much open and tradeable, independent of that gate: 142 open
  markets across 5 series (`KXHURCTOT`/`KXHURCTOTMAJ`/`KXTROPSTORM` for the
  Atlantic, `KXHURRICANE`/`KXNAMEDSTORM` for Eastern+Central Pacific), e.g.
  "Will there be more than 9 Atlantic hurricanes in 2026?". User confirmed
  via AskUserQuestion this should be built first (recommended: climatology-
  only model, no live per-storm tracking needed, largest open-market
  surface), with NOAA HURDAT2 historical data as the primary source, and
  check_series_drift() extended for just these 5 series once they had a
  real parser.

  HURDAT2 only carries FINALIZED seasons (current year's data isn't added
  until ~April the following year), so it supplies the historical base
  distribution only -- the "current season count-to-date" tilt needed a
  different source. Found one requiring no new external dependency: Kalshi's
  own settled `KXHURRICANENAMES` markets (one per pre-assigned storm name
  per basin per season, "will storm X become a hurricane?") directly encode
  NHC's real season-to-date hurricane classifications. Confirmed live this
  session that 2026's Atlantic count is 0 so far and Eastern Pacific is 2
  (Fausto, Genevieve) via this exact derivation.

What shipped:
  New module `hurricane_climatology.py`: fetches/caches NOAA's Atlantic
  HURDAT2 file and combined Eastern+Central-Pacific HURDAT2 file (storms
  distinguished by their own AL/EP/CP storm-ID prefix -- confirmed live the
  Pacific file already covers both basins), parses each storm's max
  sustained wind and the day-of-year it first crossed each of Kalshi's own
  literal settlement thresholds (34kt tropical-storm / 64kt hurricane /
  96kt major-hurricane -- matches rules_primary text exactly, not NHC's own
  separately-evolving classification-code convention). Builds a 30-most-
  recent-complete-season empirical bootstrap distribution per (basin,
  count_type) -- 30 years chosen deliberately (not just copying this
  codebase's existing "30" convention): avoids diluting a current-era
  estimate with the markedly quieter pre-1995 AMO phase. Parser cross-
  checked live against real published 2023/2024 Atlantic season totals
  (18/11/5 and 20/7/3 named-storm/hurricane/major-hurricane counts) --
  exact match both years.

  The live tilt: for each historical window year, computes that year's OWN
  count-as-of the SAME calendar day-of-year as today, then adds (today's
  real current_count minus that year's historical to-date count) to that
  year's real season-end count -- bootstraps the REMAINING count from
  history and adds it to this season's actual progress, mirroring
  acis_precip.historical_remaining_and_full_month_sums's "month-to-date-
  actual + historical-remaining" shape exactly, just discrete counts
  instead of a continuous inches total. Scoped to count_type="hurricane"
  ONLY -- major_hurricane/tropical_storm ship climatology-only (no tilt) in
  this pass; deriving a clean per-basin current count for those two would
  need a per-year storm-name-to-basin mapping table (KXHURCAT's per-storm
  tickers aren't basin-tagged) that doesn't exist yet, an honest, explicit
  scope decision, not a silent gap.

  `weather_markets.py`: `is_hurricane_count_ticker()` narrowly carves out
  the 5 series (by exact series-ticker, NOT substring/startswith --
  "KXHURCTOT" is a strict prefix of "KXHURCTOTMAJ", so anything else would
  misclassify one as the other) from `is_hurricane_ticker()`'s much broader
  marker set, which still blocks everything else. `_parse_hurricane_count_
  condition()` reads floor_strike/strike_type directly off Kalshi's own
  market fields (same established convention as every other ladder-market
  branch here), deriving basin/count_type/season_year from the ticker
  string itself (`_hurricane_count_key_from_ticker`, shared with tracker.py's
  counter below). `_analyze_hurricane_count_trade()` computes the real
  probability/edge/Kelly size via `_price_and_size()` (same shared tail
  every other market type uses) and is dispatched from `analyze_trade()`
  exactly like rain/snow's monthly-ladder fast-paths -- required threading
  a `_is_hurricane_count` bypass through the no_forecast/no_city/no_coords
  gates (this market family has no city at all, unlike rain/snow) and a new
  `HURRICANE_MAX_DAYS_OUT` (260 days -- these markets open ~7-8 months
  before close, confirmed live) replacing `MAX_DAYS_OUT` for this ticker
  family in the days-out gate.

  Shadow-only rollout, same shape as rain/snow: `_hurricane_count_gates_
  active()` (HURRICANE_TRADING_ENABLED env var + >=20 settled distinct
  (basin, count_type, season_year) events, mirroring `_rain_gates_active()`/
  `_snow_gates_active()` exactly) gates real order placement in
  `order_executor._auto_place_trades()`'s per-ticker shadow-routing branch,
  `paper.check_position_limits()`, and all 3 of main.py's manual order paths
  (cmd_order, _quick_paper_buy, cmd_paper buy) -- `analyze_trade()` itself is
  NOT gated (it always computes the real analysis, same as rain/snow, so
  calibration data accumulates regardless of the gate). Explicitly documented
  as a MUCH slower-clearing floor than rain/snow's ~2-month estimate: a
  season-count market settles AT MOST once per year per (basin, count_type)
  -- 9 combinations total across 3 basins -- so this floor could take
  several YEARS to clear, not weeks or months; a real, structural cadence
  difference, not an oversight.

  Current-count-to-date cache: `analyze_trade()`'s call chain has no live
  Kalshi client of its own (unlike every other market type, which only need
  forecast data already attached to `enriched`) -- mirrors
  `refresh_hourly_target_hours()`'s exact division of labor: a new
  `refresh_hurricane_count_to_date()`, called from `cmd_cron` right beside
  `refresh_hourly_target_hours`, fetches settled `KXHURRICANENAMES` markets
  once/basin/day and caches the count to `HURRICANE_COUNT_TO_DATE_PATH`
  (added to `paths.py`, not module-local -- matches `HOURLY_TARGET_HOURS_
  PATH`'s own shared-state precedent); `_analyze_hurricane_count_trade()`
  reads it client-free via `_get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date()`, which
  refuses a cache entry from the wrong season_year (never lets a stale
  prior-season count silently tilt the current season).

  `tracker.count_settled_hurricane_predictions()`: counts DISTINCT (basin,
  count_type, season_year) events, NOT raw prediction rows -- the same
  raw-row-vs-distinct-event inflation risk `count_settled_snow_predictions()`
  was already fixed for (a single season/count-type settles up to ~9 sibling
  strikes from the SAME real outcome).

  `check_series_drift()`/`KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES` now watch exactly these 5
  series (exact-match, not substring -- deliberately narrower than
  `is_hurricane_ticker()`'s marker set, so this can never start watching a
  hurricane series with no matching parser branch, the exact bug class the
  parent entry above warns about).

  87 new tests: `tests/test_hurricane_climatology.py` (26 -- HURDAT2 parsing
  against a hand-verifiable synthetic fixture, season counting, the tilt
  bootstrap, exceedance probability, bootstrap CI), `tests/test_hurricane_
  markets.py` (60 -- ticker/condition parsing incl. the KXHURCTOT/
  KXHURCTOTMAJ prefix-collision guard, the shadow gate, the count-to-date
  cache, the full `_analyze_hurricane_count_trade` dispatch with mocked
  climatology data, and the `check_position_limits`/`cmd_order` conditional-
  guard tests mirroring snow's own), plus 3 new shadow-routing tests in
  `tests/test_shadow_predictions.py`, 5 new distinct-event-counting tests in
  `tests/test_tracker.py`, and 1 new exclusion test in `tests/test_
  consistency.py`. 3 pre-existing `tests/test_hurricane_gating.py` tests
  updated (KXHURCTOT/KXTROPSTORM/KXNAMEDSTORM no longer hit
  `hurricane_not_supported` -- they now reach `condition_parse`/`no_date`
  instead, a real, correct behavior change, not a broken test); every other
  test in that file (KXHURCAT, per-city landfall, legacy unprefixed HUR*,
  the broadened-marker-set regression controls) unchanged and still passing.
  8 real mutations run against the highest-risk logic (basin/count_type
  classification, exceedance-probability direction, the blanket-guard
  carve-out condition, the distinct-event dedup, the tilt arithmetic,
  paper.py's conditional gate, the fail-closed dispatcher fix, and the
  consistency.py exclusion) -- all caught by the new tests, all reverted
  cleanly. Full scoped regression (test_hurricane_climatology.py +
  test_hurricane_markets.py + test_hurricane_gating.py +
  test_shadow_predictions.py + test_tracker.py + test_series_drift.py +
  test_consistency.py, 482 tests) plus a broader sweep (test_rain_
  markets.py, test_snow_markets.py, test_forecasting.py,
  test_infrastructure.py, test_weather_markets.py, test_price_and_size.py,
  test_city_registry_manifest.py, test_dead_code_scan.py) all pass -- one
  pre-existing, unrelated failure (`test_forecasting.py::TestLearnedWeights::
  test_load_learned_weights_handles_non_numeric_value`) confirmed present
  identically before this session's changes (via git stash), not caused by
  this work. ruff + ruff format + mypy clean on every touched file.

  Independent opus review (3 parallel agents, scoped by subsystem --
  climatology/math, ticker-parsing/dispatch, safety-guard wiring -- effort=
  high): 15 findings total, every one fixed before commit (none skipped as
  out-of-scope, except one explicitly pre-existing gap noted below). Most
  consequential:
  - HIGH (math): `season_end_total_distribution` derived its year window
    from `{s["year"] for s in storms}` rather than an explicit calendar
    range -- silently DROPPING any season with zero storms of the
    requested basin's prefix instead of counting it as a real 0. Invisible
    for Atlantic/Eastern-Pacific (every year has >=1 storm) but measured
    live to overstate Central Pacific's `P(>0 hurricanes)` by 23 points
    (0.600 vs the correct 0.367 over the same 30-year span) -- CPAC has 35
    real gap years out of 77 (1949-2025). Fixed by iterating an explicit
    calendar range and calling `season_end_counts()` for every year in it
    (which already correctly returns 0 for an absent year).
  - HIGH (dispatch): a hurricane-count-series ticker whose OWN fields
    failed to parse (missing `floor_strike`, unexpected `strike_type`) fell
    through `_parse_market_condition()` into the generic temperature-
    threshold parser below -- which matches this family's real "-T9"/
    "-T30" ticker suffix as a °F threshold, reproducing the exact KXHURCAT
    bug class the whole `is_hurricane_ticker()` guard exists to prevent
    (terminates in an `AssertionError` today via this file's own
    `assert city is not None` narrowing, or silently mis-scores under
    `python -O`, where asserts are stripped). Fixed: any ticker whose
    series is one of the 5 hurricane-count series now fails closed
    (returns `None` outright) at that dispatcher, regardless of why its
    own parse failed, rather than falling through.
  - HIGH (safety): adding the 5 series to `KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES` (so
    `get_weather_markets()` now returns them) exposed them to
    `consistency.find_violations()`, whose output feeds `main.py`'s arb
    auto-placer (`paper.place_paper_order`) DIRECTLY -- with no shadow-gate
    check of its own, and (unlike rain/snow) not merely "safe by
    coincidence": KXHURCTOT-style tickers' real day-level date and "-T9"
    threshold suffix both match `consistency.py`'s grouping regexes; only
    today's real title text (lacking the literal "above"/">" the
    threshold-direction fallback requires) kept it inert -- the exact
    "safe by coincidence" shape this project already burned itself on once
    for this same ticker family. Fixed by adding the same exclusion
    rain/snow/hourly already have in `consistency._group_markets()`.
  - MEDIUM-HIGH (math): an empty (non-exception) `KXHURRICANENAMES` fetch
    response -- series renamed, event-ticker format changed, transient
    API-side filter change -- previously wrote `count=0` for every basin,
    indistinguishable from a real "zero hurricanes so far" season. Fixed:
    only write a basin whose event_ticker matched at least one settled
    market at all; otherwise leave it unwritten so the existing missing-
    entry fallback (climatology-only) applies.
  - HIGH (math): the count-to-date cache's `date` field was written but
    never checked for staleness on read -- a stalled refresh job (repeated
    fetch failures, or cron simply not running) would silently serve an
    arbitrarily-old count-to-date forever, desynced from `as_of_month_day`
    (always derived from TODAY). Verified this can flip a real probability
    from 0.99 to 0.01 with no warning. Fixed: reject any cache entry older
    than 2 days, falling back to climatology-only.
  - LOW-MEDIUM (dispatch): `KXHURRICANE`'s major-vs-total count-type
    derivation (`endswith("MAJ")` else "hurricane") failed OPEN -- any
    other suffix would silently price a major-hurricane market against
    total-hurricane climatology, a materially fatter distribution, with no
    warning. Fixed with an explicit `"MAJ"`/`"TOT"` allow-list, fail closed
    otherwise (also tightened for `KXNAMEDSTORM`, previously unconditional).
  - Also fixed: `season_year` cross-checked against the market's own
    close_time (>1yr mismatch now fails closed -- protects
    `tracker.count_settled_hurricane_predictions()`'s dedup key from a
    malformed ticker); leap-year misalignment in day-of-year threshold-
    crossing comparisons (switched `threshold_day`/`as_of_*` from ordinal
    day-of-year ints to `(month, day)` tuples, which compare correctly
    regardless of either year's leap status); an absurd wind reading
    (e.g. 9999, not the `-999` missing sentinel) no longer fabricates a
    storm; a truncated/stale HURDAT2 download now logs a loud warning if
    its newest storm year falls more than 2 years behind today;
    `_get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date` no longer raises on a corrupt
    non-dict cache entry or a non-int `count`; `count_settled_hurricane_
    predictions()`'s parse-failure warning no longer fires for the
    unrelated `KXHURRICANENAMES` series (a `LIKE 'KXHURRICANE%'` prefix
    collision that would have desensitized the real "gate frozen at 0"
    alarm had that series ever been logged as a prediction).
  - NOT fixed (explicitly out of scope, flagged as a separate follow-up
    task): `cmd_today()`'s "[P] Place" interactive path bypasses
    `TRADING_PAUSED` and every shadow-only gate entirely (rain/snow/
    hurricane-count alike) -- confirmed PRE-EXISTING (rain and snow already
    had this exact gap before this session), not introduced or worsened by
    this work. Fixing it means touching the shared placement path for all
    three market families at once, out of scope for a hurricane-specific
    session.

What this does NOT do:
  Real sizing -- shadow/log-only until HURRICANE_TRADING_ENABLED=1 AND the
  20-distinct-event floor clears (expected to take years, not months, see
  above). major_hurricane/tropical_storm count types have no live tilt yet
  (climatology-only) -- only "hurricane" (category 1+) has a clean, exact,
  basin-tagged Kalshi-settled-market source today. KXHURCAT (per-storm
  category) and per-city landfall markets remain completely untouched --
  still gated by is_hurricane_ticker()'s original blanket guard, still 0
  open markets for landfall as of this session's live re-check.

When to revisit:
  - Once HURRICANE_TRADING_ENABLED is set and real settled data accumulates
    (expect a multi-year timescale, not the ~2-month rain/snow estimate) --
    check get_signal_graduation_report()-style correlation before ever
    relying on real sizing.
  - major_hurricane/tropical_storm live tilt: needs a per-year storm-name-
    to-basin mapping (WMO's pre-assigned name lists are public and fixed
    years in advance) to derive a current-count-to-date from KXHURCAT's
    per-storm settled results the same way KXHURRICANENAMES already does
    for "hurricane". Not started.
  - KXHURCAT/per-city landfall: see the updated "When to revisit" in the
    entry above -- unchanged by this session's work.

Priority: was Low (see the parent RAIN / SNOW / HURRICANE MARKETS entry) --
  now Medium, matching the season-count model's own priority above.

Problem:
  Re-verified live 2026-08-07 (this session's own first step, per the
  standing "re-verify before building" workflow): the parent entry's own

  open," which was stale -- it predated the season-count model above
  (shipped 2026-08-03) and was never updated afterward. Live re-check found
  three genuinely still-open hurricane shapes: per-storm category
  (KXHURCAT, 3 open markets on the live storm Fausto, needs a live NHC
  advisory/forecast-cone pipeline), first-hurricane-by-name

  above with no new live-data pipeline, unlike the other two. KXHURCAT and
  KXFIRSTHURRICANE remain fully open, their own future entries, not touched
  this session.

  Market shape (confirmed live against every open market in both series):
  "Will [an Atlantic hurricane / an Atlantic Category-5 hurricane] form
  before <date>?" -- floor_strike/strike_type are null; the entire condition
  is the market's own close_time (e.g. close_time "2026-09-15T03:59Z" <->
  yes_sub_title "Before Sep 15, 2026"). Both series are Atlantic-only in
  every real market (rules_primary says "in the Atlantic"; no EPAC/CPAC
  sibling series exist).

What shipped:
  hurricane_climatology.py: NEXT_EVENT_THRESHOLDS_KT = {"hurricane": 64,
  "cat5_hurricane": 137} (137kt matches KXHURCAT's own live-confirmed
  Category-5 threshold); parse_hurdat2's threshold_day now built from the
  union of COUNT_THRESHOLDS_KT.values() | NEXT_EVENT_THRESHOLDS_KT.values()
  -- one parse serves both models, no new fetch. New first_occurrence_day()
  (earliest day a season's storms first reached a given kt), and
  next_event_outcomes()/next_event_probability()/bootstrap_ci_next_event()
  (day-of-first-occurrence analog of season_end_total_distribution()/
  exceedance_probability()/bootstrap_ci()).

  A real design correction caught during implementation (self-review before
  this ever reached the user, then re-verified against live behavior): the
  first draft always conditioned the historical distribution on "today's
  date," regardless of whether the model actually KNEW the event hadn't
  happened yet this season. For cat5_hurricane (no live signal at all) and
  for hurricane type when the count-to-date cache is stale/missing, that
  would have silently ASSUMED "hasn't happened yet" -- reproducing the exact
  stale-cache "flips a probability with no warning" failure mode
  _get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date's own staleness guard already exists
  to prevent for the count model above. Fixed: next_event_outcomes() only
  conditions on as_of_month_day when the caller passes it explicitly (only
  when live data CONFIRMS "not yet happened"); otherwise it runs fully
  unconditional (every window year contributes, no eligibility filtering) --
  mirrors season_end_total_distribution's own
  "as_of_month_day is None or current_count is None -> unconditional"
  fallback exactly.

  Also caught live during implementation: parse_city_date()'s generic
  ticker-date regex, run against "KXNEXTHURDATE-26DEC01-26SEP15", matches
  the FIRST date-like segment ("26DEC01" -- a season-reference suffix shared
  identically by every "before <date>" sibling) rather than the real
  threshold date in the second segment, producing a non-None but WRONG
  target_date (Dec 1, not the market's real Sep 15 close). Confirmed live
  before writing any gate logic. analyze_trade()'s no_date/no_city/
  no_coords/no_forecast gates are all bypassed for this ticker family (same
  as monthly rain/snow, NOT the same as hurricane-count -- hurricane-count's
  own ticker date suffix IS its real close date, so it safely reuses the
  generic target_date-based past-date check; this family cannot), and it
  gets its own close_time-derived past-close check
  (_hur_next_event_close_dt) instead, exactly like rain/snow's own
  _rain_close_dt/_snow_close_dt.

  weather_markets.py: is_hurricane_next_event_ticker()/
  _parse_hurricane_next_event_condition() (condition carries only
  event_type, never a duplicated kt -- _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade

  HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_TRADING_ENABLED, own 20-sample floor via
  tracker.count_settled_hurricane_next_event_predictions() -- kept fully

  tracker.py: count_settled_hurricane_next_event_predictions() -- unlike

What this does NOT do:

Independent opus review: given the size, scoped to 3 parallel Agent(opus,
  effort=high) passes by subsystem (climatology math; ticker-parsing/
  dispatch; safety-guard wiring across main.py/paper.py/order_executor.py/
  consistency.py/tracker.py), mirroring the count model's own precedent.
  2 HIGH findings, independently surfaced by two different reviewers:
  (1) bootstrap_ci_next_event didn't clamp its output to [0.01, 0.99] the
  way next_event_probability already does -- a unanimous outcome set (the
  common case for kt=64; every recent Atlantic season has a hurricane by
  mid-September) produced an exact (1.0, 1.0)/(0.0, 0.0) CI, which
  _price_and_size's ci_high<=ci_low fallback turns into kelly_fraction(1.0,
  price)==0.0 -- silently zeroing size for the model's own highest-
  confidence signals AND (since shadow logging shares the same size-then-
  log validator) permanently freezing count_settled_hurricane_next_event_
  predictions() at 0, so the 20-sample graduation gate could never open.
  Fixed by clamping. (2) No minimum-sample floor on conditional mode --
  measured against real Atlantic data, the eligible-year subset already
  drops below 15 by ~Aug 1 and hits 0 by mid-September, so the model could
  compute (and shadow-log, poisoning Brier scoring) a full-strength signal
  off 2-3 data points, or fabricate a bare 0.5 from zero. Fixed:
  _analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade now falls back to the unconditional
  baseline (same one used when occurred_this_season is unknown) whenever
  the eligible set is below 15, the same threshold bootstrap_ci_next_event's
  own floor already uses.
  3 more MEDIUM findings fixed: _CONDITION_CONFIDENCE was missing a
  "hurricane_next_event" entry entirely, so the `.get(condition_type, 1.0)`
  fallback silently gave the least-validated model in the codebase the
  MAXIMUM confidence multiplier -- added an explicit 0.50 (below
  hurricane_count's own 0.55, same "a season IS the sample unit" reasoning
  plus this model's extra within-season granularity). target_month_day used
  close_dt's raw UTC date, but Kalshi's "Before <date>" wording is an ET
  calendar date (close_time "...T03:59Z" is 23:59 ET the PRIOR day) --
  measured as a systematic ~1/window_years bias per boundary year, material
  for the smaller cat5 sample; fixed via ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
  conversion before reading .month/.day, mirroring _metar_lock_in's own
  city-local-date pattern. The condition_type exclusion lists gating live-
  trading maturity signals (tracker.count_settled_predictions/_rolling,
  get_rolling_win_rate) and ML training pools (calibration.py, ml_bias.py)
  were never extended for EITHER hurricane sub-model -- closed for both
  hurricane_count (pre-existing gap, closed while touching the same lists)
  and hurricane_next_event across all 9 sites, with regression tests
  (confirmed load-bearing for ml_bias.py's train_all_temperature_scaling in
  particular -- hurricane rows always carry days_out>=1 and a real
  city="HUR_<basin>", so neither of that function's existing NULL-checks
  would have caught them).
  Also fixed: parse_city_date() returned a non-None but WRONG target_date
  (the ticker's shared season-reference suffix, not the real close date) for
  this ticker family -- several downstream consumers (tracker.log_prediction's
  market_date/days_out, order_executor.py, main.py, trade_cycle.py,

  if _date is None" pattern that only rain/snow's (always-None) and
  hurricane-count's (always-correct) _date values were safe against --
  fixed by making parse_city_date() return None for this series explicitly,
  same as rain/snow. consistency.py's own exclusion test wasn't actually
  mutation-proof (real next-event tickers can't be parsed by _parse_
  threshold's -T/-B suffix regex regardless of the guard, so disabling the
  guard didn't change the test's outcome) -- added a second test using an
  adversarial -T5/-T6-suffixed ticker shape, confirmed via manual mutation
  to actually fail when the guard is removed. The tracker.py counter's SQL
  LIKE prefix (a coarse pre-filter) was broader than is_hurricane_next_
  event_ticker()'s series-exact match -- currently unreachable (a lookalike
  series would contain "HUR" and never pass analyze_trade()'s blanket guard
  to get logged at all) but tightened to exact-match in Python anyway,

  identical risk shape. first_occurrence_day() now raises on an unrecognized
  kt instead of silently returning a confidently-wrong all-False result

  Also strengthened 3 weak tests in test_hurricane_climatology.py (one

  distinguish "takes the season minimum" from "takes whichever storm is

  NOT fixed, documented as explicit known limitations rather than silently
  dropped: (a) a genuine design gap, CONFIRMED (not speculative) via the
  official Kalshi contract terms PDF (assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/
  STORMDATE.pdf, fetched and read live this session): the real Payout
  Criterion is "any Atlantic tropical storm... reaching <storm category>
  intensity... at any point after Issuance and before <date>" -- anchored to
  this specific CONTRACT'S Issuance (its own open_time), not season start --
  and "After the initial Contract, Contract iterations will be listed on an
  as-needed basis," confirming Kalshi DOES roll this ticker over to a fresh
  "next hurricane" question (a new Issuance point) after each qualifying
  storm. This model's occurred_this_season boolean is keyed off season-wide
  count-to-date, not "since this specific event's Issuance" -- so once a
  rollover happens, the occurred_this_season=True -> 0.99 shortcut would
  misprice a genuinely-still-open post-rollover question as already
  resolved. The two readings coincide TODAY only because the Atlantic count
  is genuinely 0 so far AND this event's own open_time (2026-08-06,
  confirmed live) predates any hurricane this season -- confirmed live via

  zero markets ever created under it -- this product never actually

  to verify against). User's explicit decision after reviewing this
  research: defer as its own follow-up backlog entry rather than fix now
  (see the new entry filed alongside this one) or partially fix -- not
  fixed to any degree in this pass.
  (b) `order_executor._ticker_edge_share`'s event-key (`(city, date, var)`)
  conflates hurricane-count and hurricane-next-event opportunities sharing a

  one sub-model can dilute a live-gated opp's Kelly sizing from the other --
  zero impact today (both sub-models are shadow-gated), only matters once
  one of the two graduates first; redesigning the shared edge-share

  raises IndexError -- identical latent issue already exists unfixed in the
  sibling bootstrap_ci this codebase has run in production; not exercised at

When to revisit:
