[OPEN 2026-08-07 -- new, split out of "HURRICANE MARKETS -- TIME-TO-NEXT-EVENT MODEL SHIPPED SHADOW-ONLY" above per its own "user's explicit decision: defer as its own follow-up entry" note] HURRICANE NEXT-EVENT MODEL'S OCCURRED_THIS_SEASON SIGNAL IS SEASON-SCOPED, NOT ISSUANCE-SCOPED (KALSHI CONFIRMS ROLLOVER)
Priority: Low -- shadow-only, zero live-money risk regardless (see below);
  only affects the accuracy of a shadow-logged signal, not any real order.

Problem:
  Confirmed via the official Kalshi contract terms PDF (assets.kalshi.com/
  contract_terms/STORMDATE.pdf, fetched and read live this session -- not
  speculation): KXNEXTHURDATE/KXNEXTCAT5HURDATE's real Payout Criterion is
  "any Atlantic tropical storm has been classified... reaching <storm
  category> intensity... at any point after Issuance and before <date>" --
  anchored to THIS SPECIFIC CONTRACT's Issuance (its own open_time), not
  season start. And: "After the initial Contract, Contract iterations will
  be listed on an as-needed basis at the discretion of the Exchange" --
  Kalshi confirms it rolls this ticker over to a fresh "next hurricane"
  question (a new Issuance point) after each qualifying storm settles the
  current one early (the PDF's own Expiration Date rule: "If an event
  described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an
  earlier date").

  The shipped model (weather_markets._analyze_hurricane_next_event_trade)
  has no concept of "since this event's Issuance" -- occurred_this_season
  (event_type="hurricane") is keyed off `_get_cached_hurricane_count_to_date`,
  a SEASON-WIDE cumulative count, and the unconditional-mode fallback's
  first_occurrence_day() climatology measures "day of the season's FIRST
  qualifying storm" from historical Januarys/Mays, not "days elapsed since
  a specific mid-season Issuance date." Both are season-start-anchored
  proxies for what should be an Issuance-anchored question.

  Confirmed live this session: the currently open event's own open_time is
  2026-08-06 (mid-season, not season start -- itself circumstantial
  evidence this event may already be layered on prior seasons' pattern of
  waiting until real hurricane-season activity picks up before listing, not
  necessarily evidence of a rollover). client.get_events(series_ticker=
  "KXNEXTHURDATE") shows exactly ONE real event today ("KXNEXTHURDATE-
  26DEC01"); a second event ("KXNEXTHURDATE-0", sub_title "In 2025") exists
  but has ZERO markets ever created under it in any status (open/settled/
  closed) -- this product never actually launched with real markets before
  2026, so there is no historical rollover instance to directly observe and
  verify the exact mechanics against (e.g. whether ALL 8 "before <date>"
  siblings in an event settle simultaneously on rollover, or something more
  granular).

  Practical impact today: "since season start" and "since this event's
  Issuance" currently coincide -- the Atlantic hurricane count-to-date is
  genuinely 0 so far this season (confirmed live via the existing
  hurricane_count_to_date.json cache), and this event's own open_time
  predates that. The gap is real but latent -- it activates the first time
  a hurricane forms this season AND Kalshi lists a rollover event, at which
  point occurred_this_season=True would misprice a genuinely-still-open
  post-rollover question as already resolved (prob=0.99), and the
  unconditional-mode fallback's season-wide climatology would still be
  answering "day of season's first hurricane" instead of "days since this
  new Issuance."

Why not now:
  - Correctly fixing occurred_this_season requires a genuinely new live
    signal: WHEN each settled KXHURRICANENAMES storm actually crossed
    hurricane strength (a date), not just a cumulative season count, so it
    can be compared against a specific event's open_time. Real new data/
    cache design work, closer in size to the original count-to-date cache
    itself than to a quick fix.
  - User's explicit decision (asked via AskUserQuestion after this research
    was presented): defer as its own follow-up entry rather than build the
    full signal now or ship a partial mechanical fix (e.g. swapping the
    conditional-mode "as_of" reference from today's date to the market's
    own open_time -- a cheaper, strictly-more-correct change that was also
    on the table and also NOT taken this pass).
  - Entirely shadow-only in the meantime (HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_TRADING_
    ENABLED defaults off) -- the mispricing this entry describes can only
    ever affect a logged shadow prediction's accuracy, never a real order.

When to revisit:
  - The moment either (a) hurricane_count_to_date.json's ATL count first
    goes from 0 to 1 this season, or (b) client.get_events(series_ticker=
    "KXNEXTHURDATE") first returns more than the one current event --
    whichever comes first. At that point, check live whether the existing
    open "before <date>" markets settled/closed (confirming the rollover
    actually happened) before assuming the gap has activated.
  - If ever prioritized: build the per-storm-became-hurricane-date signal
    (mirrors refresh_hurricane_count_to_date's shape, sourced from settled
    KXHURRICANENAMES markets' own settlement timestamps rather than just
    their yes/no result), then key occurred_this_season off "any qualifying
    storm since this event's own open_time" instead of season-wide count.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-08] hurricane_climatology.fetch_hurdat2_raw's CACHE WRITE ISN'T ATOMIC -- THE ONLY RAW-TEXT CACHE IN THIS CODEBASE THAT SKIPS safe_io
Priority: Low -- currently low-probability (needs two processes racing to
  refresh the SAME stale HURDAT2 cache file within the same narrow window),
  but a real corruption path this project has already been burned by once
  for the identical bug CLASS on JSON caches (see "SAFE_IO -- EMERGENCY-COPY
  FALLBACK SILENTLY CLOBBERED THE ORIGINAL FILE" elsewhere in this file,
  RESOLVED 2026-07-27), and today's routine
  multi-parallel-worktree-session pattern (all worktrees share ONE physical
  data/ directory via paths.py -- see [[feedback_worktree_data_dir_gotcha]])
  makes concurrent collisions on this exact file meaningfully more likely
  than when it shipped as a single-session feature.

Problem:
  hurricane_climatology.py:144 (fetch_hurdat2_raw, shipped 2026-08-03 as
  part of the season-count hurricane model -- not introduced by the
  2026-08-07 time-to-next-event session, just never caught before) writes
  its disk cache with a plain `cache.write_text(text)`. Every OTHER
  cache-shaped write in this same area of the codebase goes through
  safe_io.atomic_write_json() instead -- confirmed live via
  `grep -n "cache.write_text\|atomic_write" hurricane_climatology.py
  acis_precip.py climatology.py`: acis_precip.py and climatology.py both
  consistently use safe_io.atomic_write_json for their own caches (climate
  archive data, forecast_sigma.json); hurricane_climatology.py's HURDAT2
  cache is the lone plain-write holdout. A concurrent write from a second
  process refreshing the same stale cache (two parallel worktree sessions
  both triggering hc.load_basin_storms() around the same time, or a live
  cron cycle overlapping with a manual research script) risks a reader
  seeing a partially-written file mid-write, or one write's content
  silently interleaving with another's -- the same corruption shape
  atomic_write_json's own emergency-copy-fallback bug (fixed 2026-07-27,
  see that entry) existed specifically to prevent for JSON caches.

  Not a drop-in fix: safe_io.atomic_write_json() is JSON-shaped (its own
  name says so); hurricane_climatology.py's cache is raw HURDAT2 text, not
  JSON. There is currently no safe_io helper for atomic raw-text writes --
  confirmed via `grep -n "^def " safe_io.py`: only atomic_write_json and
  atomic_write_json_with_history exist.

What it would look like:
  Add a generic safe_io.atomic_write_text() (or atomic_write_bytes(),
  whichever safe_io's existing tempfile+rename internals generalize to more
  cleanly) mirroring atomic_write_json's own write-to-tempfile-then-
  os.replace() shape, then swap hurricane_climatology.py's
  `cache.write_text(text)` for it. Small, mechanical once the helper exists
  -- the real work is designing the helper to share safe_io's existing
  emergency-copy-fallback/PID-keyed-tempfile conventions rather than being a
  parallel, independently-maintained implementation.

Why not now:
  User explicitly asked for this to be filed rather than fixed immediately
  (2026-08-07) -- currently low-probability (narrow race window: only
  matters when the 30-day cache is actually stale AND two processes refresh
  it in the same window) and shadow-only downstream (a corrupted HURDAT2
  cache would degrade a probability model's accuracy, not place a bad
  order), so not urgent enough to interrupt other in-flight work for.

When to revisit:
  - Before HURRICANE_TRADING_ENABLED or HURRICANE_NEXT_EVENT_TRADING_ENABLED
    is ever flipped on for real (a corrupted cache feeding a real-money
    Kelly size is a materially different risk than feeding a shadow log).
  - If parse_hurdat2 ever starts raising on malformed input (it currently
    doesn't -- see parse_hurdat2's own "stopping parse" comments) a
    corrupted mid-write cache read could produce a hard crash rather than a
    silently-degraded probability; worth re-checking this entry's own risk
    assessment if that changes.

RESOLVED 2026-08-08: Re-verified every claim in this entry live before
  touching code -- all held (hurricane_climatology.py:144's plain
  `cache.write_text(text)`; acis_precip.py/climatology.py both exclusively
  use safe_io.atomic_write_json; safe_io.py had exactly 2 WRITE-shaped
  public functions, atomic_write_json and atomic_write_json_with_history --
  both JSON-only, no raw-text/bytes variant existed). Correction (opus-
  review-caught 2026-08-08): the "2 public functions" phrasing above
  originally undercounted -- safe_io.py actually had 4 public functions
  total (project_root and check_emergency_copies are real, unrelated to
  writing); the substantive claim (no non-JSON atomic-write helper existed)
  was and is correct, the count of ALL public functions was not. Also
  confirmed atomic_write_json_with_history is itself already a thin wrapper
  around atomic_write_json (history-backup, then delegates) rather than a
  duplicate implementation -- the existing precedent for exactly the
  composition this entry's own "What it would look like" asked for.

  Shipped safe_io.atomic_write_text(text, path, retries=3,
  fallback_dir=None, emergency_copy=True) by extracting atomic_write_json's
  write-temp/fsync/rename/retry/emergency-copy core (previously all inline
  in atomic_write_json's own body) into a
  new private _atomic_write_payload(payload: str, ...) helper, then having
  BOTH atomic_write_json (serializes to JSON first) and the new
  atomic_write_text (uses the raw text as-is) call it -- not a parallel,
  independently-maintained implementation. atomic_write_json's external
  behavior is unchanged (all 31 pre-existing safe_io tests pass unmodified).
  Two of the shared helper's own log messages were still hardcoded to say
  "atomic_write_json" even though atomic_write_text now goes through the
  same path -- caught and fixed before it became a real caller-misleading-log
  issue in production, not just a review finding.

  Swapped hurricane_climatology.py's `cache.write_text(text)` for
  `safe_io.atomic_write_text(text, cache)`, matching the exact bare-call
  (no local try/except around just that line, an outer function-level
  try/except already provides the same fail-open safety net) convention
  already used by every safe_io.atomic_write_json call site in
  acis_precip.py/climatology.py.

  fetch_hurdat2_raw had ZERO existing test coverage of any kind before this
  session (confirmed via repo-wide grep). Added a new TestFetchHurdat2Raw
  CacheWrite class (2 tests: successful-fetch-writes-via-atomic_write_text,
  cache-write-failure-still-returns-fetched-text) plus new tests in
  test_safe_io.py: round-trip correctness, parent-dir auto-creation, shared
  retry/raise behavior with atomic_write_json (same total-failure scenario,
  same AtomicWriteError), and emergency-copy-on-failure. A 3rd
  hurricane_climatology test (racing writers never produce a torn cache
  file) was written but moved to test_safe_io.py during opus review round
  1 -- it never actually exercised hurricane_climatology.py's own code, see
  below.

  Mutation-tested the wiring specifically (not just the underlying
  primitive): temporarily reverted hurricane_climatology.py's call back to
  the original bare `cache.write_text(text)`, confirmed 2 of the 3 new
  hurricane_climatology tests correctly failed (the spy-based "atomic_write_
  text was actually called" assertion, and the write-failure-must-not-write-
  a-file assertion, which failed because the mocked failure path no longer
  applied to the reverted code), then restored the fix.

  Independent opus review (effort: high) of that state found the fix was
  sound but incomplete, 6 findings:

  - MEDIUM: the emergency-copy machinery is unconditional, and cron.py's
    check_emergency_copies() monitor pages an operator (notify.
    send_system_alert()) every cycle for ANY file in data/.emergency/,
    described as needing manual attention -- a disposable, trivially
    re-fetchable 4-7MB HURDAT2 cache tripping all 3 retries would falsely
    trigger that alert for data that isn't actually at risk. Fixed by
    adding an `emergency_copy: bool = True` opt-out to atomic_write_text
    (and the shared _atomic_write_payload core), with hurricane_climatology.
    py passing emergency_copy=False. AtomicWriteError still raises on
    total failure either way -- only the recovery-copy attempt is skipped.
  - MEDIUM: the "two racing writers never produce a torn file" test was
    structurally unable to fail. Its 5000-char payloads fit inside a
    single buffered write() syscall regardless of atomicity, and it only
    checked file content AFTER both writers had already joined, never
    sampling DURING the race window. Rewritten with multi-megabyte payloads
    (matching real HURDAT2 cache sizes) and a reader thread polling
    continuously while writers race -- moved to test_safe_io.py since the
    original never actually exercised hurricane_climatology.py's own code
    (it built its own cache_path and called safe_io.atomic_write_text
    directly, making its DATA_DIR monkeypatch dead code).
  - LOW: read/write encoding asymmetry -- atomic_write_text hard-codes
    utf-8, but hurricane_climatology.py's 2 cache.read_text() call sites
    were still locale-default (cp1252 on this box). Fixed both to pass
    encoding="utf-8" explicitly.
  - LOW: the renamed shared-helper log messages lost the calling public
    function's name AND broke a documented operator grep pattern
    (backlog.txt's own FORECAST_SIGMA.JSON ATOMIC WRITE CONTENTION entry
    documents `atomic_write_json attempt.*failed` as the exact recurrence-
    check grep). Fixed by threading a `caller_name` parameter through
    _atomic_write_payload so JSON callers keep the byte-identical original
    message and text callers get an accurate "atomic_write_text attempt..."
    instead.
  - LOW: _atomic_write_payload's own docstring wrongly said `path` was
    "assumed to already exist" and "resolved" -- neither true (it's the
    write target, not resolved until the emergency-candidate comparison
    later). Reworded.
  - LOW (2 narrative-accuracy issues): this note's own "safe_io.py had
    exactly 2 public functions" undercounted (4 exist total; only 2 are
    WRITE-shaped, which was the actual claim) -- corrected above. The new
    test class's docstring claimed hurricane_climatology was "the only
    raw-text cache in this codebase" skipping safe_io -- false:
    climate_indices.py's PDO/PNA cache (feeds apply_pdo_pna_correction(),
    called live from weather_markets.py's analyze_trade) and backtest.py's
    own cache both also write via plain write_text(). Re-scoped the
    docstring's wording; filed as a separate follow-up entry rather than
    fixed here (different module, genuinely out of this entry's own
    scope) -- see "climate_indices.py's PDO/PNA CACHE AND backtest.py's
    OWN CACHE ALSO SKIP safe_io" below.

  While re-verifying the rewritten concurrent-writers test's own
  discriminating power (per this project's mutation-testing discipline --
  temporarily swap in a deliberately non-atomic write, confirm the test
  actually catches it), self-caught TWO further issues before they ever
  reached review:

  - A first version of the harness (tight-loop reader, no sleep, isolating
    nothing) only caught a deliberately non-atomic write 1 of 3 local runs
    -- too unreliable to ship. A stronger version (multi-MB payloads, 8
    reader threads, no sleep) caught it reliably (10/10) -- but a bare run
    of this harness as a standalone script (not yet wired through pytest's
    tmp_path/monkeypatch) left a real 5MB test-payload file in THIS
    repo's actual data/.emergency/ directory (project_root() wasn't
    mocked). Found and deleted immediately; the shipped test always
    monkeypatches safe_io.project_root to tmp_path.
  - The same 8-reader-thread harness, run against the REAL (correct)
    atomic_write_text, surfaced a genuine, 100%-reproducible NEW bug, not
    an artifact of the test: on Windows, os.replace() can fail with
    PermissionError (WinError 5 "Access is denied") whenever another
    thread has the target file open for reading, even briefly -- a
    transient-contention failure unrelated to a real disk-full/permissions
    problem (POSIX rename() has no such restriction). Zero torn reads were
    ever observed (the atomicity guarantee itself held), but the WRITE
    could fail outright under concurrent-read pressure -- exhausting all 3
    retries and firing the emergency-copy path for no real reason. Given
    this project's own routine multi-parallel-worktree-session pattern on
    Windows sharing one physical data/ directory, this is a live risk, not
    a theoretical one. Raised via AskUserQuestion rather than silently
    filing it as yet another follow-up or silently fixing a shared
    primitive with 14 other callers -- user chose fix now. Added
    safe_io._replace_with_retry() (a short, bounded 0.5s retry loop on
    PermissionError specifically, same "retry briefly, don't treat
    transient contention as a hard failure" approach paper.py's own
    msvcrt.locking retry loop already uses for the identical Windows
    file-sharing-contention class), wired into both os.replace() call
    sites (primary write, emergency copy). Re-verified: 5/5 runs, 0 write
    errors, 0 torn reads against the fixed implementation; mutation-tested
    by reverting to bare os.replace(), confirmed the shipped concurrent-
    writers test correctly fails 3/3 runs, then restored.

  Independent opus review round 2 (effort: high) of that state found 9
  more findings (1 MEDIUM-HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 6 LOW). Most significant:
  _replace_with_retry had ZERO platform-independent test coverage -- every
  mocked os.replace elsewhere in the file raised plain OSError, never
  PermissionError, and this repo's CI runs on ubuntu-latest where POSIX
  rename() never raises PermissionError for an open destination regardless
  of whether the retry logic exists at all. Reviewer proved the gap by
  mutation (swallowing a permanent PermissionError and returning silent
  "success" left 97/97 tests passing on Windows). Fixed with 3 new
  platform-independent unit tests exercising _replace_with_retry directly
  via a mocked os.replace: succeeds after N transient PermissionErrors,
  re-raises after exhausting deadline_secs (destination never created),
  and does NOT retry a non-PermissionError OSError (propagates
  immediately, unretried). Also fixed: worst-case latency compounding
  (documented in _replace_with_retry's own docstring; the emergency-copy
  call site now passes a shorter deadline_secs=0.1, since read contention
  on a data/.emergency/ or system-temp destination isn't the expected
  failure mode there -- caps total worst-case latency at ~3.7s instead of
  ~4.5s); a docstring that misattributed the WinError-5 discovery to the
  review process when it was actually self-caught during mutation-testing;
  4 more unprotected bare os.replace() sites elsewhere in the codebase
  (tracker.py x2, weather_markets.py, alerts.py) -- filed as a separate
  follow-up entry rather than fixed here, out of this entry's own scope
  (see "OTHER bare os.replace() CALL SITES OUTSIDE safe_io.py ALSO
  EXPOSED TO THE SAME WINDOWS SHARING-VIOLATION FAILURE MODE" below); the
  concurrent-writers test's own writer thread only caught
  AtomicWriteError, not any exception, which could have silently let one
  writer do nothing and the test still pass -- broadened to catch
  Exception generally; the new emergency-copy test (and, for consistency,
  its pre-existing JSON sibling) didn't isolate project_root() even though
  an explicit fallback_dir should make that path unreachable in practice --
  added the same belt-and-suspenders monkeypatch this session's own
  data/.emergency/ pollution incident argues for; several new/rewritten
  tests read without explicit encoding="utf-8", the exact asymmetry LOW #3
  above fixed in production code -- fixed in the tests too; and this
  note's own test counts were wrong (measured directly via `pytest
  --collect-only`: 61 hurricane_climatology tests, not 62; 39 safe_io
  tests, not 36).

  Final (re-measured, not estimated): 61 hurricane_climatology.py tests +

Priority: Low -- same real Windows PermissionError/WinError 5 failure mode

  behavior; this is the WRITER side of the same underlying OS quirk.

  verify each site's own retry/emergency-copy needs first, since not all 4
  may want the same defaults, e.g. tracker.py's _PINS_PATH/_RETIRED_PATH

  safe_io._replace_with_retry into a narrower public helper

[RESOLVED 2026-07-25] NEAR-SETTLEMENT LOG (near_settlement_log) SILENTLY BROKEN SINCE IT SHIPPED -- WRONG FIELD NAMES ON THE TRADE-RECORD DICT
Priority: was Medium -- a shipped calibration-data feature had been a
  complete no-op since it shipped (2026-06-14), with a "success" log line
  every time it ran and zero rows to show for it.

Problem:
  Found via the same "what's next" live-data check that surfaced this
  session's other candlestick-capture bug: `near_settlement_log` had exactly
  0 rows in the live DB. Checked every daily predictions.db backup from
  2026-06-29 through 2026-07-25 (11 backups) -- all 0. bot.log showed 3
  "near_settlement_log: logged 1 trade(s)" INFO lines (all from the very
  start of the retained log, ~2026-06-30), so the code path WAS running and
  believed it succeeded; the DB simply never got the rows.
  Root cause: cron.py's near-settlement block read
  `_tr.get("forecast_prob")` / `_tr.get("recommended_side")` on `_tr`, which
  is a stored paper-trade record (paper.place_paper_order/get_open_trades)
  -- but those two field names belong to the ANALYSIS dict shape
  (order_executor.py's `analysis.get("forecast_prob")` /
  `analysis.get("recommended_side")`), not the trade-record shape, which
  uses "entry_prob"/"side" instead (confirmed against all 198 real trades in
  paper_trades.json: 198/198 have "side" and "entry_prob", 0 have
  "recommended_side" or "forecast_prob" anywhere in the codebase on a trade
  record). This is the same "confused the analysis-dict boundary with the
  trade-record boundary" bug class backtest.py already hit and fixed on
  2026-07-05 (that fix's own comment documents the exact same field-name
  confusion) -- this cron.py call site was a second, still-broken instance
  nobody had re-checked.
  The `trade_side` column is `TEXT NOT NULL`; `_tr.get("recommended_side")`
  always returned None, so every INSERT violated that constraint --
  reproduced live in a standalone SQLite check. The statement was
  `INSERT OR IGNORE`, and SQLite's IGNORE conflict resolution silently drops
  NOT NULL violations (not just UNIQUE/PK ones) without raising -- so the
  code's own success log fired every cycle while writing nothing, for over a
  month, with zero test coverage on this feature to catch it.

What shipped:
  Fixed the two field names (`entry_prob`/`side`). Extracted the insert loop
  into a new `_log_near_settlement_trades(near, db_path) -> (attempted,
  written)` helper (matching the extraction precedent from this session's
  other fix) so it's directly unit-testable and so the caller can tell a
  real write apart from a silently-dropped one: `cmd_cron` now logs a
  WARNING (not the old blanket INFO) whenever written < attempted, closing
  the exact visibility gap that let this run silently for a month.
  Data is not backfillable -- this is a point-in-time snapshot (the
  migration's own comment already said so) -- so the ~40 days of missing
  snapshots are gone; this only fixes collection going forward.
  6 new tests: 5 unit tests on the extracted helper (correct write with real
  field names; a mutation-style regression reproducing the exact original
  silent-failure shape -- a trade dict using "recommended_side"/
  "forecast_prob" instead of "side"/"entry_prob" -- asserting written=0,
  attempted=1, not an exception; dedup via the existing unique index;
  multiple trades all written; days_out defaulting to 0 for pre-days_out
  trade records); 1 new end-to-end test through the real cmd_cron path
  (places a real open paper trade via paper.place_paper_order closing
  within the 0-2h window, runs cmd_cron, asserts the real row lands with
  correct ticker/our_model_prob/trade_side values). Full scoped regression
  (test_near_settlement_log.py + test_cron_integration.py) -- 26 passed.
  ruff + mypy clean. No opus review for this one -- small, single-cause,
  two-field-name fix plus a rowcount hardening, not a multi-subsystem change.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-25] CANDLESTICK CAPTURE (price_history) SILENTLY BROKEN SINCE IT SHIPPED -- market.get("series_ticker") READS A FIELD THAT NEVER EXISTED ON THE REAL API
Priority: was High -- a shipped, believed-working data-collection feature had
  been a complete no-op since 2026-07-12 (13+ days), with zero trace in logs.

Problem:
  Found while checking on the deferred candlestick-analysis entries (backlog's
  own HISTORICAL MARKET-PRICE CAPTURE / MARKET_LIFECYCLE_V2 "check
  `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM price_history`" notes) as part of a routine "what's
  next" status check. Live query: `price_history` had exactly 0 rows across
  0 tickers, while its sibling `trade_history` (same trigger, same
  sync_outcomes() call, wired the identical "fires once per market on
  settlement, isolated try/except" way, shipped one week later on
  2026-07-19) had 23,218 real rows across 13 tickers. That asymmetry, on two
  structurally-identical backfills, was the tell.
  Root cause, confirmed via a live `client.get_market()` call against a real
  settled ticker: the response has NO `series_ticker` field at all -- the
  real key set is `event_ticker`/`ticker`/`open_time`/`close_time`/etc.,
  never `series_ticker`. `sync_outcomes()`'s candlestick-backfill block reads
  `market.get("series_ticker")` and skips the fetch entirely (silently, no
  exception, hence no warning log either) whenever it's falsy -- which was
  always. Confirmed via `bot.log`: zero candlestick-related lines in the
  bot's full retained history, not even the failure-path warning the block's
  own try/except would have logged had `get_candlesticks()` ever actually
  been reached and errored. The sibling trade-history backfill never needed
  `series_ticker` at all (`get_trades(ticker, ...)` -- no series param),
  which is exactly why it worked from day one while candlestick capture
  never worked at all.
  The existing test suite never caught this because its mock `market` dict
  included a fabricated `"series_ticker": "KXHIGHNY"` key that doesn't exist
  on any real response -- the same "synthetic fixture proves the math, not
  real API shape" bug class already documented twice in this file (the
  `is_stale`/`gated_edge`/`_liquidity_edge_scale` volume_fp string bug, and
  `fit_market_implied_distribution`'s identical volume_fp gap) -- now a third
  confirmed instance.
  A real derivation for the missing value already existed in this codebase,
  unnoticed by this feature: `consistency.py`'s `_group_markets()` already
  falls back to `ticker.split("-")[0]` when `series_ticker` is absent (with
  its own "Derive from ticker prefix" comment) -- confirmed live this is
  exactly a market's real series ticker (e.g. `KXHIGHDEN-26JUL09-T91` ->
  `KXHIGHDEN`, a real member of `KNOWN_WEATHER_SERIES`).

What shipped:
  1. `tracker.py`'s `sync_outcomes()` candlestick block now reads
     `market.get("series_ticker") or ticker.split("-")[0]`, mirroring
     `consistency.py`'s own established fallback for the identical gap
     (kept `market.get("series_ticker")` as the first-preference source, in
     case a future/different API response ever does carry a real value).
  2. New `tracker.backfill_price_history(client) -> int`, mirroring
     `backfill_emos_data()`'s shape: `sync_outcomes()` only ever backfills a
     ticker's candlesticks the FIRST time it settles (an existing `outcomes`
     row means it's never revisited), so the code fix alone could not
     recover the 241 tickers that already settled under the broken guard --
     this is the one-off recovery pass, reusing the exact same
     `get_market()`/`get_candlesticks()`/`log_price_candles()` sequence.
     Safe to re-run (already-filled tickers, keyed by a real price_history
     row existing, are skipped by the query) -- no `--force` flag needed,
     unlike `backfill_emos_data`, since a market's OHLC history never
     changes once the market has closed.
  3. New `py main.py backfill-price-history` CLI command + README entry.
  Ran live against the real production DB after shipping: 241/241 settled
  tickers backfilled cleanly (9,105 real candle rows recovered), a second
  run confirmed idempotent (0 backfilled). This also fixes candlestick
  capture going forward -- confirmed via a mutation test on the fallback
  expression itself (reverted to the bare `market.get("series_ticker")`,
  confirmed the exact predicted `get_candlesticks` never-called symptom,
  restored) rather than only trusting the retroactive backfill's success.
  14 new/updated tests (first pass, before the independent review below):
  2 existing sync_outcomes candlestick tests (which had been the exact
  tests masking this bug) fixed to use a real API-shaped mock market dict
  (no fabricated `series_ticker` key), 1 new test proving a real
  `series_ticker` field (if one is ever actually present) still wins over
  the fallback, 1 renamed/narrowed test isolating the real skip condition
  (missing `open_time`, not missing `series_ticker`) from the now-fixed
  one; 8 new tests for `backfill_price_history` itself (fills missing
  rows, skips already-filled/disputed tickers, uses the real series_ticker
  when present, skips a ticker with no open_time, a single ticker's
  `get_market`/`get_candlesticks` failure doesn't abort the whole pass);
  2 for the CLI command.

  Independent Agent(opus, effort=high) review before push independently
  re-verified the live production data 6 ways (row/ticker counts,

[RESOLVED 2026-07-30] FORECAST_SIGMA.JSON ATOMIC WRITE CONTENTION -- INTERMITTENT, SELF-RECOVERING, WATCHING
Priority: was Low (no data loss observed, flagged to watch for recurrence).
  Re-verified 2026-07-30 during a backlog-wide audit: this was NOT a single
  occurrence -- it recurred on 2026-07-19 (before this entry was even
  written), -07-25 (the occurrence documented below), -07-27, and again
  2026-07-30 (today), all self-recovering via the same emergency-copy
  fallback. A real, code-level root cause was found and fixed -- see
  RESOLVED note below.

  failed all 3 retry attempts writing data/forecast_sigma.json on 3

RESOLVED 2026-07-30: found via a backlog-wide audit that this recurred 4x
  (07-19, -25, -27, -30), not once -- the OneDrive-sync theory above was
  never confirmed and turned out to be the wrong culprit. Real cause: a
  thread race, not an external process. climatology.py's `load_all_sigmas()`
  (called via weather_markets._load_dynamic_sigma()) checked its module-
  global `_sigma_mem_cache`/on-disk cache with no lock -- cron.py's
  `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8)` scan lets multiple worker threads call
  it concurrently, and on a cold cache (process start, or the monthly
  refresh boundary), every thread that saw the cache empty independently
  recomputed the full per-city sigma table and raced to
  `safe_io.atomic_write_json()` the same forecast_sigma.json at nearly the
  same instant -- colliding on the rename step (WinError 32/5/2 matches
  exactly). Confirmed by checking whether cron.py runs a second concurrent
  process (it doesn't -- ruled out in the original Problem section) versus
  concurrent threads within the SAME process (not previously considered);
  the 07-30 occurrence's tmp filename already included a PID suffix
  (`.forecast_sigma.json_<pid>_0.tmp`) yet the contention still recurred,
  which rules out cross-process collision and points at same-process
  threads racing instead.
  Fix: added `_sigma_lock = threading.Lock()` (climatology.py) wrapping
  `load_all_sigmas()`'s entire check-compute-write body, matching
  climate_indices.py's `_indices_lock` convention for the identical
  check-then-fetch-then-cache shape. Concurrent callers now serialize on the
  lock; the first one computes+writes, the rest see the now-populated
  `_sigma_mem_cache` on their turn and return immediately without
  recomputing or re-writing.
  New test (tests/test_climatology.py::TestLoadAllSigmasBehavior::
  test_concurrent_cold_cache_calls_compute_only_once): 8 threads hit a cold
  cache simultaneously (lined up on a `threading.Barrier`) against a
  `compute_sigma_from_climate` slowed with `time.sleep(0.05)` to widen the
  race window; asserts exactly 2 compute calls happen (one city's max+min,
  computed once) instead of up to 16, that every thread gets the real
  computed result (not a partial one from a losing racer), and that the
  on-disk file is valid/correct. Mutation-tested by replacing `with
  _sigma_lock:` with `if True:` (no-op) -- the test failed by literally
  reproducing the live symptom (WinError 32/5/2 on the rename step, the
  emergency-copy fallback also failing under the heavier concurrent load the
  test applies), then the lock was restored and all 14 tests in the file
  pass again. Full climatology-adjacent regression sweep (test_climatology.py,
  test_gaussian_prob.py, test_city_registry_manifest.py) — 58 passed; ruff +
  ruff format + mypy clean on climatology.py.
  Did not touch weather_markets.py's own `_dynamic_sigma` global/
  `_load_dynamic_sigma()` -- its own check-then-set has the same unlocked
  shape, but it never itself calls atomic_write_json (that only happens
  inside climatology.load_all_sigmas(), now locked), and once the
  climatology-level lock serializes callers there, redundant callers into
  `_load_dynamic_sigma()` just make a few extra cheap, lock-protected calls
  into an already-memoized function -- no data-corruption risk, so left
  as-is rather than adding a second lock with no corresponding bug.

  Independent opus review (effort=high) of this fix found the ACTUAL general
  root cause was one level deeper than the `_sigma_lock` fix above addresses:
  `safe_io.atomic_write_json()`'s temp-file name was keyed by PID+attempt
  ONLY (`.{name}_{pid}_{attempt}.tmp`), not by thread -- so two THREADS in
  the same process (not two processes, which the function's own comment
  claimed was the only real scenario) shared one temp file and could
  legitimately race on it. This is a defect in a shared utility with 20+
  callers, not specific to the sigma cache: `climatology.fetch_historical()`
  (climatology.py:97, writes `climate_{city}.json`) is reached from the same
  cron.py thread pool via a completely different, UNLOCKED call path
  (`climatological_prob` -> `_climatological_prob_inner`) and was not
  protected by the new `_sigma_lock` at all -- confirmed live: `cron.py`
  never calls `preload_all()` (only `main.py`'s `cmd_scan`/`cmd_top`/
  `cmd_setup` do), so on the cron path every per-city climate cache is
  ALSO populated lazily from inside the thread pool, the same shape that
  caused the sigma race. The review further found the `_sigma_lock` fix
  slightly WIDENS this specific overlap (holding the lock across a serial
  ~21-city fetch loop lengthens the window an unlocked worker doing
  `climatological_prob` for the same city can collide with it).
  Real fix (safe_io.py): added `threading.get_ident()` to BOTH temp-file
  name constructions (the primary write at safe_io.py:~88 and the emergency-
  copy fallback at safe_io.py:~165) so concurrent threads within one process
  never share a temp file, matching the same protection two concurrent
  PROCESSES already had. Comment updated (the old one asserted "two
  processes... is the exact scenario," which was an incomplete premise --
  same-process threads are an equally real scenario this fix now also
  covers).
  New test (tests/test_safe_io.py::
  test_atomic_write_concurrent_threads_same_target_no_collision): 8 threads
  lined up on a `threading.Barrier` all call `atomic_write_json()` against
  the SAME target path, with `os.fsync` slowed 20ms to widen the race
  window; asserts every thread's call succeeds (default retries=3 -- the
  existing retry+backoff is what absorbs a residual, harder-to-hit
  same-DESTINATION `os.replace()` collision distinct from the shared-temp-
  file bug, confirmed by first trying `retries=1` and observing it correctly
  fail with the exact live WinError 5 symptom on a second, different race:
  two threads' `os.replace()` calls to the identical destination, now with
  distinct temp sources, still contending on Windows without the retry
  loop's backoff -- using the real default retries reflects actual call-site
  behavior rather than testing a synthetic zero-retry configuration no real
  caller uses), that the final file is valid, uncorrupted JSON from exactly
  one whole writer, and that no leftover temp files remain. Mutation-tested
  by reverting the primary temp-path change -- the test failed by literally
  reproducing the live WinError 32/5 symptom, then the fix was restored and
  all 21 tests in the file pass again.
  Regression sweep: test_safe_io.py, test_backtest.py,
  test_cleanup_data_dir.py, test_climatology.py, test_cron_group_c.py,
  test_infrastructure.py, test_phase2_batch_m.py (every test file touching
  safe_io/atomic_write_json or climatology) -- 134 passed; ruff + ruff
  format + mypy clean on safe_io.py and climatology.py.
  The `_sigma_lock` fix above is kept (not reverted) -- it still eliminates
  redundant recompute+write entirely for the sigma cache specifically
  (rather than merely making concurrent writes non-colliding), which is
  strictly better for that one call site even with the deeper fix in place.
  Residual, deliberately NOT fixed in this pass (separate, lower-severity,
  cross-process case -- see climatology.py's `load_all_sigmas()` docstring,
  updated to state this explicitly): web_app.py's Flask process (threaded,
  separate PID from cron.py) can still read `forecast_sigma.json` mid-rename
  by a concurrent cron.py write; `_sigma_lock` is process-local and cannot
  cover this, though it's the same class of collision `safe_io`'s retry/
  backoff already absorbs for other cross-process cases.
  Also NOT fixed in this pass (found via the same review, filed as its own
  consideration rather than expanded into this fix): `climatology.
  fetch_historical()`'s per-city `climate_{city}.json` writes, reached via
  the unlocked `climatological_prob` path from the same thread pool, have
  no equivalent to `_sigma_lock` -- the safe_io.py fix above protects them
  from the temp-file-collision failure mode, but not from the (much rarer)
  same-destination-replace race the retry loop absorbs. Worth a dedicated
  lock if this ever shows up in bot.log the way the sigma cache did.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-25] TEST SUITE: date.today() VS PRODUCTION-TIMEZONE MISMATCH -- FULL AUDIT
Priority: was Low-Medium -- not a live-trading bug (test-only), but was a real
  correctness gap in test coverage: an affected test could silently pass or
  fail depending purely on the sandbox's local timezone/wall-clock moment
  when it happened to run, independent of any real code change.

Problem:
  Found 2026-07-24/25 while investigating 4 reported test failures (see
  [RESOLVED 2026-07-25] entry below for the fixed instances). Root cause:
  weather_markets.py computes "today"/days_out from a real, timezone-aware
  clock at multiple sites -- datetime.now(UTC).date() (temperature/
  forecasting paths, e.g. weather_markets.py's METAR-locked branch and
  days_out gates) or datetime.now(ZoneInfo(city_tz)).date() (precip path,
  _analyze_precip_trade). Several tests instead build their fixture dates
  via plain date.today() + timedelta(...), which resolves in the TEST
  RUNNER's system-local timezone -- a different, uncontrolled value. When
  the sandbox's local timezone diverges from whichever timezone the
  exercised code path actually uses (true for a meaningful fraction of
  every real day), the test's date and production's internally-computed
  date disagree by one calendar day, shifting days_out and silently
  changing blend weights, dampening windows, or gate outcomes -- occasionally
  enough to flip an assertion or a None-return gate, as it did for the 3
  fixed instances.
  A repo-wide grep (`grep -rl "date\.today() + timedelta" tests/*.py`) found
  this exact pattern in 13 files: conftest.py, test_data_freshness.py,
  test_edge_version.py, test_forecasting.py, test_gaussian_prob.py,
  test_integration.py, test_ml_bias.py, test_p9_p10.py, test_paper.py,
  test_price_and_size.py, test_signal_quality.py, test_tracker.py,
  test_weather_markets.py. Only the 3 specific call sites that were
  ACTUALLY observed failing (one in test_price_and_size.py, one in
  test_forecasting.py -- see the RESOLVED entry) were fixed; test_forecasting.py
  and test_price_and_size.py both still have OTHER, unaudited
  date.today()-based fixtures beyond the ones fixed, and none of the other
  9 files were even opened. Not every occurrence is necessarily a live bug
  -- many tests' assertions may be loose/relative enough not to care about a
  ±1-day shift (e.g. TestSnowTradeWiring in test_price_and_size.py uses a
  fully fixed date and was never exposed at all) -- this hasn't been
  triaged file-by-file to separate real exposure from harmless usage.

What the fix looks like:
  Per-file/per-test triage: for each date.today()-based fixture, determine
  (a) which timezone the exercised production code path actually uses for
  its own "today" (grep the target function for datetime.now(...) call
  sites -- this session found at least two different answers, UTC and
  city-local ZoneInfo, don't assume one convention holds everywhere), and
  (b) whether the test's assertions are actually sensitive to a ±1-day
  days_out shift (many aren't). Fix only the ones that are, using the same
  pattern the 3 already-fixed instances established: derive the test's date
  from the SAME timezone-aware "now" the code under test uses, not
  date.today(). A shared test helper (e.g. in conftest.py) for "today in
  timezone X" might be worth extracting once 2-3 more instances are fixed
  this way, rather than hand-rolling the zoneinfo call at each site (per
  backlog.txt's own general aversion to premature abstraction from a single
  data point -- 3 instances already exist, so this may already be past
  that threshold if picked up).

Why not now:
  - Discovered as a byproduct of fixing 4 specific, currently-failing tests,
    not as its own planned session -- auditing 10+ more files for a
    currently-invisible (right now, all suites pass) latent flakiness class
    is a real, multi-hour task, not an adjacent one-line fix.

RESOLVED 2026-07-25: Full audit completed, scope larger than originally
  estimated. The 13-file estimate came from a narrow grep pattern
  (`date\.today() + timedelta`, exact spacing); a broader sweep for any
  `date.today()`/`datetime.date.today()`/aliased-import form found ~90
  real call sites across ~25 files (also test_dedup.py, test_hourly_markets.py,
  test_p9_p10.py, test_trading.py, test_walk_forward.py,

  test_weather_markets.py (test_analyze_trade_returns_adjusted_edge_key --

[RESOLVED 2026-07-25] TestMetarLockInLowMarketAsymmetry -- UTC-VS-CITY-LOCAL-TIMEZONE MISMATCH, A DIFFERENT SHAPE THAN THE date.today() ENTRY ABOVE
Priority: was Low-Medium -- test-only, but was currently live and reproducible
  for part of every real day (not hypothetical, not a sandbox-only artifact).

Problem:
  Found 2026-07-25 while re-verifying backlog state for the user (not part
  of a planned session) -- both tests in
  tests/test_weather_markets.py::TestMetarLockInLowMarketAsymmetry
  (test_low_market_above_already_below_margin_is_locked,
  test_low_market_below_already_below_margin_is_locked) currently FAIL,
  live, right now. Root cause is NOT the date.today()-vs-timezone entry
  above's pattern (that one's repo-wide grep for `date\.today() + timedelta`
  would not catch this -- this test doesn't use date.today() at all).
  The test's `_call()` helper (test_weather_markets.py:3985) builds
  target_date via `datetime.now(UTC).date()`. The production function it
  exercises, weather_markets.py's `_metar_lock_in` (line 6941), computes
  its own "is this actually today" gate via
  `datetime.now(ZoneInfo(_city_tz_str)).date()` -- city-local time (NYC ->
  America/New_York), NOT UTC (weather_markets.py:6972, guard at line 6979:
  `if not (_metar_sta and target_date == _local_today): return False, 0.0,
  {}`). UTC's calendar date and US-Eastern's calendar date genuinely
  disagree for ~4 hours every day (20:00 EDT through local midnight, since
  UTC has already rolled to the next day) -- confirmed live 2026-07-25
  00:21 UTC (date 2026-07-25) vs. 20:21 EDT same instant (date 2026-07-24).
  During that window, target_date != _local_today, the guard fires, and
  the function returns locked=False regardless of the test's actual
  intent -- exactly the observed `assert False is True` failures.
  This is real, time-of-day-flaky (not permanently broken -- it passes
  outside the ~4h window), and would recur identically on every future run
  that happens to land in that window, on any machine, regardless of the
  machine's own local timezone (since neither side of the comparison uses
  system-local time -- this is a UTC-vs-city-local mismatch, a third
  timezone-convention-mismatch shape distinct from both the date.today()
  entry above and the "3 timezone-flaky tests" already fixed in the
  RESOLVED entry below).

What the fix looks like:
  Same principle as the date.today() entry above (derive the test's date
  from the SAME timezone convention the exercised code path actually
  uses), applied here specifically: build `target_date` in `_call()` via
  `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("America/New_York")).date()` (matching NYC, the
  hardcoded city in this test class) instead of `datetime.now(UTC).date()`.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-24] OPEN-METEO ENSEMBLE-API FREE TIER WAS RATE-LIMITING batch_prewarm_ensemble
Priority: was Medium -- not blocking trade placement (TRADING_PAUSED covers
  that), but degraded signal quality on every cron run that tripped: GEM/UKMO
  accuracy tracking never got data, and -- the worse part -- precip (icon/
  gfs/ecmwf_ifs025, feeds the live blend) silently lost every cycle too,
  since it was fetched AFTER GEM/UKMO and requires all 3 of its models to
  succeed or it writes nothing.

Problem:
  Root cause confirmed empirically 2026-07-24 (not just inferred from prior
  context): replayed cron's exact 20-city call pattern against the live
  `ensemble-api.open-meteo.com` endpoint and reproduced the identical 429
  ("Minutely API request limit exceeded") after ~7-8 sequential 20-city
  calls. This is an undocumented, strict rolling-~60s per-IP request budget
  on the free/anonymous ensemble endpoint -- far tighter than Open-Meteo's
  documented 600 calls/min (that figure applies to the paid/API-key
  customer endpoint, not this shared one). `batch_prewarm_ensemble()` was
  making 13 sequential calls/cycle (10 temp + 3 precip), always exceeding
  the ~7-8 budget, tripping `open_meteo_ensemble` every run.
  Tested and ruled out combining multiple models into fewer HTTP requests
  as a fix -- the throttle scales with total requested locations x models
  (data volume), not literal request count, so packaging doesn't help
  (confirmed: 3 combined-model requests still hit the same wall as 8
  single-model ones). Also ruled out splitting the 20-city batch into
  smaller location chunks -- the budget is a fixed ~140 city-units/minute
  regardless of chunk size (confirmed via a 5/10/15/20-city sweep, product
  constant across all four).
  Separately, the same 2026-07-23 evidence that first surfaced this also
  showed `open_meteo_seasonal` (a different endpoint/circuit breaker, in
  acis_precip.py, feeding rain-market ACIS tilt) tripping the same day --
  NOT covered by this fix, split out to its own entry below since it's a
  separate code path never investigated here.

What shipped:
  `batch_prewarm_ensemble()` (weather_markets.py) now fetches in two tiers:
  blend-critical models + precip (9 calls, feed the live trading blend) go
  first; then a real 65s pause (`_ENSEMBLE_TRACKING_TIER_DELAY_SECS`) lets
  Open-Meteo's rate window reset before GEM/UKMO (tracking-only, 4 calls)
  go last. No request-combining, no new response-parsing logic -- same
  single-model-per-request code as before, just reordered with a pause
  inserted, so a rate-limit trip now only ever costs a delayed accuracy
  sample, never live-trading data. Also protects precip, which was
  previously guaranteed to lose every cycle regardless of tier ordering
  since it ran after GEM/UKMO.
  Verified live: `python main.py cron` completed all 10/10 ensemble
  model/var calls with zero 429s and zero circuit-breaker trips.
  Shipped in `6a3809a`.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-24 -- reproduced/ruled out empirically; the entry's own
  anticipated "may need no fix at all" outcome, plus a proactive caching
  hygiene fix shipped alongside it]
  OPEN-METEO SEASONAL API MAY ALSO BE RATE-LIMITING -- UNCONFIRMED, UNADDRESSED
Priority: Low -- only affects rain-market directional tilt on a trip
  (falls back to ACIS-only, a real quality loss but not a trading-safety
  issue), and hasn't been reproduced with the same rigor as the now-fixed
  ensemble-api case.

Problem:
  The 2026-07-23 ~17:29 UTC cron run that first surfaced the ensemble-api
  rate-limiting also tripped `open_meteo_seasonal` (5 straight 429s
  fetching Houston/Miami/Dallas monthly precip, 600s cooldown) around the
  same time. This is a SEPARATE circuit breaker hitting a SEPARATE
  endpoint (`seasonal-api.open-meteo.com`, acis_precip.py's `_om_seasonal_cb`,
  failure_threshold=5) from `open_meteo_ensemble` -- plausibly the same
  class of undocumented free-tier throttling confirmed for the ensemble
  endpoint, but this has NOT been independently reproduced or measured.
  The ensemble-api fix (tiered fetch + a real pause) does not automatically
  carry over: the seasonal endpoint's request volume/pattern and its actual
  rate budget (if any) are unconfirmed.

What it would look like:
  Same empirical approach used for the ensemble-api fix: reproduce the 429
  live by replaying acis_precip.py's actual seasonal-API call pattern,
  determine the real rate budget for that endpoint specifically, then
  design a fix sized to what's actually needed (could be as simple as a
  short delay if seasonal calls are infrequent enough, or may need no
  change at all if this doesn't reproduce under current call volume).

RESEARCH 2026-07-24 (mechanism confirmed, not yet applied to this specific
  endpoint): found the actual rate-limiting mechanism behind the now-fixed
  ensemble-api case, straight from Open-Meteo's maintainer (Patrick
  Zippenfenig, github.com/open-meteo/open-meteo issue #439, and confirmed
  independently on the pricing page's own "How is one API call defined?"
  section): free-tier limits are 600 calls/min, 5,000/hr, 10,000/day, but
  a "call" is NOT one HTTP request -- it's weighted as
  (ensemble members x variables / 10) PER LOCATION, summed across every
  location in a batched request. This is exactly why combining models
  into fewer HTTP requests didn't help the ensemble-api fix -- the throttle
  scales with data volume, not request count. Live-verified ensemble member
  counts (2026-07-24, via a direct ensemble-api query) for this bot's 5
  models: icon_seamless=40, gfs_seamless=31, ecmwf_aifs025_ensemble=51,
  gem_global=21, ukmo_global_ensemble_20km=18, across this bot's 20 cities.
  Working the same formula for acis_precip.py's seasonal-API calls (monthly
  precip, ECMWF SEAS5 ensemble) would follow the identical method -- just
  needs that endpoint's own member count and call pattern plugged in,
  which this pass didn't do (out of scope -- was researching the ensemble-
  api mechanism for a different, now-resolved question, not this entry).
  Paid tiers remove the per-minute/hour/day ceiling entirely (dedicated
  instance, monthly call budget only) but likely still apply the same
  weighted-call counting toward that budget -- unconfirmed whether paid
  tier changes anything for THIS specific endpoint's behavior, since the
  free-tier ensemble-api problem was fully resolved via the code-level
  tiered-fetch fix instead of a purchase. No purchase currently justified
  for this entry either -- same reasoning, try the free reproduce-and-fix
  approach first.

When to revisit:
  - If `open_meteo_seasonal` circuit-breaker trips recur in cron output, or
    as part of a broader Open-Meteo rate-limit pass if one is scheduled
    later for other reasons. When picked up, start from the weighted-call
    formula above rather than re-deriving it from scratch.

  acis_precip.fetch_seasonal_precip_mean_mm had ZERO caching before this --

[RESOLVED 2026-07-23] SYNTHETIC TEST DATA (PROB*/BAD* OUTCOME ROWS) CORRUPTED THE LIVE P10.3 BRIER ALERT FOR 4+ DAYS
Priority: was High -- silently corrupted a live model-quality safety signal
  (P10.3 Brier alert) undetected since 2026-07-19; same root-cause class as
  the already-resolved 2026-07-21 KXBADDATE3 incident (see MYSTERY REVERT-
  adjacent entry / project memory), second occurrence of the same failure
  pattern.

Problem:
  Found while reviewing routine `python main.py cron` output: the P10.3
  Brier alert fired "Brier score has exceeded 0.22 for two consecutive
  weeks (0.2687, 0.4525)" on back-to-back cron runs two days apart with
  byte-identical figures despite new settlements happening in between --
  the tell that something was frozen/fake, not a live-recomputed signal
  (`get_brier_over_time()` is in fact a live, uncached SQL query every
  call, so "frozen" pointed at contaminated inputs, not stale caching).
  Root cause: 36 synthetic rows (`PROB0`-`PROB17`, `BAD0`-`BAD17`, all
  `city=None`, `method='ensemble'`) sitting in `predictions.db`'s
  `predictions`/`outcomes` tables, all inserted in a single batch at the
  exact same `predicted_at` timestamp (2026-07-19 21:04:58), with
  fabricated `settled_at` values in Jan/Feb 2026 -- physically before their
  own `predicted_at`, an impossible sequence for a real trade. Almost
  certainly an ad-hoc `python -c` test of the Brier-alert/disputed-row path
  run directly against the live production DB (same failure shape as the
  2026-07-21 KXBADDATE3 incident: `_auto_place_trades()` called ad-hoc
  against real DB paths instead of pytest's auto-sandboxed temp DB), never
  cleaned up. The fabricated pair (0.95-prob "PROB" rows all settling YES,
  0.05-prob "BAD" rows also all settling YES) averages to exactly 0.4525 --
  matching the alert's reported figure to 4 decimal places. Real W27
  (0.2687, 3 genuine multi-day predictions) was legitimate; W28 had ZERO
  real multi-day settlements until this was found -- the alert's "second
  consecutive bad week" was 100% synthetic.
  This wasn't limited to the alert: `brier_score_by_method()` (drives the
  "lifetime Brier 0.3200, ensemble pin not auto-renewing" warning logged on
  every single cron run) joins the same `multiday_predictions JOIN
  outcomes_valid` shape, filtered to `method='ensemble'` -- exactly what
  all 36 fake rows were tagged as. A narrower fix scoped only to the alert
  function would have left the strategy-retirement/pin-expiry path (a
  real live-trading-relevant decision) still corrupted.

What shipped:
  Verified full scope via 3 independent sweeps before touching anything:
  (1) `settled_at < predicted_at` across the whole DB (not just multi-day)
  -- found exactly these 36 rows, nothing else; (2) non-`KX`-prefixed
  ticker scan across `predictions`/`multiday_predictions`/`outcomes_valid`
  -- same 36, no other city affected; (3) batch-identical-`predicted_at`
  scan (>5 rows sharing one exact timestamp) across all cities -- the only
  match besides legitimate same-cron-cycle multi-city batches (6-7 rows,
  multiple real distinct cities each) was this one 36-row, single-city=None
  batch. Confirmed isolated to one incident, no other city/table affected.
  Used the existing `tracker.mark_outcome_disputed()` function (built
  2026-07-18, see DISPUTED-ROW EXCLUSION PREDICATE entry below) instead of
  deleting rows or writing a new bespoke filter -- one call per ticker sets
  `disputed=1`, which every one of the 43 `outcomes_valid`-joined consumers
  (`get_brier_over_time`, `brier_score_by_method`,
  `brier_score_by_method_rolling`, `brier_skill_score`, calibration
  training, etc.) already excludes automatically, with zero new code.
  Non-destructive and reversible -- rows remain as a forensic record,
  simply excluded from scoring. Verified the fix: W28 (100% synthetic)
  disappeared entirely from `get_brier_over_time()`'s output; `ensemble`
  method Brier dropped from the contaminated 0.3200 lifetime figure to a
  real 0.2681. Data-only fix -- no code changed, no commit.
  Note: W26/W27's real Brier (0.2678/0.2687) are both still above the 0.22
  threshold on genuine data, so the P10.3 alert may legitimately fire again
  next run -- that would be a real signal worth investigating on its own
  merits, not more contamination.

Why not now (resolved):
  - The specific contamination found is fully cleaned up. The general risk
    class -- ad-hoc debugging sessions writing directly to production DB
    files instead of an isolated/temp DB -- is NOT fixed by this entry and
    remains open; see note below.

When to revisit:
  - If a similar contamination is found a third time, especially one using
    a valid-looking ticker AND a plausible (non-impossible) settled_at --
    the impossible-timestamp signature that caught both this incident and
    KXBADDATE3 would NOT catch a more careful fabrication. Worth
    considering a lighter-weight guard (e.g. a `test_data` marker column,
    or a habit of always pointing ad-hoc investigative scripts at a copied
    DB) before a third occurrence.

     shape/columns as the raw table, `SELECT *`).
  2. Widen `test_disputed_row_guard.py` from a single hardcoded
     `_TRACKER_PY` path to scanning every production `.py` file in the
     repo (excluding `tests/`, which have their own legitimate reasons to
     touch raw tables via fixtures) -- this is the actual root-cause fix:
     it makes sure a *future* new raw-outcomes query anywhere in the
     codebase gets caught automatically by CI, instead of requiring
     another manual repo-wide grep like the one that found this.
  3. Add paper.py's settled_temp_f lookup to the (now repo-wide) allowlist
     with its documented reason, matching get_outcome_for_ticker's
     existing entry.
  4. Mutation-test the widened guard (temporarily add a fake new
     unallowlisted raw-outcomes query in a non-tracker.py file, confirm
     the guard fails, revert) -- same methodology the original guard used
     on itself.

RESOLVED 2026-07-23, pushed `5f94910`: implemented as scoped above, with one
  correction and two hardening fixes found by an opus review before commit.
  Fixed all 9 sites to join `outcomes_valid` (backtest.py, calibration.py x2,
  ml_bias.py x4, main.py x2, web_app.py) -- pure JOIN-target swaps, `SELECT
  *`-equivalent view, no other query-shape changes needed. Widened

  etc., not a path allowlist, so a future new production subdirectory is
  covered automatically).
  Review correction: `paper.py`'s `_score_ensemble_members` was going to be
  allowlisted (settled_temp_f lookup for the ticker just settled) using the
  same reasoning as `sync_outcomes` ("can't be disputed before it has a
  settlement") -- the reviewer traced the real call graph and found this
  doesn't hold: `audit_settlement()` sets `settled_temp_f` and `disputed` in
  the *same pass* on a Kalshi-vs-archive mismatch, and `_score_ensemble_members`
  requires `settled_temp_f` non-NULL before it runs -- so it only ever
  executes after a row could already be disputed, and it feeds live
  `_dynamic_model_weights()`. Fixed as a 10th real site (joins
  `outcomes_valid`) instead of allowlisted.
  Review-caught guard hardening (both latent, no live exploit, but the exact
  "one caller gets missed" shape this guard exists to prevent, just
  relocated): (1) the original line-scan used a column-0 `^def` regex for
  function attribution, invisible to methods and nested functions -- a
  second unsafe query added inside an already-allowlisted function's body
  would have passed silently; fixed with a real `ast.FunctionDef`/
  `AsyncFunctionDef` walk producing a true innermost qualified name
  (`Outer.inner`, `Class.method`). (2) the scan matched line-by-line, so a
  `JOIN`/table-name split across two lines could never match even though
  the regex pattern itself is newline-tolerant (`\s` matches `\n`); fixed by
  scanning each file's full text in one pass instead of splitting into
  lines first. Both hardening fixes mutation-tested (injected a nested-
  function violation and a multi-line-split violation in a scratch function
  in backtest.py, confirmed the guard caught each with the correct
  attribution, reverted via `git checkout` after a manual string-replace
  revert attempt silently failed to match).
  Three hand-rolled test fixtures (`test_calibration.py` x2,

Priority: was High -- verify before resuming live trading (~2026-07-30 return), not a

RESOLVED 2026-07-12: Migrated place_order()/cancel_order() to POST/DELETE
  /portfolio/events/orders per the plan below (commit bc7e10c), then a
  second-opinion review found and fixed one real HIGH bug -- a successful
  POST followed by a failing get_order() follow-up could strand a live
  order under status="failed" with no poller ever picking it up again
  (commit 58a4e3b). 156+ tests pass, lint/mypy clean. This item is done;
  kept below for historical context on the migration decisions.

Problem:
  kalshi_client.py's live order-placement and order-cancellation code
  targets endpoints Kalshi is migrating off of. The split is "reads stay,
  writes move," not a wholesale change:
    - GET /portfolio/orders (kalshi_client.py:313, list resting/executed
      orders) and GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id} (kalshi_client.py:423,
      get single order) are UNAFFECTED -- reads stay on this path
      permanently per Kalshi's own docs.
    - POST /portfolio/orders (kalshi_client.py:364, place_order) and
      DELETE /portfolio/orders/{order_id} (kalshi_client.py:427,
      cancel_order) are the legacy WRITE endpoints being deprecated. The
      new V2 write endpoints are POST /portfolio/events/orders and
      DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id} (confirmed via both
      Kalshi's changelog and an independent third-party SDK
      -- github.com/TexasCoding/kalshi-python-sdk -- whose docs describe
      the identical old-path/new-path split).
  This is NOT just a URL rename: Kalshi's changelog describes the new V2
  write endpoints as using "a bid/ask single-book shape with fixed-point
  dollar prices and lightweight responses" -- a different request/response
  shape. The third-party SDK's docs show the new response includes
  order_id, remaining_count, fill_count, reduced_by, ts_ms -- diff this
  against what kalshi_client.py currently parses out of the old response
  before assuming the migration is small.
  Timeline: legacy write rate-limit costs escalated to 10x V2-equivalent by
  2026-06-04; deprecation was announced for "sometime between June 18 and
  June 25, 2026." No changelog entry confirms the deprecation was actually
  enforced/completed -- legacy writes may still work today, just at 10x
  rate-limit cost, with no confirmed grace period remaining. No real order
  has ever been placed by this bot yet (ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE=False), so this
  has not caused a live incident.

What the fix looks like:
  1. Quick check first: hit place_order/cancel_order against DEMO_BASE
     (https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2) and see whether they still
     succeed, return a deprecation error, or already 404/reject.
  2. Migrate kalshi_client.py's place_order (line 364) and cancel_order
     (line 427) to POST/DELETE /portfolio/events/orders[/{order_id}].
     Read Kalshi's live API reference for the exact current request body
     (fixed-point dollar prices, bid/ask single-book shape) and response
     field names before writing the migration -- do not assume the old
     request/response dict shape carries over unchanged.
  3. Leave the two GET /portfolio/orders* call sites (line 313, 423) alone
     -- they are not affected by this migration.
  4. While in there, evaluate the new orderbook_delta WebSocket
     get_snapshot action (see FEATURE CANDIDATES section below) since it's
     adjacent surface area.

Why not now (only reason to defer, not to skip):
  - TRADING_PAUSED=true and ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE=False mean nothing is
    currently broken in production -- but this should be resolved before
    either flag flips, not discovered live when it does.

When to revisit:
  - Before the Belgium trip ends (~2026-07-30) and live trading is
    considered for resumption. This is a hard prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.

Original problem (kept for history):
  Kalshi's "Climate and Weather" category also lists an "Hourly Directional
  [City] Temperature" market family, structurally invisible to this bot:
  check_series_drift() only ever diffs KXHIGH*/KXLOW* prefixed series, so
  this family never surfaces as a gap no matter how much volume it gets.
  Confirmed live 2026-07-08: KXTEMPMIAH, KXTEMPBOSH, KXTEMPLAXH, KXTEMPCHIH,
  KXTEMPAUSH, KXTEMPDCH, KXTEMPNYCH all exist; only KXTEMPNYCH currently has
  open markets (24 of them, e.g. KXTEMPNYCH-26JUL0804-T76.99 -- an hourly
  threshold, not a daily high/low). The other 6 cities are dormant right now.

What the fix looks like:
  This isn't a ticker-list fix -- it needs a per-hour threshold-crossing
  probability model instead of the daily high/low ensemble blend this bot
  runs today. The good news: the same-day nowcasting infra this would lean
  on (live METAR observation override, persistence baseline, HRRR same-day
  fetch -- see analyze_trade()'s days_out==0 path in weather_markets.py, and
  cron.py's "Same-day markets... re-enabled" same-day trading logic) already
  exists and is live for daily markets, not still-deferred as an earlier
  version of this backlog entry assumed. Still needs new work though: the
  existing pipeline reasons about "will today's high/low cross X," not
  "will the temp at hour H cross X" -- the per-hour target and the shorter
  settlement window are a real design difference, not just reused as-is.

  Calibration follows the same precedent already established for same-day
  vs multi-day: ml_bias.train_all_temperature_scaling() fits a dedicated
  'sameday' T from days_out=0 rows only, with apply_temperature_scaling()
  enforcing zero fallback to the global/multi-day T (their probability
  distributions are too different to share a scale -- see commit chain
  c773474 -> 9f5bb40, 2026-06-02/05). An hour-level model needs the same
  treatment: its own training pool and its own T, not folded into either
  the daily same-day pool or the multi-day pool. Don't assume the existing
  'sameday' calibration path could just absorb hourly rows -- it can't
  without the same care taken to keep the pools separate.

Why not now (superseded -- both conditions below have since fired, see
  RESOLVED note above):
  - No existing model for the hour-level target specifically (only daily).
  - Only 1 of 7 cities in this family is currently even active.
  - Worth confirming KXTEMPxxxH volume is durable (not a one-off) before
    investing in an hour-level model.

Problem:
  "Climate and Weather" has 287 series total; this bot only ever looks at
  ~45 of them (KXHIGH*/KXLOW*, 20 tracked cities). Live-checked 2026-07-08:
  16 KXRAIN* city series exist, 2 currently with real open volume
  (KXRAINDENM -- Denver rain, 7 open markets; KXRAINSTPM, 7 open markets);
  ~23 snow series and ~40 hurricane series (path/category/landfall by city)
  exist but were all dormant/closed at check time. Separately, a handful of
  real weather markets (RAINNYC, KXRAINMIA, KXRAINNOSB) live entirely
  outside the "Climate and Weather" category (filed under "World"), so even
  widening check_series_drift's prefix filter within that one category
  wouldn't catch those.

What the fix looks like:
  Not a ticker-coverage fix -- each market type needs its own forecasting
  model with no shared architecture with the temperature-ensemble blend
  this bot runs today: precipitation-probability modeling for rain,
  snowfall-total modeling for snow, storm-track/intensity modeling for
  hurricanes. Treat as three separate potential product lines, not one
  task. If ever prioritized, rain is the most promising starting point --
  it already has real live volume (Denver/St. Paul) and precip-probability
  modeling is a smaller lift than storm-tracking.

Why not now:
  - No existing model architecture for any of the three.
  - Effort scales per market type, not incrementally with the current bot.
  - check_series_drift()'s KXHIGH*/KXLOW*-only filter is a deliberate
    simplification of an already-noisy check; widening it without picking
    a market type to actually act on would just add more unactionable noise.

When to revisit:
  - If there's real appetite to add a new market type (not just "cover more
    tickers") -- start with rain given current live volume.

  STEP 2 HANDOFF (separate future session, own plan + review -- do not
  build speculatively without re-checking these first):
  1. Real monthly-accumulation probability model in analyze_trade(),
     replacing today's unconditional None-return guard for KXRAIN*M
     tickers. No data provider gives monthly exceedance probability
     directly (confirmed this session against every provider this bot
     already uses) -- the model is a synthesis job, not a fetch. Recommended
     combo, researched and partly live-verified this session: NOAA ACIS
     StnData (`http://data.rcc-acis.org/StnData`, POST JSON, `elems:
     [{"name":"pcpn","interval":"dly"/"mly","duration":"dly"/"mly",
     "reduce":"sum"}]`, unauthenticated public API, this bot has never
     touched it) for (a) real month-to-date actual precip and (b) 30yr daily
     history to build an empirical per-city-month distribution of
     "remaining-days-of-month total" (bootstrap from historical years' D-to-
     month-end sums, not a parametric fit -- precip totals are right-skewed
     and bounded at 0), combined with the known actual-to-date value.
     Optionally tilt with Open-Meteo's Seasonal API (`seasonal-api.
     open-meteo.com/v1/seasonal`, `monthly=precipitation_mean`, ECMWF SEAS5,
     live-tested this session and confirmed working) as a directional nudge
     -- mean-only, no per-member spread, so it can adjust central tendency
     but can't itself supply distribution shape. NOAA CPC's monthly precip
     outlook (`mapservices.weather.noaa.gov/.../cpc_mthly_precip_outlk`) is
     categorical/tercile only, not a numeric CDF -- secondary signal at most,
     don't plan around it as a primary source. `_fetch_ensemble_precip`
     (existing single-day fetcher) is only practical for the final ~2 weeks
     of a month (16-day forecast cap) -- not a monthly solution on its own.
  2. Fix `_parse_market_condition()`'s real, currently-deferred bug: for
     KXRAIN*M tickers it silently collapses all 7 (or 4, NYC) ladder rungs
     into one identical `{"type": "precip_any"}`, discarding the real
     per-bracket threshold -- which lives in Kalshi's own `floor_strike`/
     `yes_sub_title`/`strike_type` market fields (confirmed via live raw
     JSON dump this session), NOT in a `-P<n>` ticker suffix or "inch" text
     in the title (real title is just "Rain in Denver in Jul 2026?"). Must
     be fixed before or alongside item 1 -- the model needs the real
     threshold to compare against.
  3. MANDATORY before any monthly-rain prediction/trade is ever logged: the
     position-sizing fail-open gap found this session. `MAX_CITY_DATE_
     EXPOSURE`/correlated-city penalties (paper.portfolio_kelly_fraction,
     order_executor.py's per-date cap) both key off `target_date_str` being
     a single-day string and silently skip when it's None -- which it
     always is for these tickers (no day component to parse). Once Step 2
     gives these tickers a real (non-None) grouping key, decide deliberately
     how monthly rain positions should be capped (extend the exposure system
     to accept a month-string key, treat the bracket's month as a synthetic
     date, or something else) -- don't let this silently start bypassing the
     caps just because target_date_str stops being None.
  4. Ladder/sibling grouping: `compute_market_implied_distributions()`'s
     current blanket exclusion needs to become real (city, month) grouping.
     `fit_market_implied_distribution()`'s weighted-least-squares machinery
     was confirmed this session to be structurally reusable (works off
     generic (lo, hi, mid_price, weight) tuples) but needs new sigma sanity
     bounds for an inches scale -- current bounds (0.1-50.0) are tuned for
     °F. NYC's ladder has only 4 brackets (not 7, a Kalshi listing choice,
     confirmed via settled history) -- handle variable ladder sizes.
  5. Settlement: `outcomes.settled_value` (float) is reusable for the
     monthly cumulative total, but `settled_var`'s existing semantic (a
     max/min-hour discriminator, from the hourly work) doesn't map cleanly
     onto "this is a monthly total" -- needs a new sentinel value or its own
     column, a real design decision, not a free reuse. `tracker.
     audit_settlement()` currently bails via `_parse_city_date()` returning
     None before reaching any settlement logic -- monthly rain needs its own
     settlement path triggered at month-end, not the "call once near a known
     instant" shape used for daily/hourly (a month's total is only final
     after the month ends, not observable at one point in time the way a
     daily high or an hourly reading is).
  6. Consensus-bonus precedent to follow, not rediscover: hourly Step 2's
     independent review caught that `_analyze_hourly_trade()`'s `consensus`
     flag was near-tautological (its two inputs weren't independent enough
     to justify `_price_and_size()`'s Kelly bonus) and had to be hardcoded
     `False` with a documented reason. A monthly-rain model will face the
     identical question the moment it has more than one signal (e.g. the
     ACIS-empirical estimate vs. the Seasonal-API-tilted one) -- verify real
     independence before wiring any consensus bonus, don't assume it.

     signal in this file (env var + sample-count floor via a new tracker

     monthly-rain predictions exist to validate real edge.
