[PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-07-23 -- item #1 (generalize _model_weights()) shipped; #2/#3/#4 (the actual graduation decision) still gated on real data, unchanged] GRADUATE GEM/UKMO (AND FUTURE TRACKING-ONLY MODELS) FROM TRACK-ONLY INTO THE LIVE BLEND
Priority: Medium -- read together with GENERALIZED PER-MODEL ACCURACY
  TRACKING above (Pass 3, conceptually: that entry generalized the
  tracking mechanism, this one generalizes the weighting mechanism the
  same way).

RESOLVED 2026-07-23 (item #1 only -- _model_weights() generalized, zero live
  behavior change today, pushed pending commit): tiers 1 (MAE-derived) and 2
  (learned_weights.json) of _model_weights() now admit any model beyond the
  fixed 3-key baseline that is a genuine candidate for the ensemble blend --
  i.e. in `baseline` or in TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES -- instead of only ever
  iterating the hardcoded 3 keys. Tier 3 (pure seasonal, no data at all)
  deliberately stays baseline-only, since a non-baseline model has no coded
  seasonal/climatological prior and consumers' own `weights.get(model, 1.0)`
  fallback already produces the identical neutral value either way.
  A real, non-obvious bug was caught by an opus review before this could ship
  as originally scoped: a naive "admit any model with tracked data" version
  (the first attempt) would have let `ecmwf_ifs025` leak into this function's
  output -- it's real, currently-tracked data (feeds
  _forecast_model_weights()'s SEPARATE daily deterministic blend, has no
  ensemble members, was never a candidate for THIS blend) that, unlike
  gem_global/ukmo_global_ensemble_20km, is NOT blocked by
  TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES from reaching mae_weights/learned_weights.json.
  The reviewer's own suggested fix (add ecmwf_ifs025 to
  TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES) was rejected as semantically wrong -- that
  constant means "excluded from EVERY live blend," and ecmwf_ifs025 genuinely
  has real live weight elsewhere. Fixed instead by restricting admission to
  `ensemble_candidate_models = set(baseline) | TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES`
  specifically (both tiers), which correctly excludes ecmwf_ifs025 without
  mislabeling it. A second opus review confirmed this correction is sound and
  complete (enumerated every model that can ever reach
  get_member_accuracy()'s output -- only ecmwf_ifs025 needed excluding, and
  is now the only one that was) and caught one more real gap: this entry's
  own item #2 text below (and this function's docstring) claimed graduation
  is a clean "one-line change: remove it from TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES, no
  other code change needed" -- that is WRONG given the fix above. Removing a
  model from TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES alone would also remove it from
  `ensemble_candidate_models` unless it's separately added to `baseline` too
  -- skipping that second step would silently re-exclude it, reproducing the
  exact bug this generalization exists to fix, just one step later.
  **Corrected graduation recipe (supersedes item #2 below): (1) remove from
  TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES, (2) add to `baseline` in _model_weights() (a
  plain 1.0 if no seasonal prior is warranted), (3) add to the live-blend
  fetch lists in get_ensemble_temps()/batch_prewarm_ensemble().** Item #3's
  MAE pre-check and item #4's per-city/global-floor reasoning below are
  otherwise unaffected and still the real remaining gate.
  Also documented (not fixed, correctly left as-is): `ensemble_candidate_models`
  treats "in TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES" as synonymous with "ensemble-blend
  candidate" -- true today (both current members are real ensemble products)
  but not a structural guarantee; flagged directly in the function's own
  docstring so a future addition to TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES for a
  non-ensemble reason doesn't silently get swept into this blend too.
  Both generalizations are confirmed INERT in production today (verified by
  both review passes): TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES models are skipped inside
  _weights_from_mae() itself before ever reaching mae_weights, so nothing
  currently exercises the new admission branches outside tests that inject a
  value directly via mock. 3 new regression tests added
  (tests/test_weather_markets.py: tier-1 admits a non-baseline model, tier-2
  admits one, a real-model-that-must-NOT-leak-in test using ecmwf_ifs025
  specifically -- not the untestable-in-practice gem_global/ukmo shape),
  each mutation-tested against a reverted version of the fix. 665 tests pass
  (up from the pre-existing 661) across the full scoped sweep
  (test_tracker.py/test_weather_markets.py/test_signal_quality.py/
  test_forecasting.py/test_phase4.py/test_weather.py); ruff/ruff-format/mypy
  clean.
  Item #1 (generalize _forecast_model_weights() too) from the original plan
  below was found NOT NEEDED after tracing the actual code: gem_global/
  ukmo_global_ensemble_20km only ever appear via the ensemble-side
  _get_gem_ukmo_means() (ENSEMBLE_BASE), never anywhere near
  _forecast_model_weights() or get_weather_forecast()'s deterministic daily
  fetch loop -- they are exclusively ensemble-shaped models. Touching that
  second live-trading-critical function would have been unnecessary surface
  area for zero benefit.

Problem:
  As of Pass 2, gem_global/ukmo_global_ensemble_20km are tracked for
  accuracy (model_forecast_means, ensemble_member_scores) but structurally
  barred from the live blend via TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES
  (weather_markets.py). The reason they're barred isn't a policy choice
  about GEM/UKMO specifically -- it's that _model_weights() (the ensemble
  blend, feeds batch_prewarm_ensemble) and _forecast_model_weights() (the
  daily point-forecast blend, feeds get_weather_forecast()) each hardcode
  a fixed 3-key baseline dict (`for model, default in baseline.items()`)
  and normalise/softmax over it -- there is no code path today by which
  ANY model outside that dict could ever earn live weight, no matter how
  much tracked accuracy it accumulates. Hardcoding GEM/UKMO in as a 4th
  and 5th baseline key would work, but repeats the exact "one more model,
  one more hand-edit in N places" pattern GENERALIZED PER-MODEL ACCURACY
  TRACKING was built to end -- and would need doing AGAIN for the next
  source (a future WeatherNext, or whatever comes after).

What the fix looks like:
  1. Generalize _model_weights() and _forecast_model_weights() to iterate
     whatever models clear their EXISTING accuracy floor (the same min_n
     that already gates _weights_from_mae's tier-1 / get_model_weights's
     MIN_OBSERVATIONS=10 softmax inclusion) minus TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES,
     instead of a fixed baseline dict -- mirroring exactly how Pass 1
     turned 4 named scalar fields into one generic dict. A model with no
     seasonal/meteorological-skill prior (unlike ECMWF's reasoned ecmwf_w)
     gets a neutral 1.0 default, same as icon/gfs today, until its own
     learned weight overrides it.
  2. Once that mechanism exists, "graduating" a specific model is a
     ONE-LINE change: remove it from TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES. No other
     code change needed -- same design promise as Pass 1's "add a source
     needs one line in analyze_trade()."
  3. Do NOT gate this one-line removal on a new, elevated sample floor.
     Re-derived from source (first pass here wrongly proposed a new 50-obs
     floor "because graduation is a bigger decision") and corrected: once
     the mechanism in #1 exists, the EXISTING per-model floor (min_n=20,
     matching ACCURACY_MIN_SAMPLE/SPRT_MIN_TRADES precedent, already used
     to decide whether ANY model's learned weight is trusted) is what
     already answers "is there enough data on this specific model" --
     inventing a separate, higher, GEM/UKMO-specific bar would be exactly
     the kind of new-signal special-casing the RUN-TO-RUN TREND entry's own
     ENABLEMENT TRIGGER text warns against ("don't invent a new... bar just
     because this signal is new").
  4. DO add a concrete, written pre-check before #2 (revised after user
     pushback on the first-pass "no formal bar, just eyeball it" proposal
     -- correctly: the inverse-MAE formula's self-regulation has a lag.
     weight = 1/mae is normalised over a ROLLING window (60 days in
     _weights_from_mae, 30 in get_model_weights), so a genuinely bad model
     only gets down-weighted gradually as its window-average MAE catches
     up -- meaning it could measurably drag on real trade probability for
     weeks after graduation before the formula discounts it. A pre-check
     run BEFORE the code change ships, not an after-the-fact hope the
     formula self-corrects, is the actual fix for that lag). The concrete
     check: at graduation time, query get_member_accuracy()/
     get_model_weights() for the SAME city and rolling window the live
     blend itself uses, and require:
       gem_or_ukmo_mae <= worst-performing current baseline model's mae
     (i.e. icon_seamless/gfs_seamless/ecmwf_aifs025_ensemble/ecmwf_ifs025's
     own MAE over that identical window/city, whichever is highest/worst
     today) -- not "must beat the average," just "must not be worse than
     the worst model already blended," so graduating GEM/UKMO can't make
     the blend's own worst-case per-model error picture worse than what's
     already live. Compute this per-city (accuracy can vary a lot by
     region -- a model competitive in NYC could be bad in Phoenix), but
     since TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES is a single global flag per model
     (see the mechanical note under "When to revisit" below), the actual
     go/no-go is the WORST city's result across all cities with enough
     data, not any single city's -- don't flip the global switch on a
     good NYC number while some other city is quietly bad. If a model
     fails this check, leave it in TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES and re-check
     again after more data accumulates, rather than graduating it anyway
     on the theory the formula will fix it. This is a documented, defined
     criterion to apply at the time -- not vague "eyeball it" -- while
     still keeping the actual code change (#1/#2) itself a deliberate,
     reviewed, separately-confirmed merge, matching this file's own
     stated philosophy for this shape of decision (see the SIGNAL
     GRADUATION entry: "leave blend wiring manual -- the deliberate human
     step is the point of the pattern").

Why not now:
  - #1/#2 are real, live-trading-critical code changes (both blend weight
    functions) that deserve their own dedicated pass, review, and test
    coverage -- not a rider on Pass 2.
  - There is no real tracked data yet: gem_global/ukmo_global_ensemble_20km
    were only wired into model_forecast_means as of Pass 2 (2026-07-23),
    so ensemble_member_scores has zero rows for either. The floor in #3
    (min_n=20, per-city or global matching _weights_from_mae's own
    fallback logic) hasn't remotely been reached and needs real elapsed
    paper-trading time, not more engineering effort right now.

When to revisit:
  - Check settled-observation counts for gem_global/ukmo_global_ensemble_20km
    in ensemble_member_scores periodically (e.g. whenever this file is next
    open for other reasons, same cadence as the RUN-TO-RUN TREND and
    DATA-DRIVEN SIGMA FROM SETTLED HISTORY entries' own settled-count
    checks -- all three are gated on the same kind of settled-trade volume
    growing over time).
  - Once min_n=20 is cleared (per-city preferred, global fallback,
    mirroring _weights_from_mae's existing tier-1 logic exactly): build #1
    (generalize both weight functions), then run #4's concrete MAE
    pre-check per-city against icon/gfs/ecmwf_aifs025_ensemble/
    ecmwf_ifs025's own numbers over the same window. Important mechanical
    note (caught while writing this up): TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES is a
    single global on/off per model, not per-city -- there is no way to
    graduate a model in NYC but leave it track-only in Phoenix without a
    bigger change (e.g. turning the set into a city-scoped structure,
    itself a separate design decision, not assumed here). So #4's
    per-city results feed one aggregate go/no-go per model: look at the
    WORST city's result across all cities with enough data, not just any
    single city's -- don't flip the global switch on the strength of a
    good NYC number while some other city is quietly bad. (Per-city
    weight variation still happens correctly AFTER graduation, via the
    existing city-preferred-else-global MAE logic already in
    _weights_from_mae -- what the pre-check gates is only the one-time
    global on/off decision, not ongoing per-city weighting.) Then do #2
    (remove from TRACKING_ONLY_MODEL_NAMES) as an explicit, reviewed,
    separately-confirmed change -- not an automatic flip the moment the
    floor is crossed.
  - GEM and UKMO should graduate independently, not as a pair -- no reason
    to hold one back for the other, and UKMO's shorter real forecast
    horizon (~9-10 of 16 days, see Pass 2's resolution above) may mean it
    never earns a competitive learned weight even with plenty of data,
    which is fine -- that's exactly what the inverse-MAE weighting is
    supposed to discover on its own.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-19] LIQUIDITY-AWARE SIZING + DYNAMIC EDGE THRESHOLD
Priority: was Medium (consolidates two existing loose ends into one
  feature).

RESOLVED 2026-07-19: split the two original mechanisms by risk profile
  rather than shipping both live, after a scoping pass that found the
  2026-07-18 UPDATE's "319 real fills" framing overstated what that data
  could actually do -- tracker.price_improvement has no volume/open_interest
  column and no join key back to book depth at fill time (price_history,
  which would let you reconstruct that, still has 0 rows); even the weak
  proxy check (does the bot's own order quantity correlate with fill
  slippage magnitude?) showed no relationship (corr ~= -0.03 to -0.07,
  n=319). So neither original mechanism could be empirically calibrated --
  both are reasoned defaults, same as the 2026-07-12 originals were.
  Given that, the two pieces were deliberately NOT shipped with equal
  confidence:
  1. paper.liquidity_kelly_scale(market) -- LIVE. Revives the deleted
     slippage_kelly_scale's exact tier shape (volume+open_interest summed;
     500/200/50 -> 1.00/0.85/0.70/0.50), wired into order_executor.py's
     _auto_place_trades sizing math (line ~2352, multiplied into adj_kelly
     right alongside corr_kelly_scale -- same call site, same pattern).
     Chosen to ship live because it fails safe: a wrong multiplier only
     ever produces a smaller (or zero) bet, never a wrong-direction one,
     and every existing position-size guardrail (MAX_TOTAL_OPEN_EXPOSURE,
     KELLY_CAP, corr_kelly_scale's own floor, daily-loss/drawdown halts)
     still sits downstream of it as a safety net.
  2. weather_markets._liquidity_edge_scale(volume, open_interest) --
     LOG-ONLY. Matches code_review_plan.md's Phase 5 Feature 3 design
     exactly (confirmed via git archaeology -- never built there). Computed
     as gated_edge = adjusted_edge / liquidity_edge_scale at the scan-loop
     level (cron.py's cmd_cron, main.py's _analyze_once) -- deliberately
     NOT inside analyze_trade() itself (mirrors run_trend's/market_implied's
     precedent of keeping unvalidated signals out of the live trade-decision
     function) and NEVER used for STRONG/MED/MIN classification. Kept
     log-only because a wrong multiplier here is a correctness risk, not
     just a sizing one -- it sits upstream of every existing safety net,
     and could in principle inflate a weak signal into STRONG rather than
     just under-sizing a good one (the same failure class as this project's
     own past T-bucket sign-inversion and net_edge cap-ordering bugs). See
     ENABLEMENT TRIGGER below for what's required before this changes.
  Logged into 2 new predictions columns (liquidity_edge_scale, gated_edge --
  migration v46/v47) via order_executor._prediction_kwargs_from_analysis,
  reading a.get("liquidity_edge_scale")/a.get("gated_edge") (same
  scan-paths-only pattern as market_implied -- cmd_market/cmd_order log
  NULL for both).
  8 new tests for liquidity_kelly_scale (tests/test_paper.py), 8 for
  _liquidity_edge_scale (tests/test_weather_markets.py), plus extensions to
  test_prediction_kwargs.py (2 tests) and test_tracker.py (2 tests). A real
  bug caught mid-build (not by review): main.py's first-draft wiring
  computed gated_edge from raw `edge` while cron.py's used `adjusted_edge`
  -- would have made the two scan paths log incomparable values, silently
  corrupting the future correlation check below. Caught by re-reading the
  two call sites side by side before moving on, fixed to derive both from
  adjusted_edge consistently.
  Independent opus review caught one real, live-money bug before push:
  paper.liquidity_kelly_scale (and both log-only call sites) read only the
  legacy market.get("volume")/market.get("open_interest") field names --
  but the current Kalshi API returns volume_fp/open_interest_fp, and
  nothing normalizes one to the other. Every other volume/OI consumer in
  this codebase (analyze_trade()'s own liquidity gate, is_liquid() partly,
  parse_market_price, schema_validator.py) already coalesces
  X_fp or X or 0 -- this new code was the one exception, and would have
  silently applied the worst-case 0.50 Kelly multiplier to every live
  trade on a market that only carries the _fp fields (which is the live,
  current-API case), halving position sizes with no error and no log.
  Confirmed via the reviewer's own repro (a genuinely deep book,
  volume_fp=2000/open_interest_fp=3000, correctly liquid but returned 0.50
  pre-fix instead of the correct 1.00). Fixed all 3 call sites
  (paper.liquidity_kelly_scale; cron.py/main.py's
  log-only _liquidity_edge_scale call sites) to match analyze_trade()'s
  exact coalescing pattern. Added 2 new tests proving the _fp names are
  read and take precedence over legacy names when both are present --
  the review's own note: the original tests only exercised plain field
  names, "exactly why they pass while live behavior breaks," so green
  tests alone hadn't caught this. Also surfaced, not fixed here (separate,
  lower-severity, pre-existing): is_liquid() (weather_markets.py) has the
  same plain-names-only gap, masked in practice by its own OR-fallback on
  real bid/ask quote presence -- worth a future look, filed as its own
  consideration rather than silently patched as a drive-by here.
  696 tests pass across the full scoped run (test_tracker.py, test_paper.py,
  test_weather_markets.py, the cron/shadow-prediction cluster,
  test_trade_improvements.py, test_live_execution.py), lint clean.

ENABLEMENT TRIGGER (the actual ask: when to wire gated_edge into
  STRONG/MED/MIN classification instead of adjusted_edge) -- do NOT change
  the classification threshold until:
  1. A meaningful number of settled trades exist with non-NULL gated_edge
     (same sample-floor precedent as every other signal in this file --
     ACCURACY_MIN_SAMPLE=20 / SPRT_MIN_TRADES=20 -- don't invent a lower bar
     just because this signal is new).
  2. A real check has been run against that data: among trades gated_edge
     would have downgraded a tier (STRONG under adjusted_edge but only MED
     or below under gated_edge), did those trades actually perform worse
     (win rate, Brier score) than trades that stayed at the same tier under
     both? If thin-book downgrades really did underperform, that's the
     evidence to wire gated_edge in. If not, close this as not-applicable
     rather than activating it on the mechanism sounding plausible alone --
     same discipline as every other log-only signal's enablement trigger.
  3. liquidity_kelly_scale's own tiers (500/200/50 -> 1.00/0.85/0.70/0.50)

  a one-off analysis against live data, not a wiring decision; the same

FOLLOW-UP BUG, FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-19 (same day, later -- caught live
via `python main.py cron`, not via review): the fix above corrected the
field NAME (read volume_fp/open_interest_fp, not just legacy volume/
open_interest) but not its TYPE. volume_fp/open_interest_fp are
FixedPointCount strings on the real API (e.g. "10.00"), not numbers --
`market.get("volume_fp") or market.get("volume") or 0` returns that
string as-is when present, and `volume > 0` raises TypeError comparing a
str to an int (no implicit str/int ordering in Python 3). This crashed
cron.py's entire scan loop in production the moment any market actually
had real volume: a live `python main.py cron` run scanned 480 markets,
crashed via is_stale() on the first market with nonzero volume_fp, and
reported "no actionable signals found" -- not because there were none,
but because analysis never got a chance to run for the cycle.
is_liquid() has the identical bug but never crashed in practice --
`has_yes or has_no or volume > 0` short-circuits before reaching
`volume > 0` for any market with real bid/ask quotes, masking it the
same way the original field-name gap was masked.
Root cause of why the original fix's own regression tests didn't catch
this: both new tests added for the fix above used plain Python ints for
volume_fp/open_interest_fp (`"volume_fp": 500`), not strings matching the
real API's FixedPointCount shape -- an int never triggers a str/int
comparison error, only a real API response (or a correctly-typed test
fixture) does. Same lesson as this entry's own "matches Kalshi's real
field names, not just any truthy value" discipline, one level deeper:
matching the field name isn't enough, the fixture's VALUE TYPE has to
match too.
Fixed by wrapping both reads in float(...), matching every other
volume_fp/open_interest_fp reader in this file (analyze_trade's own
liquidity gate, market-implied-distribution weighting). Fixed the 2
existing under-typed tests to use real string fixtures ("500.00" not
500), and added 3 new regression tests reproducing the exact crash
(string volume_fp present and nonzero; string volume_fp present and
genuinely zero, confirming the fix didn't break the zero case;
is_liquid()'s masked equivalent with no quotes so the short-circuit
can't hide it). Mutation-tested both fixes independently by reverting
each float() wrapping and confirming the new tests reproduce the exact
live TypeError, then restoring. Verified end-to-end against the real
crash scenario twice more via actual `python main.py cron` runs (prod
API, TRADING_PAUSED=true so no order-placement risk) -- no crash, and
the resulting gate breakdown (between_no_metar/extreme_price/liquidity/
min_volume/model_mkt_gap/model_spread/retired_method/spread summing to
exactly 480) confirmed every market was legitimately filtered by
pre-existing gates, not silently mis-handled by a lingering bug.
367 tests pass across the full regression sweep (every file touching
is_stale/is_liquid); ruff/ruff format/mypy clean.

Independent second-opinion review (Agent, opus), requested given this
touches the real production scan loop: found the fix above was NOT the
full extent of this bug class -- grepped every .py file (not just
weather_markets.py) for volume_fp/open_interest_fp reads and surfaced 3
more unguarded sites with the identical root cause, none caught by this
session's own earlier review:
  1. weather_markets._liquidity_edge_scale (HIGH) -- both real callers
     (cron.py's cmd_cron, main.py's _analyze_once) pass the raw coalesced
     string straight in; the function's own body does
     `(volume or 0) + (open_interest or 0)`, which on two strings is
     STRING CONCATENATION (no error at that line), then crashes one line
     later at `liq >= 500`. Worse than is_stale()'s bug: a non-empty
     string is always truthy, so this fires even for a genuinely-zero
     "0.00", not just a real nonzero value. This call sits INSIDE the
     exact same cmd_cron scan loop already fixed above, reached only for
     markets that clear every analyze_trade-internal gate -- the day's
     480-market verification run happened to hit zero such markets (hence
     "no crash" was observed), which is exactly why this was missed by
     re-running cron rather than reading the code: the next actionable
     market would have reproduced the identical scan-loop-crashing
     failure this whole entry exists to fix.
  2. main.py's cmd_market whale-alert print (MEDIUM) -- same
     volume/open_interest > threshold comparison, interactive-CLI-only
     (not the live scan loop), but still a real crash on the normal live
     shape.
  3. main.py's cmd_market Vol table column (LOW, cosmetic only) -- no
     crash (tabulate just str()s whatever's in the cell), but displayed
     the raw fixed-point string unconverted instead of a clean number.
  Fixed all 3: _liquidity_edge_scale now converts volume/open_interest to
  float() internally (at the function itself, not each call site, so
  both current callers are fixed by one change and any future caller is
  protected too) -- also dropped its now-inaccurate `: int` type hints,
  since real callers were never passing ints. Whale-alert wrapped in
  float() to match. Vol column wrapped in float() for display
  consistency. 2 new tests for _liquidity_edge_scale (string-input
  addition proven not concatenation; string "0.00" proven not truthy-
  masking a real zero), mutation-tested (reverted the float() wrapping,
  confirmed the exact TypeError reproduces, restored). No dedicated test
  added for the whale-alert/Vol-column fixes (pure CLI display output,
  matching this same code's own prior "not proportionate to unit-test in
  isolation" precedent from the original field-name fix) -- verified
  manually instead against the real API shape.
  416 tests pass across a wider regression sweep (cron/market-implied-
  distribution/p1-remaining/paper/weather_markets/menu-ux/trading test
  files); ruff/ruff format/mypy clean.

Original problem (kept for history):
  Market analysis is per-bracket independent; nothing chooses the optimal
  COMBINATION of sibling brackets for one city/date against the model's
  full temperature distribution. (The arb auto-trade block in main.py:1542+
  only fires on sum-to-1 violations — different mechanism.) Sequential
  per-market Kelly with position caps is not the same as jointly allocating
  across mutually-exclusive outcomes of one event.

What the fix looks like:
  Group candidate signals by event (city/date/series) before sizing; solve
  the joint Kelly allocation across the group (mutually-exclusive outcomes
  make this a clean simplex problem) instead of greedy per-market sizing.
  Smallest useful version: within an event group, cap total exposure and
  allocate proportionally to per-bracket edge rather than first-come.

Why not now:
  - Real sizing-math design work + touches the same order-placement path as
    several entries above; sequence it after the execution work stabilizes.

When to revisit: N/A -- resolved (smallest useful version shipped). If the
  same-series sibling co-occurrence rate ever climbs materially above the
  observed ~5x/quarter (e.g. once the bot trades more cities/markets
  concurrently), the full joint-Kelly/simplex solve becomes worth
  reconsidering -- re-check the trigger rate against real data rather than
  assuming it changed.

  (main.py:1262), purely to print a human-readable orderbook table -- it has
  nothing to do with the live WS trading pipeline. Confirmed via
  docs.kalshi.com/websockets/orderbook-updates that subscribing to
  orderbook_delta for a ticker already triggers Kalshi's own automatic
  orderbook_snapshot message first, then incremental deltas -- and
  kalshi_ws.py's parse_message() already handles that exact
  "orderbook_snapshot" message type (kalshi_ws.py:88). So there's no
  REST-call redundancy to remove; book init is already snapshot-via-WS with
  zero REST involvement.
  get_snapshot's real, narrower value for this bot: a one-off book peek for
  a ticker that is NOT in the persistent per-cycle subscription list (e.g.
  previewing a candidate market's current book before deciding whether to
  add it to cron.py's per-cycle _ws.subscribe() call), without growing the
  subscription list or opening a second connection. That's a smaller,
  different use case than "simpler book initialization" as originally
  framed -- there's no current call site that needs it (this bot always
  subscribes up front to every scanned ticker), so it stays a nice-to-have
  pending a concrete use case, not a simplification of existing code.

What the fix looks like:
  No current call site needs this. If a future feature wants a one-off book
  check for a ticker outside the active subscription list (rather than
  simplifying anything that exists today), use update_subscription's
  get_snapshot action for that instead of adding a new REST call or growing
  the persistent subscription list.

Why not now:
  - Unverified against this repo's actual current book-init code path;
    purely a simplification if it applies, no functional gap being closed.
  - Re-verified 2026-07-12: it doesn't apply as a simplification (there's no
    existing REST-call redundancy to remove) -- only relevant if/when a
    concrete one-off-book-peek use case appears.

When to revisit: N/A -- closed. Re-open as a new entry if a concrete
  one-off-book-peek use case (outside the active subscription list) ever
  actually appears.

  SIGNAL
Priority: Low-Medium (cheap to capture, speculative value)

Problem:
  kalshi_ws.py subscribes only to ticker + orderbook_delta (line 301);
  Kalshi's public `trade` channel (executed trades feed) is unused. Signed

What the fix looks like:

    bot runs continuously.

[RESOLVED 2026-07-30 (fetch/plumbing piece), CLOSED 2026-08-07 (LLM
  confidence/lean scoring half, declined by user -- not worth pursuing) --

Priority: was Low (stretch/novel — highest differentiation, least proven)
  -- fetch/plumbing piece is done; the actual differentiating signal
  (confidence/lean scoring) is still exactly as unproven as before, just
  no longer blocked on infrastructure.

Problem:
  Each WFO publishes an AFD where human forecasters state confidence and
  explicit disagreement with model guidance ("models overmixing, expect
  highs 2-3F below guidance") — exactly the correction the recurring
  NWS-bias investigations hunt for statistically, published free per city
  per day. Nothing consumes it.

What the fix looks like:
  Fetch AFDs via the same IEM afos API already scoped for the CLI-report
  fetch (shared city->WFO table — build once for both). LLM-extract a
  per-city confidence score + directional lean vs guidance; feed as a
  small bounded blend adjustment, gated behind tracked accuracy like any
  other source.

Why not now:
  - Adds an LLM dependency + per-day API cost to the pipeline; extraction
    quality needs its own evaluation before the signal can be trusted;
    depends on the same WFO table as the CLI-report fetch (build together).

When to revisit:
  - Alongside the CLI-report fetch (shared infrastructure), or as a fun
    standalone experiment scored in shadow mode first.

RESOLVED 2026-07-30 (fetch/plumbing piece only -- confidence/lean scoring
  still open, see below): built nws_afd.py. Re-verified this entry's own
  claims before starting: confirmed live (queried api.weather.gov/points
  for every weather_markets.CITY_COORDS city) that the `gridId` field
  returned is identical to `cwa` for all 21 cities, then cross-checked each
  resulting AFD<office> PIL actually resolves to a real bulletin on IEM's
  afos mirror (200 + a real <pre class="afos-pre"> block) for all 20
  distinct offices -- this is CITY_WFO_OFFICE, registry #9 (see
  weather_markets.city_registry_report()'s "PER-CITY KNOWLEDGE SCATTERED"
  docstring, and tests/test_city_registry_manifest.py's new
  test_wfo_office_fully_covered). Static table, not derived live at
  call-time, matching _CITY_METAR_STATION's convention -- a city's WFO is
  effectively constant, and deriving it live on every fetch would add a
  second network dependency for a value nws.py's own _get_gridpoint
  already resolves and caches elsewhere.
  fetch_afd_discussion(city) mirrors mos.py's _fetch_nbp_percentiles
  fetch/cache pattern (same IEM AFOS text-mirror endpoint, same
  <pre class="afos-pre"> extraction, same retry-on-5xx session config,
  1h TTL matching _NBP_CACHE_TTL, cached per-WFO-office so cities sharing
  an office -- Austin/SanAntonio, both EWX -- share one fetch) -- the one
  real difference is AFD's PIL is WFO-office-keyed (AFD<office>) rather
  than NBP's station-keyed one, so it needed its own table rather than
  reusing metar.MARKET_STATION_MAP.

  Independent opus review (effort:high, before push, per standing
  workflow) found 3 real issues the first pass missed and 6 lower-severity
  ones -- every one addressed, not just the HIGH/MEDIUM ones:
    - HIGH (real bug): the first pass only matched bare ".DISCUSSION...".
      BOU's (Denver's) live bulletin heads the section
      ".DISCUSSION /Through Wednesday/..." -- a bracketed time-range
      qualifier on the header line -- which the original regex silently
      missed, so `py main.py afd Denver` reported nothing while a full
      discussion sat in the bulletin. Denver is the snow-market city
      shipped 2026-07-26, so this wasn't a cosmetic miss. Fixed:
      _AFD_SECTION_RES's pattern now tolerates `[^\n]*?` between the
      header name and "...", live-verified this doesn't reintroduce the
      false-match risk the non-greedy "&&" boundary already guards
      against.
    - HIGH (real gap, not just a bug): live-checking all 20 offices (the
      first pass only smoke-tested 2 -- NYC/LasVegas -- which happened to
      both use the bare ".DISCUSSION..." form; the review correctly called
      this selection bias, not validation) found 11 of 20 offices were
      broken by the original bare-header regex -- 10 that structurally
      don't use ".DISCUSSION" at all (using SYNOPSIS/NEAR TERM/SHORT TERM/
      LONG TERM instead), plus BOU/Denver, which DOES use ".DISCUSSION"
      but with a bracketed qualifier the bare regex also missed (that
      one's the H1 fix, not this one -- see below; correcting an
      imprecise "11 don't use DISCUSSION at all" framing an opus
      follow-up review caught, since BOU does use it). Of the 10 true
      non-DISCUSSION offices: LOX (LA)/SEW (Seattle) use SYNOPSIS+SHORT+
      LONG TERM, OUN (Oklahoma City) uses NEAR+SHORT+LONG TERM, the
      remaining 7 use SHORT+LONG TERM only. Fixed by extending extraction
      to concatenate whichever of SYNOPSIS/NEAR TERM/SHORT TERM/LONG TERM/
      DISCUSSION the current
      bulletin actually contains (canonical order), rather than assuming
      exactly one always exists -- deliberately still excludes .KEY
      MESSAGES (a terse bullet summary, not the same kind of prose
      reasoning), so a bulletin with none of the 5 known section names
      still correctly returns None rather than silently substituting a
      different kind of content.
      SELF-CAUGHT FOLLOW-ON BUG while re-verifying this fix (not opus):
      the qualifier-tolerance fix for the HIGH regex bug above needed to
      apply to ALL 5 section names, not just DISCUSSION -- several
      non-DISCUSSION offices ALSO put a bracketed qualifier on their
      headers (e.g. PSR's ".SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH FRIDAY/..."). An

      "PSR correctly returns None" example. Re-ran the check with the
      same qualifier-tolerant pattern _AFD_SECTION_RES actually uses (not
      a separate ad hoc one) before finalizing: all 20 offices produced at
      least one real narrative section that day once applied uniformly.

      not ship a test asserting real-office behavior that turned out to
      be an artifact of the wrong verification tool rather than a real
      case -- caught before it became a false "regression guard."
      Documented the corrected per-office breakdown in nws_afd.py's module
      docstring (previously framed as a vague "format drift" edge case)
      and in fetch_afd_discussion's own docstring.
    - HIGH (validation gap): the "live-smoke-tested against NYC and
      LasVegas" claim in the first pass of this note was true but
      misleading given both are in the working-by-luck 9-of-20 group.
      Re-verified this pass across all 20 offices directly (not just 2)
      before considering it done.
    - MEDIUM: the "no narrative section found" and "no afos-pre block"
      paths logged at DEBUG, which main.py disables by default (only

      this project's own established convention (mos.py's

    - MEDIUM: an empty (but present) narrative section -- e.g.

    - LOW: backlog claim "zero changes to the trading/scan path" was

    - LOW: "shadow-mode experiment"/"fetch/store-only" wording overstated

    - LOW: a new hand-rolled TTL dict, working against backlog.txt's own
      "ForecastCache EXISTS, BUT ~14 HAND-ROLLED TTL DICTS" entry. Fixed:
      switched to ForecastCache directly rather than adding a 15th --
      caught a real latent bug while doing this swap (see below).
      REAL BUG CAUGHT DURING THE SWAP (self-caught, not opus): ForecastCache
      .get() returns None both on a genuine cache miss AND on a fresh
      negative-cache hit (a stored None value, e.g. from a prior failed
      fetch) -- there's no way to tell them apart from get() alone, so
      naively porting the raw-dict code's "if cached is not None: return
      cached" logic to .get() would have silently defeated negative
      caching (every call after a failure would re-fetch, forever, instead
      of respecting the TTL). Used get_with_ts()'s `hit` flag instead,
      which does distinguish them.

    - MEDIUM (real, live-reproducing bug): the per-section extraction

[CITY-LOCAL AFTERNOON SAME-DAY SWEEP]
Priority: Low (mostly covered by loop/watch when they run)

Problem:
  By early afternoon a day's high is substantially determined and METAR
  lock-in gets very sharp, but there is no scan timed to each city's local
  ~2pm. loop (every 4h) and watch (every 5min) cover this incidentally when
  running; the manual-cron cadence does not.

What the fix looks like:
  A lightweight `cron --sameday-only` mode (skip multi-day scan + batch
  prewarm; METAR + same-day markets only) cheap enough to run at each
  city's local afternoon window, or an extra loop-mode wake timed to the
  2pm ET / 2pm PT bands.

Why not now:
  - Marginal over a continuously-running loop; only meaningfully valuable
    during manual-cadence periods like the current trip.

UPDATE 2026-07-20 (research pass, no code changed) -- premise checked
  against live state and found weaker than "valuable during manual-cadence
  periods like the current trip" implies:
  - Confirmed TRADING_PAUSED=true right now (.env), and is_trading_paused()
    gates _auto_place_trades() entirely -- no paper or live trade is placed
    regardless of when cron runs, until Belgium return (2026-07-31). This
    feature's actual point (catch the same-day lock-in signal before it's
    missed so a trade can be placed on it) is inactive for the whole
    remaining window it would otherwise help with. The only live value
    today is shadow-prediction logging continuity (still logged while
    paused, for Brier/calibration tracking) -- much less timing-sensitive,
    since a later same-day scan produces an equally or more confident
    lock-in read, just with less time to act on it.
  - Likely superseded, not just delayed: this entry's own "why not now"
    already scopes the value to manual-cadence gaps specifically -- and the
    already-decided fix for manual-cadence unreliability is the MOVE OFF
    LOCAL CRON entry (VM running `watch --auto --live` continuously).
    Once that lands, watch's 5-minute cadence covers every city's local
    afternoon window for free and this feature has no remaining job.
    Building it now risks throwaway work for the gap between today and
    whichever of (Belgium return, VM move) happens first.
  - Recommendation if picked up again: re-check both triggers (has
    TRADING_PAUSED cleared? has the VM move executed?) before building --
    if the VM move has landed, close this as superseded rather than
    implementing it.

When to revisit:
  - Not before 2026-07-31 (Belgium return), and only if manual cron cadence
    is still the operating mode at that point (i.e. the VM move hasn't
    landed yet) -- check both conditions fresh rather than assuming either

[RESOLVED 2026-07-17] REAL NBM VIA IEM NBS STATION BULLETINS -- REPLACE THE SILENT best_match SUBSTITUTE
Priority: was Medium-High -- the bot believed it had an "nbm" ensemble
  member; it actually had an arbitrary auto-selected model.

Problem (as originally scoped):
  fetch_temperature_nbm() no longer fetched NBM at all -- Open-Meteo removed
  the model -- and requested models: "best_match" instead, an uncalibrated
  auto-selection, yet still fed model_temps["nbm"] in analyze_trade's
  Phase-C extended ensemble and _compute_ensemble_spread. mos.py already
  integrated IEM's MOS API but only ever requested GFS/NAM.

CORRECTION during implementation -- the original entry's field-name claim
  was wrong:
  This entry's own "Live-verified 2026-07-16" note claimed NBS rows carry
  "n_x (the NBM day-max/night-min field)". Re-verified live 2026-07-17
  against 7 stations across all 4 CONUS timezones: n_x is None on every
  single NBS row, for every station. The actual field carrying the daily
  extreme is "txn" (confirmed against IEM's raw CSV export, where it's an
  unlabeled trailing column matching the classic NWS raw-MOS-bulletin "X/N"
  convention), and it is populated only on rows whose forecast-valid time
  lands exactly on a 00Z or 12Z boundary -- not a dedicated always-present
  field the way n_x was assumed to be. This also meant the "Why not now"
  risk below (per-station 12-hourly semantics, same timezone care as CLI
  settlement) was real and had to be solved, not just verified-and-shipped:
  which of the 00Z/12Z rows is the local daytime max vs. nighttime min
  depends on each station's UTC offset in general, but empirically (checked
  KNYC/Eastern, KMDW/Central, KDEN/Mountain, KLAX/Pacific) the 00Z-ending
  12h period is ALWAYS the higher (max) value and 12Z-ending ALWAYS the
  lower (min), station-timezone-independent -- because CONUS UTC offsets
  are always whole hours, so each station's ~12h local daytime window
  always falls entirely inside one UTC-anchored period or the other, never
  split. This is a genuine, verified, general rule for all 20 traded
  cities, not a KNYC-specific coincidence.

What shipped:
  mos.py: new _fetch_nbs_daily_extremes(station, city_tz) parses every
  available txn row into {(local_date, "max"|"min"): temp_f} using the
  00Z=max/12Z=min rule above (local_date computed by converting ftime to
  the station's timezone and taking .date(), which safely lands inside the
  12h period without crossing local midnight for any CONUS zone). Cached
  per (station, city_tz), 1h TTL, matching _MOS_CACHE_TTL. New public
  fetch_nbm_iem(station, target_date, city_tz, var) wraps it. Also removed
  two now-redundant local `from datetime import UTC, datetime` imports
  mos.py had (dead weight once UTC/datetime moved to the top-level import
  this entry's datetime.strptime parsing needed anyway).

  weather_markets.fetch_temperature_nbm() now tries fetch_nbm_iem() first
  (via _metar_station_for_city(city), which covers all 20 traded cities --
  NOT mos.py's 6-city _MOS_CITIES subset used by GFS/NAM MOS, per this
  entry's original "extend beyond" note), and only falls back to the old
  Open-Meteo best_match substitute when NBS has no coverage for that
  station/date (expected for same-day markets -- NBS's own forecast
  horizon is short and same-day rows are frequently absent in the current
  cycle; the METAR pipeline already covers same-day elsewhere in this
  codebase). No changes needed to analyze_trade's Phase-C ensemble or
  _compute_ensemble_spread -- both already consume fetch_temperature_nbm()'s
  return value, so the real-vs-substitute swap is fully transparent to them
  ("wire it in now" was the explicit choice made here, not log-only-first,
  since this replaces an already-live-blended signal's data source rather
  than introducing a brand-new one).

  Tests: tests/test_mos_nbs.py -- the 00Z=max/12Z=min rule verified against
  both an Eastern and a Pacific station (proving it's genuinely
  timezone-derived, not hardcoded), a mutation-proof swapped-assignment
  check, off-cycle/missing-txn row handling, cache-hit/network-failure
  behavior. tests/test_nbm.py updated (the IEM path is tried first, so its

  for) plus two new tests for the IEM-first preference and the
  no-station-mapped skip path. Mutation-tested the max/min assignment by
  hand-flipping it and confirming 6 of the new tests fail with the exact
  expected wrong values, then reverting.

  Drive-by fix: tests/test_forecasting.py's
  test_log_prediction_called_with_forecast_cycle (an AST-based check that

  **_prediction_kwargs_from_analysis(...), not a literal keyword) but not

  stripping the unpack from main.py and confirming the test fails, then

  Independently reviewed (Agent, opus) before commit, matching this
  project's standard for anything touching a live probability-blend input.

  offset including Phoenix's no-DST America/Phoenix, no off-by-one-day in
  the local-date attribution, tests genuinely correct not just plausible)
  and caught one real bug fixed before commit: fetch_temperature_nbm's

  pre-dating this entry) -- but NBS has per-var coverage gaps at its ~3-day
  horizon edge (a date can have a real IEM max with no IEM min yet, or vice

  mutation-tested by restoring the old unconditional-dual-write and

  Also hardened mos.py's ftime parsing per the review's second finding: if
  IEM ever changes the timestamp format, every txn row would silently fail
  to parse and the feature would permanently no-op to the Open-Meteo
  fallback with no signal -- now logs a warning when every txn-bearing row

[RESOLVED 2026-07-17] DISCRETIZATION-CONSISTENT T-BUCKET THRESHOLDS -- HALF-DEGREE CONTINUITY
Priority: was Medium-High -- systematic, direction-consistent probability
  skew on every tail-bucket trade; bordered a correctness issue, not just a
  feature idea.

Problem (as originally scoped):
  _parse_market_condition already reasons explicitly about integer
  settlement for between-buckets -- B87.5 -> [86.5, 88.5], with a comment
  that brackets "must tile without gaps" (weather_markets.py:3719-3723).
  But T-buckets kept raw integer thresholds: T92 -> {"above", 92.0}, and
  every prob path taking condition raw (_forecast_probability,
  ensemble_cdf_prob, EMOS, nws_prob, ...) used that raw value directly,
  so the ladder didn't tile under the code's own between-bucket
  convention -- dropping probability mass near every tail-bucket boundary.

CORRECTION during implementation -- the original "What it would look
  like" below had the sign backwards:
  This entry's own original proposal ("above: val-0.5; below: val+0.5")
  was never live-verified and turned out to be wrong. Before writing any
  code, fetched real rules_primary text from 8 live Kalshi T-bucket
  markets across 4 cities (KXHIGHNY/CHI/DEN/MIA) via the API. Every
  sample showed the same pattern: a "T{val} above" ticker's actual rule
  is "greater than {val}" -- e.g. T86 "above" has subtitle "87° or above"
  and rules_primary "is greater than 86" -- meaning integer settlement
  must be val+1 or higher, not val or higher as this entry originally
  assumed. Matching the between-bucket code's own already-committed
  tiling convention (a "85-86" between-bucket is B85.5 -> [84.5, 86.5]),
  the correct continuous boundary is val+0.5 for above and val-0.5 for
  below -- the OPPOSITE sign from the original proposal. Shipping the
  original proposal as written would have shifted every T-bucket
  threshold a full 1.0°F in the wrong direction (turning a 0.5°F bug into
  a 1.0°F bug on the other side), not fixed it. Full ladder check around
  a boundary: T67-below (wins <=66) -> 66.5; B67.5 -> {67,68}; T68-above
  (wins >=69) -> 68.5. Integer 68 lands in exactly B67.5 and not in
  T68-above (68 > 68.5 is false) -- tiles with no gap or overlap.

What shipped:
  _parse_market_condition (weather_markets.py) now returns a second,
  sibling key on above/below condition dicts: "prob_threshold" (val+0.5 /
  val-0.5), alongside the existing "threshold" (raw ticker/rule value,
  UNCHANGED). Deliberately did not mutate "threshold" in place -- several
  consumers must keep comparing against the literal raw rule value
  (tracker.audit_settlement's archive cross-check against Kalshi's actual
  rule text, weather_markets._metar_lock_in's same-day METAR lockout
  check, and condition_threshold= DB/logging bookkeeping in
  main.py/order_executor.py) and mutating threshold would have silently
  corrupted all three. A single shared helper, utils.prob_threshold(condition)
  (falls back to raw "threshold" for between/precip conditions, which
  don't have "prob_threshold"), is now the one place every genuine
  continuous-probability consumer reads from, instead of each site
  reimplementing its own shift/fallback -- avoiding the
  triplicated-logic-one-drifts pattern already hit elsewhere in this file
  (LOG_PREDICTION KWARGS, KALSHI CENTS/DOLLARS NORMALIZATION). Updated
  every genuine probability-math call site: ensemble_cdf_prob,
  _forecast_probability, _bootstrap_ci, _get_consensus_probs (model-
  consensus safety gate), analyze_trade's EMOS exceedance/interval calls,
  raw ensemble-fraction fallback, gaussian_probability call, extended-
  ensemble (NBM/ECMWF) raw fraction, near-threshold detection, the
  climate-index adj_condition shift (now shifts both threshold and
  prob_threshold by index_adj so they stay consistent), and the
  persistence-baseline _tlo lookup -- plus nws.py's nws_prob and
  obs_prob, climatology.py's _climatological_prob_inner, and backtest.py
  (so backtest results keep matching live behavior). Confirmed
  audit_settlement, _metar_lock_in, settlement_monitor.py, and the DB/
  logging call sites were left untouched and still read raw "threshold".
  Tests (tests/test_weather.py): parse-time above/below prob_threshold
  values, a tiling-identity test (between-bucket upper == adjacent
  T-bucket's prob_threshold, live-ticker-verified), utils.prob_threshold's
  fallback behavior, and mutation-proof tests for _forecast_probability
  and ensemble_cdf_prob (forecast/members placed exactly in the old
  gap -- verified these fail if the fix is reverted, by actually
  reverting one line, running the suite, confirming the expected failure,
  then restoring it).

  Independently reviewed (Agent, opus) before commit: re-derived the
  sign/magnitude from the tiling argument independently (confirmed
  correct), audited every touched call site (confirmed each is a genuine
  probability computation, not a should-stay-raw site), searched for
  missed consumers, and checked the None-handling `or 0` idiom used at
  two sites for a silent-remap-of-a-real-0.0-threshold bug (confirmed
  safe -- T-ticker thresholds are always half-integers, never exactly
  0.0, and both sites are already type-guarded so the fallback can't
  fire on a real market anyway). No bugs found.

Known residual (not fixed here, correctly out of scope):
  - sigma_audit.py's _forecast_prob() replicates the Gaussian CDF from DB
    columns threshold_lo/threshold_hi, which tracker.py populates from
    the raw (unshifted) threshold by design -- so this diagnostic-only
    script still carries the same tail skew. Revisit if/when sigma_audit
    output is used for more than diagnostics.
  - nws.py's nws_prob_from_quantiles() is dead code (only referenced by
    tests/docs/backlog, not wired into analyze_trade or any live path,

    If it's ever wired in, its caller must pass prob_threshold, not raw

  - Calibration-reset interplay (per-city Platt/temperature scaling may
    have been partially absorbing the average skew this fixes) not

[RESOLVED 2026-07-19] AMEND ORDER (V2) -- REPLACE CANCEL-VERIFY-REPLACE IN THE REPRICE LOOP
Priority: was Medium -- removes the exact client-side race window the
  reprice feature needed hardened plumbing to work around, and halves
  write-call count per reprice.

RESOLVED 2026-07-19:
  Re-verified the endpoint shape against Kalshi's live docs before coding
  (https://docs.kalshi.com/api-reference/orders/amend-order-v2) rather than
  trusting this entry's 2026-07-16 summary alone -- confirmed POST
  /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}/amend, request {ticker, side, price,
  count, client_order_id?, updated_client_order_id?, exchange_index?},
  response {order_id, client_order_id, remaining_count?, fill_count?,
  average_fill_price?, average_fee_paid?, ts_ms}. One clarification the
  original entry didn't capture: count is NOT "how many more to add" --
  it's the order's TOTAL desired fillable count (already-filled +
  desired-remaining-resting), the same semantics as create-order's count.
  For this bot's only use (reprice at an unchanged quantity), that means
  passing the same count used at original placement, unchanged -- Kalshi
  computes the filled/still-resting split internally.
  Shipped kalshi_client.amend_order() (V2 fixed-point body via the existing
  _to_v2_side_price mapping, deterministic updated_client_order_id via the
  same hash-based idempotency pattern as place_order, client_order_id
  included only when the caller has it) and order_executor._amend_live_order
  (mirrors _replace_live_order's gate-recheck + execution_log bookkeeping
  shape). Wired into _reprice_or_cancel_pending_orders's reprice-improve
  branch only (same order, new price) -- the taker-cross branch stays on
  cancel+replace exactly as before, since it changes time_in_force to
  immediate_or_cancel, a different order type amend cannot express, matching
  this entry's own original scoping.
  Execution_log design decision (surfaced via AskUserQuestion -- amend keeps
  the SAME exchange order_id, unlike cancel+replace's genuinely-new one, so
  this needed a real call): user chose the "new row, chained via
  replaces_order_id" option over "update the row in place", matching this
  entry's own "Log replaces_order_id chains the same way" plan. The old
  row gets a new status="amended" (deliberately distinct from "canceled" --
  the original order was never actually canceled, just repriced).
  Found and fixed a real live-money correctness gap this design choice
  would otherwise have introduced, caught by tracing every consumer of
  orders.status before finalizing the new status string (per
  [[feedback_trace_all_call_sites]]): execution_log.get_today_live_spend()
  (the MAX_DAILY_SPEND gate's data source) sums quantity*price across every
  row NOT IN ('failed','canceled','cancelled') -- 'amended' wasn't in that
  exclusion list, so an amended order's old row AND its new row would both
  count, double-counting the same resting position's capital on every
  reprice and inflating the live spend cap toward premature (fail-safe-
  direction, not fail-unsafe, but still a real bug) halts. Fixed by adding
  'amended' to that query's exclusion list. Checked every other
  orders.status consumer in execution_log.py (was_recently_ordered,
  was_traded_today, was_ordered_this_cycle: harmless either way, since the
  new row already signals "traded" regardless of the old row's status;
  get_open_live_positions's exact status='pending' match and
  order_executor._count_open_live_orders's exact status='pending' match:
  both naturally exclude 'amended' already, no change needed) -- only
  get_today_live_spend needed the fix.
  Adjacency note, NOT fixed (flagging per this project's convention rather
  than silently folding it in): execution_log.log_order_result() always
  overwrites response/error/error_code/error_type (not COALESCEd) even when
  the caller only means to update status -- _amend_live_order's mark-old-
  row-as-"amended" call inherits this same pre-existing behavior already
  present in _finalize_cancel's cancel-marking call (nulls out the old
  row's response JSON on every cancel too, not something this change
  introduced). Worth a real fix if execution_log.py is next open for
  other reasons.
  Not verified against DEMO_BASE (no live/demo order was actually placed) --
  ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE=False and TRADING_PAUSED throughout this session, same
  as every other live-order-path change to date; implemented and tested
  against the documented shape (live docs fetch above), matching how the
  original V2 create/cancel migration was done. Worth a real demo-order
  smoke test whenever live trading is actually being prepared to resume.
  20 new tests: kalshi_client.amend_order() body construction (V2 side/price
  mapping reused correctly, client_order_id included/omitted correctly,
  updated_client_order_id deterministic+idempotent, raw response passthrough
  -- tests/test_kalshi_client.py::TestAmendOrder, 7 tests);
  order_executor._resolve_amend_status's fill/no-fill/partial-fill/
  unparseable boundary cases (4 tests, mutation-tested by flipping the
  remaining_count<=0 comparison and confirming the boundary test fails for
  the right reason, then restoring); get_today_live_spend's 'amended'
  exclusion (2 tests, one directly proving the double-count bug by running
  the pre-fix query alongside the real one and asserting they diverge);
  updated 2 existing reprice-branch tests
  (test_rested_past_blanket_gate_but_not_taker_gate_reprices_not_crosses,
  test_price_moved_reprices_as_new_maker_order) from asserting cancel_order/
  place_order calls to asserting amend_order calls, since those tests were
  exercising an implementation detail (the mechanism) that genuinely
  changed by design, not just an outcome; replaced
  test_fill_race_during_cancel_skips_replacement (which tested the
  cancel+verify fill-race protection this change makes moot for the
  reprice-improve branch -- amend's atomicity closes that race window by
  construction) with test_amend_that_crosses_the_book_is_logged_as_filled,
  proving the analogous scenario (amend's own price change immediately
  crosses the book) is read correctly from the SAME atomic response instead
  of a separate verification call; added 2 new execution_log bookkeeping
  tests for the amend success/failure paths (old row -> "amended" only on
  success, left "pending" on failure so a future cycle can retry).
  602 tests pass across the full scoped regression sweep (every test file
  touching order_executor.py/kalshi_client.py/execution_log.py); ruff +
  ruff format + mypy clean.
  Independent second-opinion review (Agent, opus) caught one real issue
  before push: _amend_live_order's try/except wrapped BOTH the exchange
  amend_order() call AND the two subsequent execution_log bookkeeping
  writes in one block -- if the exchange call succeeded but a bookkeeping
  write then raised (e.g. a genuine SQLite "database is locked", plausible
  given web_app.py's dashboard and the WS thread can touch the same DB
  concurrently), the new row got marked "failed" even though the order had
  genuinely repriced live on the exchange, orphaning it (never picked up
  again by _poll_pending_orders' status='pending' filter). Fixed by
  splitting into two try/except blocks: only the amend_order() call itself
  can produce a "failed" classification and a False return; once a
  response is in hand, a bookkeeping failure is logged loudly (error, not
  warning) but the function still returns True, since the exchange-side
  reality is what matters for whether a future cycle should retry.
  New regression test (test_amend_exchange_success_survives_bookkeeping_
  failure) mocks execution_log.log_order_result to raise after a
  successful amend_order() call and asserts True is still returned --
  mutation-tested by reverting to the single-try-block shape and
  confirming the test fails with the exact predicted symptom (an
  unhandled RuntimeError instead of a clean True), then restoring. 126
  tests pass in the two most directly affected files after the fix; ruff/
  ruff format/mypy clean.

Problem (as originally scoped, still accurate for historical context):
  kalshi_client.py exposes only place/get/cancel (place_order :401,
  get_order :551, cancel_order :560) -- no amend. So
  _reprice_or_cancel_pending_orders (order_executor.py:779) does a

POST-RESOLUTION REGRESSION, FIXED 2026-07-19 (see the "is_liquid() (AND 4
  MORE SITES)..." entry for the full narrative): fit_market_implied_
  distribution()'s weighting line read plain market.get("volume") only,
  never the current API's volume_fp -- so on real live data every sibling
  bracket's weight computed as 0, and the fit almost certainly returned
  None on every real scan since it shipped below. The "verified...
  essentially exact" claim in the original resolution was true of the fit
  math (checked against synthetic fixtures using plain "volume"), but
  those fixtures never matched real API field-name shape, so the bug was
  invisible to the test suite that shipped with this feature. Fixed with
  the same `volume_fp or volume or 0` coalescing used everywhere else in
  this codebase, plus a new regression test built from live-API-shaped
  fixtures (volume_fp only, no "volume" key) confirming a real fit comes
  back. Lesson for future signals in this codebase: a synthetic-fixture
  test proving the MATH is correct is not the same as proving the
  function works against real API data shape -- verify field names
  against a real live payload (or at least against analyze_trade()'s own
  known-correct coalescing pattern) before calling a new market-data
  consumer "verified."

RESOLVED 2026-07-18: shipped as scoped in "What it would look like" below,
  with two design decisions surfaced to and confirmed by the user via
  AskUserQuestion first (call-site scope; liquidity-weight field), plus one
  reversal caught by re-deriving rather than restating a first-pass
  recommendation (the delta column -- see below).
  weather_markets.fit_market_implied_distribution(siblings) fits a Normal
  (mean, sigma) by weighted least squares: each liquid bracket's mid-price
  is the implied probability mass over its threshold (above/below/between),
  weighted by volume (chosen over open_interest because is_liquid() -- the
  same function gating the thin-book floor -- only ever checks volume,
  keeping one definition of liquidity instead of introducing a second).
  Reuses _forecast_probability's exact above/below/between mass formula
  conceptually, but reimplements it as a vectorized numpy expression rather
  than calling it per-point per-optimizer-iteration: profiling showed scipy.
  stats.norm.cdf's per-call overhead dominates (~200ms/fit via the
  non-vectorized version vs ~29ms vectorized, for a 6-bracket event) --
  documented inline so a future reader doesn't "simplify" it back to the
  slow, more-obviously-DRY version. weather_markets.
  compute_market_implied_distributions(markets) groups a scan's full market
  list by (city, date) via parse_city_date and fits each event once.
  Verified against a synthetic ladder built from a known Normal(70,5) (and
  separately an all-"between" ladder, since real weather markets are
  commonly all-between with no above/below siblings at all): fit recovered
  (70.0009, 5.0013) -- essentially exact.
  Wired into predictions via 3 new columns (implied_mean, implied_sigma,

CORRELATION CHECK RUN 2026-07-30 (per this entry's own ENABLEMENT TRIGGER --
  a one-off analysis against live data, not a wiring decision; picked up as
  the higher-value of the 2 signals a same-day backlog audit found had just
  cleared their 20-sample floor, over LIQUIDITY-AWARE SIZING's gated_edge
  check, because this one's needed columns -- implied_mean, forecast_temp_f,
  settled_temp_f -- are all logged directly, while gated_edge's check needs
  an unlogged `adjusted_edge` re-derived from other fields):
  n=22 settled predictions with non-NULL implied_mean/forecast_temp_f.
  Tested market_delta = implied_mean - forecast_temp_f against forecast_error
  = settled_temp_f - forecast_temp_f (does the market's tilt away from our
  forecast predict which direction the actual outcome misses our forecast
  by, the same directional-persistence hypothesis this entry's own text and
  run_trend's ENABLEMENT TRIGGER use). Result: Pearson r=0.405, sign
  agreement 14/22 (64%, vs 50% chance), two-sided p=0.061 (90% CI for r:
  [0.05, 0.67]) -- borderline, not conventionally significant at n=22, but
  directionally consistent with the market carrying real information rather
  than pure noise.
  One real wrinkle surfaced and checked before trusting the headline number:
  implied_sigma ranges from 1.06 to 47.30 across these 22 rows -- some fits
  are tight (a plausible real forecast sigma), others are numerically
  degenerate (a 47°F sigma is meaningless for a daily temp forecast, almost
  certainly an under-constrained thin-ladder fit). Re-ran the correlation
  filtered to sigma<=5 and sigma<=10 to confirm the degenerate-sigma rows
  weren't driving the result -- r stayed 0.37-0.41 across all three cuts, so
  the finding isn't an artifact of the noisiest fits.
  Real caveat for any FUTURE wiring decision (not relevant to whether the
  signal is real, only to how it could ever be used): market_delta's
  magnitude is ~3x forecast_error's (mean |market_delta|~=7.7°F vs mean
  |forecast_error|~=2.7-3.4°F depending on the sigma cut) -- even rows where
  the market points the right direction overshoot badly, so this could never
  be wired in as a raw additive correction; it would need heavy shrinkage.
  Conclusion: NOT wired into the blend (correctly stays log-only) --
  directionally promising but n=22/p=0.061 isn't conclusive. Re-run this
  same check once more settled rows accumulate; unlike run_trend/richer-ML
  (which are still far from their own floors), this signal is right at the
  edge of a real answer, so it's worth checking again soon rather than
  waiting for another full backlog audit to resurface it.

RESOLVED 2026-08-03 (one of the two deferred analysis passes -- "did

  has ZERO rows with filled_at or market_mid_at_fill populated -- no live
  order has ever actually filled (matches ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE being off) --
  so the "adverse selection around our own fills" half is structurally
  unanswerable right now, not just thin. Dropped from this pass per
  explicit AskUserQuestion confirmation rather than built against a 0-row
  table.

  (70,362 trade rows / 43 tickers; 13,820 candle rows / 274 tickers; full
  43/43 ticker overlap between the two tables) -- comfortably past a cold
  start.
  Shipped tracker.get_trade_flow_settlement_correlation(
  min_trades_per_market=10, min_candles_per_market=4, min_markets=15,
  min_early_trades=3) -- for each ticker with both trade_history and
  price_history rows, splits the trade series at its own time midpoint
  (half the trades before, half after, using each trade's parsed
  created_time epoch) and computes early signed flow ((yes-taker volume -
  no-taker volume) / total volume in the early half, in [-1, 1], requiring
  at least min_early_trades contributing trades so a single trade at a
  timestamp tie can't swing it to +-1.0) against late price drift (the last
  candle with a real, non-NULL price_close minus the earliest candle at/
  after that same midpoint that also has a real close -- both walks skip
  past NULL closes rather than trusting the first/last candle blindly, and
  candles are filtered to the earliest candle's own period_interval first
  so two OHLC resolutions can never silently interleave), then
  Pearson-correlates across markets using the same manual formula as
  get_recent_city_correlations (matching that function's convention, not
  because scipy is otherwise unavailable in this project -- it is, see
  weather_markets.py's scipy.stats/scipy.optimize imports). Markets below
  the trade/candle/early-trade floors are counted under
  markets_skipped_thin; markets that clear those floors but have no usable
  price at either end of the drift window are counted separately under
  markets_skipped_no_price, so a "thin" report never conflates two
  unrelated failure reasons.
  Real finding, run live against the actual DB: n=42 markets cleared the
  floor (43 considered, 1 skipped thin, 0 skipped for missing price),
  r=-0.035 -- indistinguishable from zero at this sample size. Early signed
  taker flow does NOT show a detectable relationship with each market's
  subsequent price drift in the current dataset. This is informational, not
  dispositive (n=42, single fixed early/late split point per market, no
  significance test attached) -- but it does NOT support building the live
  WS mechanism PUBLIC TRADE-FLOW SIGNAL describes on urgency grounds.
  get_trade_flow_settlement_correlation is a real, callable, tested query,
  not a one-off script -- re-run it as trade_history keeps accumulating
  rather than re-deriving the analysis from scratch next time.
  14 new tests (tests/test_tracker.py TestTradeFlowSettlementCorrelation):
  no-data, perfect 3-market correlation (3 collinear points -> r==1.0
  exactly, verifying the Pearson formula), a zero-variance guardrail
  (identical flows across markets -> r stays None, not a divide-by-zero),
  below-min-markets (n reported, r=None), thin-market skips (too few
  trades / too few candles / zero early volume / below the early-trade-
  count floor), the trade_history-without-price_history join-exclusion
  case, a mixed-period_interval-candles filter case, and 3 tests directly
  targeting the NULL-price-handling fix below.
  Independent Agent(opus, effort=high) review (before push, per standing
  workflow) reproduced the live result independently (byte-identical

  issues in the first draft -- all fixed, not just the HIGH one:

  like the count_fn miss noted in an earlier session's `9eec753` fix --
  added, matching get_price_history/get_trade_history's existing entries.
  (2) HIGH-severity-in-practice correctness bug -- the first draft used
  candles[-1]["price_close"] directly for the "last" price. 24% of all
  price_history rows have a NULL price_close (a period with no trades), and
  13 of the 43 real join tickers -- among the highest-volume markets in the
  set -- had a NULL close on their literal final candle, so they were
  silently mis-counted as "thin" and dropped (n was 29, not 42, before this
  fix; r was -0.042, not -0.035). Fixed by walking backward from the end
  until a real close is found, recovering all 13 markets.
  (3) MEDIUM -- the matching fix on the other end: the first draft took the
  first candle at/after the trade-series midpoint regardless of whether
  that specific candle had a real price, silently substituting an unrelated
  index-based fallback price when it didn't. Fixed to walk forward past any
  NULL-close candles at that boundary too.
  (4) MEDIUM -- the first draft's fallback (when no candle at/after the
  midpoint existed at all) computed drift entirely from candles before the
  midpoint, which could invert the lead-lag relationship the function
  exists to test (measuring a window that precedes the "early flow" window
  rather than following it). Removed the fallback entirely -- such a market
  is now skipped and counted under the new markets_skipped_no_price
  counter instead of silently contributing a wrong-direction data point.
  (5) MEDIUM -- docstring and a single skip counter undercounted/mislabeled
  the actual skip reasons once (2)-(4) existed -- split into
  markets_skipped_thin and markets_skipped_no_price and rewrote the
  docstring to describe all three real skip paths.
  (6) LOW -- the created_time parse only caught ValueError; broadened to
  also catch AttributeError/TypeError so a future non-string created_time
  (e.g. if Kalshi ever changed format) fails soft instead of crashing the
  whole report.
  (7) LOW -- added an explicit min_early_trades=3 floor (a market could
  previously reach the volume-only floor via a single early trade at a
  timestamp tie); LOW -- added a period_interval filter so two OHLC
  resolutions for one ticker could never silently interleave (not observed
  live as of this writing, but not structurally prevented either); LOW --
  gave the function an explicit `-> dict[str, int | float | None]` return
  type instead of a bare `dict`; LOW -- reworded a docstring line that
  implied scipy was unavailable in this project (it isn't -- the manual
  Pearson formula matches get_recent_city_correlations' own convention,
  nothing else) and another that overstated "settlement" when the measured
  endpoint is the last logged candle, not necessarily literal settlement.
  Two of the new tests initially had real gaps caught only by re-verifying
  the review's own mutation-testing claims by hand, not just trusting the
  review's summary: the first version of a NULL-close-boundary mutation
  test silently passed because its candle timestamps were small toy
  integers nowhere near the trade series' real 2026 epoch values, so the
  time-aligned code path never actually executed; and the first version of
  the period_interval-filter test used only 2 markets, which is
  mathematically always exactly r=+-1 regardless of the underlying values
  (any 2 distinct points are collinear), so it could not have caught the
  filter being removed entirely -- both rebuilt (real epoch-aligned
  timestamps; a 3-market design where a wrong value measurably moves r off
  1.0) and re-confirmed against the actual mutation.
  350 tests pass across tests/test_tracker.py (was 344); ruff + ruff format
  + mypy clean on tracker.py, tests/test_tracker.py, and
  tests/test_dead_code_scan.py (one pre-existing, unrelated ruff-format nit
  elsewhere in test_tracker.py left untouched -- confirmed via diff scope,
  not introduced by this change).
  Zero live-trading-behavior change: read-only query function, no existing
  code calls it (by design -- see the dead-code-scanner allowlist entry),
  TRADING_PAUSED/ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE untouched, no order was placed or
  closed.
  Still open: the "adverse selection around our own fills" half (execution_
  log.orders has zero fills to analyze -- revisit once ENABLE_MICRO_LIVE is
  ever flipped and real live fills start accumulating).

When to revisit (adverse-selection half only -- flow-vs-settlement analysis
  above is closed):
  - Once execution_log.orders has real filled_at/market_mid_at_fill rows to
    join against -- currently 0 of 198.

[PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-07-23 -- tracker.get_regional_recent_bias() shipped
  log-only; wiring into an actual forecast lean still gated on more data]
  CROSS-CITY RECENT-ERROR POOLING -- SYNOPTIC-REGIME BIAS SHARE
Priority: Low-Medium -- the spatial correlation structure is already
  learned and stored; it's only ever used to *penalize risk*, never to
  *improve the forecast*.

Problem (as originally scoped):
  Bias correction is strictly per-city and slow: _get_combined_station_bias
  (weather_markets.py:303-337) blends a static table with
  tracker.get_dynamic_station_bias (min 10 samples, weeks of
  accumulation, 4h cache). Nothing used the last 24-48h of realized
  errors in *other* cities to nudge today's forecast -- even though
  forecast errors are spatially correlated under a shared synoptic
  regime, and the bot already quantifies exactly those correlations
  (_CITY_PAIR_CORR paper.py:313-332; tracker.get_recent_city_correlations
  refreshed into monte_carlo.simulate_portfolio) -- but solely for
  portfolio VaR.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-23 before picking this up: the "3-14 per-city" count
  cited above was stale (2026-07-12 audit) -- live counts were actually
  1-28 per city, and the settlement-latency question was resolved
  affirmatively (median lag ~1 day across 237 recent settlements, so
  yesterday's correlated-city errors ARE typically available by today's
  scan).

What shipped:
  tracker.get_regional_recent_bias(city, var, hours=48, as_of=None) --
  correlation-weighted mean of correlated cities' settled errors, using
  the exact _CORRELATED_CITY_GROUPS/_CITY_PAIR_CORR tables named above,
  with a ROW_NUMBER dedup to each ticker's latest logged prediction and
  outcomes_valid's disputed-row exclusion. `as_of` (SQLite datetime()
  string) lets a caller reconstruct a specific historical point in time
  without lookahead -- used to retrospectively validate against real
  settled data: Pearson r ~= 0.35 between pooled regional bias and same-
  city same-day error, but thin per-estimate coverage (85/229 candidate
  rows had any signal, averaging 1.67 correlated-city samples each). 9
  new tests, opus review clean (one defense-in-depth hardening applied:
  bound predicted_at by as_of too). Pushed `fd94bf7`.

Still open:
  - NOT wired into any live forecast lean or blend weight -- the r~0.35
    result is real but too sparse to trust yet, correctly shipped as a
    log-only/ad-hoc utility per this entry's own sequencing.

When to revisit:
  - Re-run the retrospective validation once more settled data has
    accumulated; if correlation holds up with denser per-estimate
    coverage, size a bounded lean capped well below
    _get_combined_station_bias's magnitude.
